documents.text:
### 6.8 Garments with shoulder pads

Shoulder pads are foam or wadding sewn or fused into the shoulder. They compress,
they take up moisture, and they do not give it back at the same rate as the
shell.

- Use programme 09. Reduce inflation (F1 = 1.5 kPa) so the pad is not pushed
  out of its position while wet.
- Increase cool time to 28 s. A pad that is released warm and damp will hold
  whatever shape it was in.
- Feel the pad through the shell at unload. If it is warm and damp, the cycle
  was too short; add 10 s to F5 rather than raising the temperature.
- **GARMENT RISK.** Foam pads in garments more than about fifteen years old
  become brittle and can crumble under steam. If a pad feels crunchy through the
  shell, do not run the garment on the form. Finish it by hand and note it on
  the ticket.
- A pad that has shifted inside its pocket will not be corrected by the form.
  It must be re-seated by the alterations hand before finishing.

### 6.9 Lined jackets

A lining is cut with ease — deliberate slack — at the back and at the hem, and
it is usually a different fibre from the shell. Acetate and viscose linings
behave differently from a wool shell under steam.

- Dress the jacket so the lining hangs freely inside. Do not pull the lining
  down with the shell into the hem clamps. Clamp the shell only.
- Keep F7 at or below 40%. A hard hem pull is what breaks the lining's ease
  pleat at the centre back, and once broken it will show as a drag line for the
  life of the garment.
- Keep F4 at or below 80 °C. Acetate linings glaze above about 90 °C at the
  fabric face and the glaze is permanent.
- Check the lining at unload by opening the front. A lining that is still damp
  when the shell is dry means the airflow is being blocked — check the form
  cover and the inlet filter.
- If a lining bubbles or ripples where it is fused to a fusible interlining, the
  bond has failed. Stop. Steam will make it worse. Refer the garment to
  alterations.

## 7. Spotmaster SB-40 spotting board

### 7.1 Description

The Spotmaster SB-40 is a vacuum spotting board. It is the position at which a
stain is identified, classified and removed before the garment goes to cleaning
or to finishing. Everything in this section assumes the spotter has already
identified the fibre and checked for colour-fastness (see 7.3 and 7.7).

The board comprises:

- a **main board**, 1,400 × 800 mm, foam-padded and covered with a replaceable
  nylon cover (TV-SB-1200 cover, TV-SB-1210 padding);
- a **vacuum table**, 620 × 420 mm of perforated stainless steel let into the
  board, connected to the integral 1.1 kW side-channel blower through a lint
  screen and a filter element;
- a removable **arm board**, 900 × 380 mm, for sleeves and trouser legs;
- a **steam gun**, regulated to 350 kPa, 1.6 mm nozzle;
- an **air gun**, 620 kPa, 2.0 mm nozzle;
- **two chemical guns**, each drawing from a 1.0 L bottle and delivering a fine
  spray at 200 kPa;
- a **rinse pot** and cold water tap;
- a **task lamp**, 18 W LED at 5,000 K giving 1,200 lux at board centre;
- a **local exhaust hood** at the rear, 850 m³/h.

**The vacuum table** is the working part of the board. Vacuum pulls the loosened
stain and the flushing medium down through the fabric and out of the garment
rather than letting it spread sideways. Spotting without vacuum drives the stain
into the fabric and produces a ring. The vacuum is operated by a foot pedal and
must be running during every flush, every steam application and every dry.

**The steam gun** flushes with saturated steam. Steam does three things: it
carries chemistry into the fabric, it flushes the loosened stain out, and it
adds heat which speeds most reactions. Hold the gun 100 to 150 mm from the
fabric, at a shallow angle, and move it. A gun held still and close will wet the
fabric through and will scald the operator's hand.

**The air gun** dries the treated area and feathers the edge of a wet patch so
that no ring is left. Use it with the vacuum on, moving outward from the centre.

**The two chemical guns** are normally charged as gun 1 = wet side, gun 2 = dry
side. Each gun bottle must be labelled (see 7.10). Never swap the contents of a
gun without flushing it (see 8.8).

### 7.2 Wet side and dry side

Spotting chemistry divides into two families.

**Wet side** agents are water-based. They remove stains that are water-soluble
or that respond to water-borne acids, alkalis, enzymes or oxidisers: sugar,
protein, tannin, dye, salt, most food. Wet-side work must be finished with a
neutral rinse and a full dry, or the residual chemistry will keep working in the
garment.

**Dry side** agents are solvent-based. They remove stains that are oil-soluble:
grease, oil, wax, tar, lipstick, some inks, some paints. Dry-side work is done
before the garment goes into the dry cleaning machine, not after.

The rule is: **work the dry side first, then the wet side.** If a stain has both
an oily and a water-soluble component — lipstick, foundation, chocolate, gravy —
remove the oil first with a dry-side agent, then take the residual colour with
wet-side chemistry. Doing it in the other order sets the oil.

### 7.3 Test before you treat

Every agent is tested on a hidden part of the garment before it goes on the
stain. The hidden part is an inside seam allowance, the inside of a hem, a
pocket bag, or the underside of a collar.

1. Apply one drop of the agent to the hidden area.
2. Blot with a white cloth. If colour transfers to the white cloth, the garment
   is not fast to that agent. Stop.
3. Steam-flush the test area and dry it with the air gun. Check for a ring, a
   colour change, a texture change or a loss of finish.
4. If in any doubt, do not proceed. Go to 7.9.

**GARMENT RISK.** A colour-fastness test takes 40 seconds. A dye that has been
stripped off a lapel cannot be put back.

and a dry between them.

### 7.5 Standard procedure

1. Identify the fibre from the care label. If there is no label, see 7.8 and
   7.9.
2. Identify the stain. If you cannot identify it, treat it as unknown: neutral
   lubricant, dry side first, then wet side, gently.
3. Test the agent (7.3).
4. Lay the stain face down on the vacuum table where possible so the stain is
   pushed out the way it came in.
5. Start the vacuum.
6. Apply the agent sparingly. More agent is not faster.
7. Apply the permitted mechanical action (7.6) for the fibre, not for the stain.
8. Steam-flush from the outside of the stain inward.
9. Repeat from step 6 up to three times. If three applications of the correct
   agent have not moved the stain, change the approach or stop.
10. Neutralise: acid work is followed by a dilute alkaline rinse, alkaline work
    by a dilute acid rinse (TVC-11), then a clear water flush.
11. Dry with the air gun, feathering outward, vacuum running.
12. Record the treatment if the garment is at risk (7.9, Appendix D).

**Mechanical action** on this board means: the bone or spatula (light scraping
and tamping), the brush (tamping only, never scrubbing), and the fingers. There
is no fourth option. Rubbing a stain between the fingers is not a technique; it
is how chafing happens.

### 7.7 Colour-fastness and pre-checks

Before any treatment: check the care label; check for a fugitive dye by the drop
test at 7.3; check for existing damage, thin patches and open seams; check
trims, buttons and beads for solvent sensitivity; check for a previous
unsuccessful home treatment, which is the single most common reason a stain will
not respond.

Record anything found on the ticket before you start. A garment that arrives
with a hole does not become the plant's hole because nobody wrote it down.

### 7.8 Fibre-by-fibre cautions

**Wool.** Alkali-sensitive. Protein formula and ammonia will damage the fibre if
left in contact. Neutralise every alkaline treatment. Never use hot water and
mechanical action together — that is felting, and it is irreversible. Maximum
tamping: light. Chlorine bleach must never be used on wool in any circumstances.

**Silk.** The most fragile common fibre on the board. Alkali-sensitive like
wool, and additionally prone to water marking, dye bleeding and loss of lustre.
Use minimum moisture, minimum agent, minimum mechanical action, and feather
every edge. Steam at a distance. Never use oxygen bleach on coloured silk.

**Acetate.** Dissolved by acetone and by amyl acetate. TVC-05 will make a hole
in an acetate lining in seconds, not minutes. Heat-sensitive: glazes above about
90 °C. Water-marks readily. Test everything.

**Triacetate.** More heat- and solvent-resistant than acetate but still
dissolved by amyl acetate. Treat as acetate for chemical purposes.

**Rayon / viscose.** Loses about half its strength when wet. Do not tamp wet
viscose. Prone to water marking, to shrinkage, and to permanent distortion if
tensioned wet. Use minimum moisture and dry it flat and quickly.

**Cotton.** Tolerant of most chemistry and of mechanical action. Weakened by
acids: rust remover left in cotton will produce a hole at the next wash.
Neutralise after every acid treatment. Prone to ring formation, so feather
carefully.

**Linen.** As cotton chemically, but the fibre is stiff and brittle when dry.
Over-tamping breaks the fibre and produces a permanent light patch that looks
like abrasion because it is abrasion.

**Polyester.** Chemically the most tolerant fibre. Its problem is oil: polyester
is oleophilic and holds grease stains hard. Expect several dry-side passes.
Heat-set creases in polyester will not steam out.

**Nylon.** Attacked by strong acids, so rust remover is a real risk. Scavenges
loose dye out of solution readily, which is why a nylon garment picks up dye
transfer in a mixed load. Yellows with heat and with age.

**Elastane / spandex.** Present in small percentages in a great many modern
garments. Destroyed by chlorine bleach. Degraded by heat above about 110 °C and
by repeated high-temperature finishing. If a garment has lost its stretch, the
elastane has already gone and no treatment will restore it.

**Leather and suede trim.** Do not spot leather trim on this board. Water marks
it, solvent strips its finish, and steam shrinks and hardens it. Mask the trim,
work around it, or send the garment to a leather specialist.

**Bonded and laminated fabrics.** Two layers joined by adhesive. Steam, solvent
and heat all attack the adhesive. Bubbling or lifting means the bond has failed
and it cannot be repaired. Test at a hidden edge. If the fabric shows any sign
of separation, stop.

**Beaded, sequinned and printed garments.** Many sequins and most heat-transfer
prints are dissolved or lifted by dry-side solvent and by amyl acetate. Test on
a single hidden sequin. If it clouds, softens or loses colour, stop.

### 7.9 When not to spot

Some garments must go back to the customer untouched. The decision to refuse
treatment is a professional judgement and it protects both the garment and the
business. Refuse treatment where:

- **there is no care label and the fibre cannot be identified with confidence.**
  Without a fibre, no agent can be chosen safely;
- **the dye is not fast** to water, to the required agent, or to solvent, on the
  drop test at 7.3;
- **the fabric is bonded or laminated** and shows any sign of separation;
- **the garment is already damaged** — thin, split, brittle, sun-degraded, or
  showing broken fibres at the stain itself. Chemistry will finish what the
  damage started;
- **the stain has been treated at home** with an unknown product, particularly a
  chlorine bleach or a proprietary stain stick. The residue may react with the
  board chemistry;
- **the stain is dye damage, not a stain** — a colour change with no deposit on
  the surface. There is nothing to remove;
- **the garment is a leather, suede, fur or fur-trimmed article**;
- **the garment carries an owner's instruction not to treat it**;
- **the value or sentiment attached to the garment is out of proportion to the
  chance of success** — a wedding dress, a christening gown, an heirloom, a
  costume. These go to a specialist or go back untreated.

**How the decision is recorded.** Where treatment is refused or limited, the
spotter completes the Spotting Record at Appendix D before the garment leaves
the board. The record captures the ticket number, the garment, the stain, the
fibre (or "unidentified"), the reason for refusal by reference to the list
above, the tests performed, the spotter's name and the date. A copy of the
relevant lines is written onto the customer's docket, and the counter staff are
told so that the customer is advised at collection and not after it.

Where treatment proceeds on an at-risk garment, the same record is completed
with the customer's acknowledgement noted, and the record is retained for not
less than 12 months.

### 7.10 Chemical safety, storage, decanting and labelling

**Storage.** Keep the chemistry set in a dedicated, ventilated, lockable cabinet
in the finishing room, not under the board and not on the board. Acids and
alkalis on separate shelves, oxidiser (TVC-06) on its own shelf, flammables
(TVC-05, TVC-09) in a flammable liquids cabinet. Maximum quantity on the board
at any time: one 1.0 L gun bottle per gun plus the working bottles in use.

**Decanting.** Decant only into a labelled container of the same material as the
original. Decant under the exhaust hood with the hood running, with goggles and
gloves on, and over the drip tray. Never decant into a drink bottle, a food
container or an unlabelled bottle. Never top up a part-used bottle from a
different batch without confirming it is the same product.

**Labelling.** Every container on the board, including the two gun bottles,
carries a label showing the product name, the TVC part number, the hazard
pictograms, the signal word, and the date it was filled. A container without a
label is emptied to waste, not used. Do not rely on colour coding alone.

**Safety Data Sheets.** The occupier must hold a current SDS for every product
on the board. An SDS more than five years old must be replaced by the supplier's
current version. The SDS register at Appendix C lists each product, its supplier,
the SDS issue date and its review date. The register is checked quarterly. SDSs
must be readily accessible to any worker at the board — a folder within reach,
not a file on a computer that only the office can open.

**Spills.** Small spills on the board: flush with water and vacuum through.
Spills on the floor: absorb with the spill kit, bag the absorbent, and dispose
of it as prescribed industrial waste through the waste contractor. Do not wash
solvent or concentrated chemistry to the trade waste drain.

**Waste.** Board waste water goes to trade waste under the site's trade waste
agreement. Concentrated residues, empty solvent containers and contaminated
absorbent go out as prescribed industrial waste. Rags used with dry-side agents
are stored in a lidded metal bin, not in an open bin and not in a plastic bag.

- **Working correctly:** intermittent discharge, inlet temperature at saturation
  for the line pressure (about 160 °C at 550 kPa), outlet noticeably cooler.
- **Failed open (blowing through):** continuous flow, inlet and outlet at the
  same temperature, an audible continuous hiss. Wastes steam and pressurises the
  return. Replace.
- **Failed closed (blocked):** trap and inlet cold or barely warm, machine
  performance falls off, water carries over into the cabinet or the gun.
  Replace.

Record the result against the trap identifier in the weekly log. A trap that has
failed twice in twelve months indicates a dirt or waterhammer problem upstream;
fit or clean the strainer before fitting another trap.

### 8.7 Form cover replacement, FF-300

Two people. Isolate as 8.2 and allow the machine to cool. Release the hem clamp
rail and lower it fully. Release the shoulder plate clamps and lift the yoke
clear. Unhook the cover's draw cord at the base, roll the old cover up from the
hem and off over the shoulder frame. Inspect the frame for broken wires and
sharp edges; dress any burrs. Fit the new cover from the shoulder down, seat it
squarely on the shoulder plates, draw and tie the base cord, and check that no
fold is trapped under a plate. Re-assemble, restore services and run three
cycles on programme 06 with no garment to bed the cover in. Record the date and
the part number.

### 8.8 Chemical gun flushing

Weekly, and always before a gun's contents are changed.

1. Hood running, goggles and gloves on, waste pot on the board.
2. Remove the bottle. Cap it and set it aside.
3. Fit a bottle of clean water. Discharge the gun into the waste pot until the
   spray runs clear, then for a further 10 s.
4. Remove the pickup tube and check its filter, TV-SB-3120. Rinse or replace.
5. Discharge air only through the gun for 5 s to clear the passage.
6. Refit the correct bottle, check the label, and test the spray pattern on a
   waste cloth. The pattern must be an even cone; a split or one-sided pattern
   means the nozzle is partly blocked.
7. Dispose of the waste pot contents as prescribed industrial waste.

**CAUTION.** A gun that has held an acid formula must be flushed with water and
then with dilute alkaline rinse before it is charged with an alkaline formula,
and vice versa. Residue in the gun body is enough to gas off in the bottle.

### 9.2 Troubleshooting the eight most common faults

**SA-01 / FF-01 steam pressure low.** Almost always a plant problem, not a
machine problem. Check the boiler gauge first. If the boiler is at pressure and
the machine is not, the fault is between them: a closed or partly closed
isolation valve, a blocked strainer, or a failed-closed trap flooding the drop
leg. If SA-01 and FF-01 appear together whenever both machines cycle at once,
the steam supply is undersized or the header is too small; see the note at 3.7.
A machine that raises SA-01 only on the first cycle of the morning is telling
you the header has not been warmed through; warm the line before the first
garment rather than adjusting P12.

**SA-04 / FF-05 airflow and blower faults.** In nine cases out of ten the inlet
filter is blocked with lint. Wash it, dry it, refit it and restart. If the fault
returns with a clean filter, listen for the fan: if it runs but the machine
still faults, the airflow switch or its sensing tube has failed; if it does not
run, check for a tripped overload. After any electrical work, reversed phase
rotation gives a fan that runs, sounds normal and moves almost no air — this
presents as poor finishing before it presents as a fault code.

**SA-09 / FF-08 over-temperature.** The cut-out has tripped because the heaters
were on without enough air over them. Find out why before resetting. Blocked
filter, failed fan, closed damper, or a welded heater contactor. A contactor
that has welded closed will trip the cut-out again immediately after reset and
must be replaced. Do not defeat or bypass the cut-out under any circumstances.
Two over-temperature trips in a week is a machine that should be taken out of
service until a technician has attended.

**SA-10 / FF-09 cycle timeout.** The controller has not seen a phase complete.
Note which phase the display was showing. Timeout during steam usually means low
steam pressure that has not yet reached the SA-01 threshold. Timeout during hot
air usually means the plenum never reached setpoint, which is a heater or sensor
problem. Timeout during tension or inflation is mechanical: on the SA-90 a
dirty rail or a fouled garment, on the FF-300 a cover that will not hold.

**FF-03 form inflation failure.** Check in this order: the base draw cord is
tied and seated; the cover has no tear, particularly at the shoulder plate
corners where it wears first; the sleeve bladder connections are made; the
blower runs. A cover that has stretched with age will inflate slowly and fail
intermittently — this is the point at which it should be replaced rather than
patched. If the cover is sound and the blower runs, check that the relief valve
has not stuck open, which will vent the plenum and produce the same symptom.

**SB-01 vacuum low.** Clear the lint screen first; it takes 30 seconds and it is
the cause most of the time. Then wash the filter element. A filter element that
has been washed more than about ten times will no longer come back and should be
replaced. If both are clean and depression is still below 11 kPa, look for a
leak: the arm board seal, an open access panel, or a split in the duct to the
blower. A vacuum that is weak only at one end of the table is a partial blockage
under the perforated plate, not a blower fault.

**SB-03 steam gun no flow.** Purge the gun into the waste pot. If it spits water
and then runs, the drop leg was flooded and the trap should be tested. If
nothing comes out at all, the nozzle is blocked with scale; remove and clean it
with the pin, and if scale is recurring, the boiler water treatment is the real
problem. If the gun runs but weakly and the line is hot, the regulator has
failed and is a technician item. Never enlarge a blocked nozzle with a drill;
the orifice size sets the gun's flushing behaviour.

**SB-05 / SB-06 chemical gun blocked.** Usually crystallised product in the
nozzle or the pickup filter, from a gun left charged over a weekend. Flush per
8.8. If the gun blocks again within the week, the bottle contents have been
mixed or contaminated: empty it, flush the gun fully, and refill from a sealed
supply container. Never clear a chemical gun nozzle by blowing back through it
with your mouth or by pressing it against a rag and firing.

## 11. Warranty and service

### 11.1 Terms

Trevil warrants each machine against defect in materials and workmanship for
**24 months on parts and 12 months on labour**, from the date of commissioning
recorded in Appendix A. Warranty is transferable with the machine on written
notice. A warranty claim must quote the machine serial number and the fault code
displayed, and must be supported by the maintenance log for the preceding
12 months.

### 11.2 Exclusions

Warranty does not cover: consumable and wear parts, being form covers, board
covers and padding, all bladders, all filters and lint screens, all nozzles,
seals, gaskets, clamp pads, hoses and lamps; damage caused by steam quality,
including scale, carryover and wet steam; damage caused by air quality,
including water and oil carried through the compressed air supply; corrosion
from spotting chemistry; damage caused by supply voltage outside ±6% of nominal,
by phase loss or by reversed rotation; damage from freezing; garments; and any
consequential loss.

### 11.3 What voids the warranty

- operating a machine with a guard, interlock or safety device removed,
  bypassed or defeated, including setting P14 to 0 on the SA-90;
- resetting an over-temperature cut-out repeatedly without correcting the cause;
- using the SB-40 with chemistry other than that at 7.4, or with any product for
  which no SDS is held;
- work inside a control enclosure by a person who is not a licensed electrician
  or a Trevil-authorised technician;
- modification of the steam, air, drain or exhaust connections away from the
  data at Section 3, including joining the SB-40 hood into a common duct;
- failure to carry out the scheduled maintenance at Section 8, evidenced by the
  absence of the log sheets;
- relocation of a machine without re-commissioning.

### 11.4 Service

Scheduled service is by a Trevil-authorised technician at not more than
12-month intervals, and includes the quarterly and annual tasks at 8.3, 8.4 and
8.5. A service report must be issued and filed with this manual. Faults marked Y
in the table at 9.1 require an authorised technician; an operator may not clear
them.

In this Lease, unless the contrary intention appears:

**Act** means the Retail Leases Act 2003 (Vic).

**Base rent** means the amount in Item 14 as reviewed under clause 4.

**Building** means the building and land in Item 4, including the common areas, and any part of it.

**Business day** means a day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Bendigo.

**Common areas** means those parts of the Building not let or intended to be let to a tenant, including the rear yard, the Bath Lane loading area, the bin enclosure, the shared switchboard cupboard and the shared water meter cupboard.

**Contaminant** means any substance which, when present in or on land, groundwater, air or a building, gives rise to or is capable of giving rise to harm to human health or the environment, and includes perchloroethylene, hydrocarbon solvent, solvent residues, still bottoms, spent filter cartridges, waste water and separator water.

**Environment Protection Law** means the Environment Protection Act 2017 (Vic), the Environment Protection Regulations 2021 (Vic), any environment reference standard, any compliance code or guideline published by the Environment Protection Authority Victoria, and any successor legislation.

**GST** has the meaning given in the A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999 (Cth).

**Landlord's fixtures** means the items listed in Annexure C and any item the Landlord installs in the Premises during the Term at the Landlord's cost.

**Outgoings** has the meaning given in section 3 of the Act and, for this Lease, is limited to the items listed in clause 5.2.

**Premises** means the premises in Item 5.

**Rent** means base rent and every other amount payable by the Tenant under this Lease.

**Tenant's plant** means the dry cleaning machines, boiler, compressor, presses, finishing equipment, conveyor, still, solvent store, tanks, pumps, ducting and associated services installed in the Premises by the Tenant or by a previous occupier and acquired by the Tenant, and includes the items listed in Annexure D.

**Term** means the term in Item 11 and, where the option in clause 3.3 is validly exercised, includes the further term.

### 1.2 Interpretation

(a) A reference to legislation includes that legislation as amended or replaced.

(b) The singular includes the plural and the reverse.

(c) A reference to a party includes that party's successors and permitted assigns.

(d) Where two or more persons are named as Tenant, they are bound jointly and severally.

(e) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

(f) A reference to a clause, Item or Annexure is a reference to a clause of this Lease, an Item of the Reference Schedule or an Annexure to this Lease.

(g) Money is Australian currency and measurements are metric.

(h) Where a thing is to be done on a day that is not a business day, it must be done on the next business day.

### 1.3 The Act prevails

If any provision of this Lease is inconsistent with the Act, the Act prevails and the provision is read down to the extent of the inconsistency. If a provision cannot be read down it is severed and the rest of this Lease continues in force.

## 2. Grant

### 2.1 Grant of lease

The Landlord leases the Premises to the Tenant for the Term at the Rent and on the terms of this Lease.

### 2.2 Exclusive possession

The Tenant has exclusive possession of the Premises, subject to the Landlord's rights of entry under clause 9.5.

### 2.3 Rights granted

The Tenant has, in common with the Landlord and others authorised by the Landlord:

(a) the right to use the common areas for pedestrian and vehicular access;

(b) the right to use the rear loading area off Bath Lane between 6:00 am and 7:00 pm on any day for deliveries, for the delivery and collection of solvent, and for the collection of waste; and

(c) the right to run and maintain the services which serve the Premises through the Building, including the boiler flue, the solvent vent stack and the trade waste line.

### 2.4 Exceptions

The Tenant has no right to the roof, the external walls, the airspace above the Building or any part of the Building other than the Premises, except as clause 2.3 and clause 6.6 allow.

## 3. Term and option to renew

### 3.1 Term

The Term commences on the date in Item 9 and, unless ended earlier under this Lease, ends on the date in Item 10.

### 3.2 Landlord's notice of the option

The Landlord must, in accordance with section 28 of the Act, notify the Tenant in writing of the date after which the option in clause 3.3 is no longer exercisable. That notice must be given at least 6 months and not more than 12 months before the last day of the option exercise period in Item 13. If the Landlord gives that notice late, the last day for exercise is extended in accordance with section 28(2) of the Act.

### 3.3 Option

If the Tenant gives the Landlord written notice within the option exercise period in Item 13, the Landlord must grant the Tenant a lease of the Premises for the further term in Item 12 on the same terms as this Lease except that:

(a) there is no further option to renew;

(b) the base rent for the first year of the further term is the base rent payable in the final year of the Term, reviewed to the Consumer Price Index under clause 4.2 on 1 March 2029; and

(c) the security in clause 13 is adjusted to three months' base rent plus GST as at the commencement of the further term.

### 3.4 Preconditions to option

The Tenant may exercise the option only if, at the date of the notice and at the date the further term begins:

(a) the Tenant has remedied any breach of this Lease of which the Landlord has given written notice; and

(b) the Tenant has not, on three or more occasions in the preceding 24 months, been given written notice of a failure to pay Rent within 14 days of its due date and failed to remedy that failure within a further 14 days.

The Landlord may waive either precondition. A breach that has been remedied does not prevent exercise of the option.

### 3.5 Holding over

If the Tenant remains in possession after the Terminating date with the Landlord's consent and without a further lease being granted, the Tenant holds over as a monthly tenant on the terms of this Lease so far as they can apply to a monthly tenancy, at the base rent payable immediately before the Terminating date, terminable by either party on one month's written notice expiring on any day.

## 4. Rent and rent review

### 4.1 Payment of base rent

The Tenant must pay the base rent to the Landlord by equal monthly instalments of $4,866.67 plus GST in advance on the first day of each month, without deduction, set-off or demand, by electronic funds transfer to the account nominated by the Landlord from time to time. The first instalment was payable on 1 March 2024. Where a period is less than a full month, the instalment is apportioned on a daily basis.

### 4.2 CPI review

On each date in Item 15 the base rent is adjusted to the amount calculated as:

R × (A ÷ B)

where:

R is the base rent payable immediately before the review date;

A is the Consumer Price Index (All Groups, Melbourne) published by the Australian Bureau of Statistics for the last quarter for which the index was published before the review date; and

B is the same index for the quarter 12 months before the quarter used for A.

### 4.3 Review machinery

(a) The Landlord must give the Tenant written notice of the reviewed base rent, setting out the index numbers used and the calculation.

(b) Until that notice is given, the Tenant continues to pay the base rent applying before the review date. Within 14 days after the notice, the Tenant must pay the shortfall for the period since the review date.

(c) If the index is discontinued or its base is changed, the index is replaced or converted in accordance with section 36 of the Act and, failing agreement, as determined by a specialist retail valuer appointed under Part 5 of the Act.

(d) A review takes effect on the review date whether or not the notice under paragraph (a) is given on time.

### 4.4 No ratchet

If the calculation in clause 4.2 produces an amount less than the base rent payable before the review date, the base rent is reduced to that lesser amount. Any provision of this Lease which would prevent the base rent decreasing on review is void under section 35(2) of the Act.

### 4.5 Interest on late payment

If the Tenant does not pay any Rent within 14 days after its due date, the Tenant must pay interest on the unpaid amount from the due date until payment at the rate fixed from time to time under section 2 of the Penalty Interest Rates Act 1983 (Vic). The Landlord's right to interest does not affect any other right the Landlord has.

## 5. Outgoings

### 5.1 Tenant to pay

The Tenant must pay to the Landlord the Tenant's proportion in Item 8 of the outgoings in clause 5.2, in monthly instalments in advance on the days the base rent is payable, based on the estimate given under clause 5.3 and adjusted under clause 5.5.

### 5.2 Recoverable outgoings

The only outgoings recoverable under this Lease are:

(a) council rates and charges;

(b) water rates and charges and the fixed component of the trade waste agreement for the Building, other than volumetric and load-based trade waste charges which the Tenant pays direct under clause 5.7;

(c) the fire services property levy;

(d) insurance premiums for the Building under clause 9.1 and the reasonable cost of a valuation for insurance purposes, not more often than once every three years;

(e) the cost of cleaning, lighting, repairing and maintaining the common areas, including the bin enclosure and the Bath Lane loading area;

(f) the cost of the annual test and inspection of the fire services and essential safety measures for the Building;

(g) the cost of pest control for the common areas;

(h) waste collection for the common areas; and

(i) the management fee charged by the Landlord's managing agent, not exceeding 4% of the gross rental income of the Building.

### 5.3 Estimate

The Landlord must give the Tenant a written estimate of the outgoings for each accounting period, itemised by the categories in clause 5.2, at least one month before the start of that accounting period and, for the first accounting period, before the Commencing date. If the Landlord does not give the estimate, the Tenant is not required to pay the outgoings until the estimate is given, in accordance with section 46(3) of the Act.

### 5.4 Statement

Within three months after the end of each accounting period the Landlord must give the Tenant a written statement of the outgoings actually incurred, itemised by the categories in clause 5.2, prepared and reported on in accordance with sections 46 and 47 of the Act. The statement must be accompanied by an auditor's report unless the Act does not require one.

### 5.5 Reconciliation

If the statement shows that the Tenant has paid more than the Tenant's proportion of the outgoings actually incurred, the Landlord must refund the excess within 28 days or, at the Tenant's election, credit it against the next instalments of Rent. If the statement shows the Tenant has paid less, the Tenant must pay the difference within 28 days after receiving the statement, but only to the extent permitted by section 47 of the Act.

### 5.6 Prohibited amounts

The Tenant is not liable for and must not be charged:

(a) land tax, or any amount on account of land tax, which is not recoverable by reason of section 50 of the Act;

(b) any capital cost of the Building or any contribution to a sinking fund;

(c) any cost of the Landlord's own management other than the fee in clause 5.2(i); or

(d) any outgoing which is not listed in clause 5.2 or which is not stated in the disclosure statement.

### 5.7 Tenant's own charges

The Tenant must pay direct to the supplier all charges for electricity, gas, telephone and internet supplied to the Premises and separately metered, and all volumetric and load-based trade waste charges under the Tenant's own trade waste agreement with the water authority.

## 6. Tenant's covenants

### 6.1 Use

The Tenant must use the Premises only for the permitted use in Item 18. The Tenant must not use the Premises for a public auction, as a residence, or for the storage of any goods not required for the permitted use.

documents.text:
### 6.2 Continuous trading

The Tenant must keep the retail part of the Premises open for business during the core trading hours in Item 19, properly stocked and staffed, unless prevented by an event beyond the Tenant's control. The Tenant may trade outside the core trading hours. Nothing in this clause requires the Tenant to trade on a Sunday or a public holiday.

### 6.3 Repair and maintenance

The Tenant must keep the Premises in good and substantial repair and condition, fair wear and tear and damage covered by the Landlord's insurance excepted. This obligation includes:

(a) the shop front, entry doors, door furniture and rear roller door;

(b) the internal walls, floor coverings, ceilings, ceiling grid and light fittings;

(c) the plumbing, drainage and electrical services exclusively serving the Premises, from the point of connection to the Building services;

(d) the grease and lint traps, the trade waste pre-treatment pit and the solvent separator; and

(e) the exhaust ducting, make-up air louvres and the boiler flue from the boiler to the point of discharge.

### 6.4 Servicing of plant

The Tenant must maintain, under written service agreements with suitably qualified contractors, the air conditioning serving the Premises (at least twice each year), the exhaust and make-up air systems (at least twice each year) and the grease and lint traps (at least quarterly), and must give the Landlord copies of the service records within 14 days of a written request.

### 6.5 Alterations

The Tenant must not alter the Premises without the Landlord's prior written consent, which must not be unreasonably withheld for an alteration that does not affect the structure, the roof, the external appearance or the Building services. The Tenant must give the Landlord plans and specifications, and must carry out approved works in a proper and workmanlike manner, in compliance with all laws, with all necessary building and planning approvals obtained at the Tenant's cost.

### 6.6 Signage

The Tenant may keep and maintain the fascia sign above the shop front and one under-awning sign, in each case to the dimensions and position approved by the Landlord in writing before the Commencing date. The Tenant must keep the signs clean, safe and properly illuminated, must hold and comply with any planning permit for them, and must remove them and make good at the end of the Term. The Tenant must not affix any other sign to the exterior of the Building.

### 6.7 Cleanliness

The Tenant must keep the Premises clean and free of rubbish, must not allow waste to accumulate in the common areas, must keep the bin enclosure tidy and the lids closed, and must remove all trade waste from the Building at the Tenant's cost.

### 6.8 No nuisance

The Tenant must not cause or allow any nuisance, and must take all practicable steps to prevent noise, odour, vibration, steam, heat or fumes from the Premises interfering with the occupiers of the Building or of neighbouring land. Without limiting that obligation, the Tenant must operate the solvent machines with the doors closed, must keep the carbon adsorber in service, and must not vent solvent-laden air other than through the approved stack.

### 6.9 Compliance with laws

The Tenant must comply, at the Tenant's cost, with every law, regulation, permit, licence, registration and notice applying to the Tenant's use or occupation of the Premises, including the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 (Vic), the Occupational Health and Safety Regulations 2017 (Vic), the Dangerous Goods Act 1985 (Vic) and the Environment Protection Law. The Tenant must give the Landlord a copy of any notice, direction or order received from a regulator in relation to the Premises within 3 business days of receiving it.

### 6.10 Security of the Premises

The Tenant must keep the Premises securely locked when unattended, must maintain the locks, alarm and external security lighting, and must give the Landlord a set of keys and current alarm contact details for use in an emergency.

## 7. Environmental and plant obligations

### 7.1 Solvent storage and bunding

The Tenant must store all solvent, waste solvent and solvent residue in the bunded solvent store at the rear of the plant area. The Tenant must ensure that:

(a) the bund is impervious, is kept free of stored water and is capable of retaining at least 110% of the volume of the largest container stored in it, being not less than 220 L;

(b) no more than two 200 L drums of unused solvent and two 200 L drums of waste residue are held in the Premises at any time;

(c) drums are kept closed, labelled and on a hard, sealed, chemically resistant surface which is not connected to any stormwater drain;

(d) the manifest and the safety data sheets are kept at the Premises and are available at the Bath Lane entry point; and

(e) the store is kept locked when the Premises are unattended.

### 7.2 Spill containment

The Tenant must keep a fully stocked solvent spill kit adjacent to the solvent store and a second kit adjacent to the dry cleaning machines. The Tenant must clean up any spill immediately, must not allow any Contaminant to enter the stormwater system, the sewer or the ground, and must notify the Landlord in writing within 24 hours of any spill of more than 5 L or of any spill of any volume which reaches soil or a drain.

### 7.3 EPA obligations

The Tenant is the person in management or control of the Premises for the purposes of the Environment Protection Law and holds the general environmental duty in respect of the Tenant's activities. The Tenant must:

(a) identify and minimise the risks of harm to human health and the environment from its use of solvents, so far as reasonably practicable;

(b) transport and dispose of all prescribed industrial waste only through a person authorised by the Environment Protection Authority Victoria to receive and transport it, and keep the waste transport certificates for at least five years;

(c) not cause or permit a notifiable contamination event to occur and, if one occurs, notify the Authority as required and give the Landlord a copy of that notification on the same day; and

(d) comply with any notice issued under the Environment Protection Law affecting the Premises at the Tenant's cost, whether the notice is directed to the Tenant or to the Landlord, where the notice arises from the Tenant's use or occupation.

### 7.4 Contamination indemnity

The Tenant indemnifies the Landlord against all liability, loss, cost and expense (including the cost of assessment, clean-up, remediation, monitoring and legal costs) arising from the presence, escape or migration of any Contaminant in, on, under or from the Premises to the extent caused or contributed to by the Tenant's use or occupation of the Premises during the Term or during any earlier period of occupation by the Tenant. This indemnity does not extend to contamination shown by the report in Item 27 to have existed before the Commencing date, except to the extent the Tenant's use makes that contamination worse. This clause survives the end of this Lease.

### 7.5 Boiler and pressure vessels

(a) The Tenant must keep the vertical gas-fired steam boiler installed in the plant room, registration VIC-PV-118-4470, and the air receiver serving the compressor, registered, inspected and maintained in accordance with AS 3788 and the Occupational Health and Safety Regulations 2017 (Vic).

(b) The Tenant must arrange an annual external inspection of the boiler by a competent person and must give the Landlord a copy of each inspection report and of the current registration within 14 days of a written request.

(c) The Tenant must not allow the registration to lapse while the boiler remains in the Premises, must keep the boiler log at the Premises, and must notify the Landlord within 3 business days if the boiler is taken out of service for more than 14 days.

### 7.6 Trade waste

The Tenant must hold and comply with a trade waste agreement with the water authority for the discharge from the Premises, must maintain the solvent separator and pre-treatment pit, must have the separator emptied and the sludge removed as prescribed industrial waste at least every six months, and must keep the discharge within the limits of that agreement. The Tenant must not discharge any solvent, separator water or still bottoms to sewer or stormwater, and must keep the disposal records for at least five years.

### 7.7 Exhaust and ventilation

The Tenant must operate and maintain the exhaust and ventilation systems serving the plant area, including the carbon adsorber and the solvent vent stack, so that the workplace exposure standard for perchloroethylene is not exceeded. The Tenant must have the plant area atmosphere monitored at least once each year by a competent person and must give the Landlord a copy of the result on written request. The stack must not be altered, extended or relocated without the Landlord's prior written consent.

### 7.8 Environmental site condition reports

(a) The parties acknowledge that the site condition report in Item 27, prepared by Terrafield Environmental Pty Ltd and annexed as Annexure B, was obtained jointly before the Commencing date. It records the condition of the Premises, the soil and the groundwater at the Commencing date and is the baseline against which the Tenant's obligations under clauses 7.4 and 14.6 are measured.

(b) Not earlier than three months before and not later than the last day of the Term, the Tenant must obtain and give to the Landlord a further site condition report for the Premises, prepared at the Tenant's cost by an environmental consultant with appropriate professional indemnity insurance, reasonably acceptable to the Landlord, and using a scope and sampling locations equivalent to those in Annexure B.

(c) If the exit report shows contamination which is worse than the baseline in Annexure B and which is attributable to the Tenant's use, the Tenant must, at the Tenant's cost, carry out the remediation reasonably required to return the Premises to the baseline condition, and clause 14.6 applies to that work.

### 7.9 Plant penetrations

The Tenant must keep every penetration of the floor slab, walls, roof and ceiling made for the Tenant's plant properly sealed, flashed and weathertight, and must keep a written record of each penetration showing its location and purpose. That record must be given to the Landlord with the exit report under clause 7.8(b).

## 8. Landlord's covenants

### 8.1 Quiet enjoyment

While the Tenant pays the Rent and performs its obligations, the Tenant may occupy and use the Premises without interruption from the Landlord or any person claiming through the Landlord, except as this Lease allows.

### 8.2 Structural repair

The Landlord must keep in good repair and condition the structure of the Building, including the roof, the roof drainage, the external walls, the foundations, the floor slab and the Building services up to the point at which they enter the Premises, unless the disrepair is caused by the Tenant or by the Tenant's plant. The Landlord must carry out that work with reasonable diligence after becoming aware of the need for it.

### 8.3 Common areas

The Landlord must keep the common areas clean, lit, drained and reasonably fit for their purpose, and must not do anything which unreasonably obstructs the Tenant's access to the Premises from Hargreaves Street or from Bath Lane.

### 8.4 Essential safety measures

The Landlord must maintain the essential safety measures for the Building, must keep the annual essential safety measures report, and must give the Tenant a copy on request.

## 9. Insurance and indemnity

### 9.1 Landlord's insurance

The Landlord must insure the Building for its full replacement value against fire, storm, tempest and other usual risks, together with loss of rent for not less than 12 months, and must maintain public liability insurance for the common areas for not less than $20,000,000.

### 9.2 Tenant's insurance

The Tenant must take out and keep current throughout the Term, with an insurer authorised to carry on insurance business in Australia:

(a) public and products liability insurance for not less than the amount in Item 21 for any one occurrence;

(b) pollution or environmental impairment liability insurance for not less than the amount in Item 22, covering sudden and accidental pollution arising from the Tenant's use of the Premises;

(c) plate glass insurance for the amount in Item 23, including the shop front;

(d) insurance of the Tenant's plant, fixtures, fittings, stock and customers' goods in the Tenant's care, custody or control, for full replacement value;

(e) machinery breakdown insurance for the boiler and pressure vessels; and

(f) workers compensation insurance as required by law.

### 9.3 Landlord's interest to be noted

The Tenant must have the Landlord's interest noted as an interested party on the policies in clauses 9.2(a) and 9.2(b), must give the Landlord a certificate of currency for each policy in clause 9.2 before the Commencing date and within 14 days after each renewal, must not do anything at the Premises which invalidates or increases the premium of the Landlord's insurance, and must pay any increase in the Landlord's premium caused by the Tenant's use beyond the permitted use as disclosed.

### 9.4 Indemnity and release

The Tenant indemnifies the Landlord against all liability, loss, cost and expense in connection with loss of or damage to property, or injury to or death of any person, arising from the Tenant's use or occupation of the Premises, except to the extent caused by the negligence or default of the Landlord or of a person for whom the Landlord is responsible. The Tenant occupies the Premises at its own risk and releases the Landlord from liability for loss or damage to the Tenant's property or business caused by the escape of water, steam, gas or electricity, or by the act of any other occupier, except to the extent caused by the negligence or default of the Landlord.

### 9.5 Landlord's right of entry

The Landlord and its agents may enter the Premises at any reasonable time on not less than 48 hours' written notice, or at any time in an emergency without notice, to inspect, to carry out the Landlord's obligations, to carry out work required by a public authority, and to show the Premises to a prospective purchaser or, during the last six months of the Term, to a prospective tenant. Entry to the plant area is subject to the Tenant's site induction and to the Tenant's reasonable safety directions.

## 10. Damage and destruction

### 10.1 Abatement

If the Premises or the Building are damaged so that the Premises or any part of them are unfit for use or inaccessible, the base rent and outgoings abate from the date of damage in proportion to the part of the Premises unfit for use or inaccessible, until the Premises are again fit for use and accessible.

### 10.2 Repair or termination

(a) The Landlord is not obliged to reinstate the Premises or the Building.

(b) If the Landlord notifies the Tenant that the Landlord does not intend to reinstate, either party may terminate this Lease by 7 days' written notice.

(c) If the Landlord does not repair the damage within a reasonable time after the Tenant asks in writing, the Tenant may terminate this Lease by 7 days' written notice.

(d) This clause operates subject to and in accordance with section 57 of the Act.

### 10.3 Tenant's fault

Clauses 10.1 and 10.2 do not apply if the damage is caused or contributed to by the Tenant, or by an act or omission of the Tenant's employees, contractors or customers, or by the Tenant's plant, and to that extent the Rent does not abate.

## 11. Assignment and subletting

documents.text:
### 11.1 Consent required

The Tenant must not assign, sublet, part with possession of, mortgage or otherwise deal with its interest in the Premises without the Landlord's prior written consent.

### 11.2 Grounds for withholding consent

The Landlord may withhold consent to an assignment only on a ground permitted by section 60 of the Act, including where the proposed assignee proposes to change the use of the Premises, where the proposed assignee has financial resources or retailing skills inferior to those of the Tenant, or where the Tenant has not complied with clause 11.3.

### 11.3 Process

The Tenant must:

(a) ask for consent in writing and give the Landlord information the Landlord reasonably requires about the proposed assignee's financial standing and retailing skills;

(b) give the proposed assignee a copy of the disclosure statement given to the Tenant, updated in accordance with section 61 of the Act, together with details of any change in the information in it, at least 7 days before asking for consent; and

(c) procure that the proposed assignee gives the Landlord a written statement that it has received and read that disclosure statement.

### 11.4 Landlord's response

The Landlord must deal with the request in accordance with section 60 of the Act. If the Landlord has not given or withheld consent within 28 days after the request and all required information are given, the Landlord is taken to have consented.

### 11.5 Conditions of consent

Consent may be given on condition that the assignee executes a deed of covenant with the Landlord, that any guarantor of the assignee gives a guarantee in the same form as this Lease, that the assignee provides replacement security under clause 13, and that the Tenant pays the Landlord's reasonable legal and investigation costs of the assignment.

### 11.6 Change in control

A change in the persons holding a majority of the issued shares or of the voting power in the Tenant is an assignment for the purposes of this clause, other than a transfer by will or on intestacy.

## 12. Default, remedies and essential terms

### 12.1 Events of default

The Tenant is in default if:

(a) any Rent remains unpaid for 14 days after its due date, whether or not demanded;

(b) the Tenant breaches any other provision of this Lease and does not remedy the breach within the time stated in a notice given under section 146 of the Property Law Act 1958 (Vic);

(c) the Tenant is wound up, has a controller or administrator appointed, or is unable to pay its debts as they fall due;

(d) execution is levied against the Tenant and is not satisfied within 14 days; or

(e) the Tenant abandons the Premises.

### 12.2 Essential terms

The following are essential terms of this Lease: clauses 4.1 (payment of base rent), 5.1 (outgoings), 6.1 (use), 6.9 (compliance with laws), 7.1 (solvent storage and bunding), 7.3 (EPA obligations), 7.5 (boiler and pressure vessels), 7.6 (trade waste), 9.2 (Tenant's insurance), 11.1 (assignment) and 13.1 (security). Breach of an essential term is a repudiation of this Lease.

### 12.3 Landlord's remedies

If the Tenant is in default the Landlord may, subject to the Act and to the Property Law Act 1958 (Vic), re-enter the Premises and terminate this Lease, or terminate this Lease by notice without re-entry, and in either case recover from the Tenant damages for the loss of the benefit of this Lease for what would have been the remainder of the Term, in addition to Rent and other amounts owing at the date of termination.

### 12.4 Mitigation

The Landlord must take reasonable steps to mitigate its loss, including by taking reasonable steps to re-let the Premises on reasonable terms.

### 12.5 Landlord may remedy

If the Tenant fails to do anything this Lease requires it to do, the Landlord may, after giving the Tenant 14 days' written notice or immediately in an emergency, do it, and the reasonable cost is payable by the Tenant as Rent on demand.

### 12.6 No waiver

Acceptance of Rent after a default, or delay in acting on a default, does not waive the default or affect the Landlord's rights.

## 13. Security and guarantee

### 13.1 Bank guarantee

The Tenant must, before the Commencing date, give the Landlord an unconditional and irrevocable bank guarantee for the amount in Item 20, issued by an authorised deposit-taking institution, in favour of the Landlord, with no expiry date or with an expiry date not earlier than 6 months after the Terminating date.

### 13.2 Adjustment

Within 28 days after each rent review the Tenant must, if asked in writing, replace the bank guarantee with one for an amount equal to three months' base rent as reviewed, plus GST.

### 13.3 Call on the guarantee

The Landlord may call on the bank guarantee to make good any amount owing by the Tenant, any cost of remedying a breach, and any cost of remediation or make good under clauses 7.8 and 14. If the Landlord calls on the guarantee, the Tenant must restore it to the full amount within 14 days.

### 13.4 Return

The Landlord must return the bank guarantee to the Tenant within 30 days after the later of the end of the Term, the Tenant giving vacant possession, the exit report under clause 7.8(b) being given, and all amounts owing being paid.

### 13.5 Guarantee and indemnity

The Guarantor guarantees to the Landlord the payment of the Rent and the performance of the Tenant's obligations under this Lease, and indemnifies the Landlord against loss arising from the Tenant's failure to pay or perform. The Guarantor's liability is that of a principal debtor, is not affected by any indulgence given to the Tenant, by any variation of this Lease, or by the Landlord's release of any security, and continues during any holding over and during any further term granted under clause 3.3.

## 14. End of term and make good

### 14.1 Yield up

At the end of the Term the Tenant must give the Landlord vacant possession of the Premises, clean, free of rubbish, and in the condition required by clause 6.3, with all keys, access cards and service records handed over.

### 14.2 Removal of the Tenant's plant

The Tenant must, before the end of the Term, remove all of the Tenant's plant, including the items listed in Annexure D, and must:

(a) disconnect and cap the gas, water, steam, condensate, compressed air, trade waste and electrical services serving the removed plant at the point directed by the Landlord;

(b) drain, purge and certify free of solvent every tank, pipe, still, separator and duct which held solvent before removing it from the Premises;

(c) remove the solvent vent stack and the boiler flue and make good the roof and wall penetrations, weathertight, to the standard of the surrounding surface;

(d) remove the plant plinths and reinstate the floor slab to a level, sealed finish; and

(e) make good all penetrations recorded under clause 7.9.

### 14.3 Landlord's fixtures

The Tenant must not remove any of the Landlord's fixtures listed in Annexure C, and must leave them in the condition required by clause 6.3.

### 14.4 Election to retain

The Landlord may, by written notice given at least three months before the end of the Term, elect that any item of the Tenant's plant remain in the Premises, in which case that item becomes the property of the Landlord at the end of the Term at no cost and the Tenant is released from its obligation to remove it and to make good in respect of it.

### 14.5 Failure to make good

If the Tenant does not comply with clauses 14.1 to 14.3, the Landlord may carry out the work and recover the reasonable cost from the Tenant as a debt, and may treat any of the Tenant's plant left in the Premises more than 14 days after the end of the Term as abandoned and dispose of it.

### 14.6 Environmental report a condition of make good

Make good is not complete until the exit report under clause 7.8(b) has been given to the Landlord and any remediation required by clause 7.8(c) has been completed.

## 15. Retail Leases Act 2003 provisions

### 15.1 Disclosure statement

The Tenant acknowledges receiving from the Landlord a disclosure statement in the form required by the Act on the date in Item 26, being at least 14 days before this Lease was entered into, together with the Small Business Commission's information brochure and a copy of the proposed lease.

### 15.2 Copy of lease

The Landlord must give the Tenant a copy of this Lease signed by both parties within 28 days after this Lease is returned to the Landlord signed by the Tenant.

### 15.3 Registration

The Tenant may lodge a caveat or, if this Lease is capable of registration, register this Lease at the Tenant's cost. The Landlord must do all things reasonably required to enable registration, including obtaining any mortgagee's consent.

### 15.4 Dispute resolution

If a dispute arises under this Lease, either party may refer it to the Victorian Small Business Commission for mediation under Part 10 of the Act. Neither party may commence proceedings in the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal in respect of a retail tenancy dispute unless the Commission has certified that mediation has failed or is unlikely to resolve the dispute. This clause does not prevent either party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.

### 15.5 No land tax

Nothing in this Lease requires the Tenant to pay land tax or any amount on account of land tax, and any provision to that effect is void under section 50 of the Act.

### 15.6 No key money

The Landlord has not sought or accepted key money or any payment for the goodwill of the Tenant's business, and must not do so.

### 15.7 Costs

Each party bears its own costs of negotiating and preparing this Lease. The Landlord must not recover from the Tenant the Landlord's costs of preparing, negotiating or executing this Lease, in accordance with section 51 of the Act. The Tenant must pay the Landlord's reasonable costs of any consent, variation or assignment requested by the Tenant, and all stamp duty and registration fees.

## 16. Notices, GST and general

### 16.1 Notices

A notice under this Lease must be in writing and may be given by hand, by prepaid post to the address in Item 24 or Item 25, or by email to the address in Item 24 or Item 25. A notice is taken to be received: if delivered by hand, on delivery; if posted, on the third business day after posting; if emailed, at the time the email enters the recipient's information system, unless the sender receives an automated notice of non-delivery. A party may change its address by notice.

### 16.2 GST

All amounts payable under this Lease are exclusive of GST. If GST is payable on a taxable supply made under this Lease, the recipient must pay the supplier the GST at the same time as the consideration, on receipt of a valid tax invoice. Where a party must reimburse another party for an expense, the amount reimbursed is the expense less any input tax credit available.

### 16.3 Entire agreement

This Lease and the disclosure statement record the entire agreement between the parties about the Premises and supersede all earlier agreements and representations. A variation must be in writing and signed by both parties.

### 16.4 Governing law and severance

This Lease is governed by the law of Victoria and the parties submit to the jurisdiction of the courts and tribunals of Victoria. If a provision of this Lease is void or unenforceable it is severed and the rest of this Lease continues in force.

### 16.5 Further assurance

Each party must do all things reasonably necessary to give full effect to this Lease.

The Premises include the staff toilet and kitchenette in the south-west corner and the roofed section of the rear loading platform. The solvent store is in the south-east corner of the plant area, adjacent to the Bath Lane roller door.

Site condition report for Shop 4, 118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo, prepared by Terrafield Environmental Pty Ltd, reference TF-2401-118HG, dated 22 February 2024. A copy is held by each party. Sampling locations are recorded on figure 3 of that report and are to be reproduced in the exit report under clause 7.8(b).

The following remain the property of the Landlord and must not be removed by the Tenant:

## PART 2 — OPERATIVE PROVISIONS

## 1. Definitions and interpretation

### 1.1 Definitions

In this agreement, unless the contrary intention appears:

**Accounting year** means the period in Item 13.

**Centre** means the shopping centre in Item 4, including the mall, the car park, the service corridors, the loading dock, the amenities and every other common area, and any part of it as it exists from time to time.

**Centre rules** means the rules in Annexure B, as amended by the Licensor from time to time under clause 8.3.

**Fee** means the licence fee, the turnover fee, the promotion levy and every other amount payable by the Licensee under this agreement.

**Gross turnover** has the meaning given in clause 5.1.

**Licensed Area** means the area in Item 5.

**Licensor** includes the owner of the Centre from time to time and any person appointed by the owner to manage the Centre.

**Retail Leases Act** means the Retail Leases Act 2003 (Vic).

**Term** means the period from the Commencing date in Item 7 to the Expiry date in Item 8.

**Turnover threshold** means the amount in Item 12.

### 1.2 Interpretation

(a) A reference to legislation includes that legislation as amended or replaced.

(b) The singular includes the plural and the reverse.

(c) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

(d) A reference to a clause, Item or Annexure is a reference to a clause of this agreement, an Item of the Reference Schedule or an Annexure to this agreement.

(e) Money is Australian currency and measurements are metric.

(f) Where the Licensor's consent or approval is required, it may be given conditionally unless this agreement says otherwise.

## 2. Nature of this agreement

### 2.1 A licence, not a lease

This agreement grants the Licensee a personal, non-exclusive, contractual right to occupy and use the Licensed Area for the permitted use for the Term. It does not grant, and is not intended to grant, a lease, a tenancy, an easement, or any estate or interest in the Centre or in any land.

### 2.2 What that means

The parties acknowledge and agree that:

(a) the Licensor retains legal possession and control of the whole of the Centre, including the Licensed Area;

(b) the Licensee does not have exclusive possession of the Licensed Area, and the Licensor and its employees, contractors and agents may enter the Licensed Area at any time under clause 8.5;

(c) the Licensor may relocate the Licensee within the Centre under clause 8.6, which is inconsistent with the grant of an estate in a defined parcel of land;

(d) the rights granted are personal to the Licensee, are not assignable except under clause 11, and do not run with the land;

(e) the Licensee must not lodge a caveat or any other dealing against the title to the Centre, and irrevocably authorises the Licensor to withdraw any caveat lodged in breach of this paragraph; and

(f) on the Expiry date, or on earlier termination, the Licensee's right to occupy simply ends, and the Licensee is not entitled to any notice to quit, to compensation for goodwill, or to any right of renewal.

### 2.3 Why the parties have used a licence

The parties have chosen a licence because the Licensed Area is a small serviced position on the mall alignment, formed of counter and racking only, without demising walls, without a separate services connection beyond lighting, power and the hand basin, and because the position may need to be moved to accommodate the Licensor's leasing, refurbishment and remerchandising of the Centre. The Licensee acknowledges that it has been given the opportunity to obtain its own legal and financial advice about the difference between a licence and a retail lease before signing.

### 2.4 Revocation

The Licensor may revoke this licence only in accordance with clause 12. Nothing in clause 2.1 or 2.2 entitles the Licensor to revoke the licence at will during the Term while the Licensee is not in default.

## 3. Grant and term

### 3.1 Grant

In consideration of the Fee and of the Licensee's obligations, the Licensor grants the Licensee the right to occupy and use the Licensed Area for the permitted use in Item 16 during the Term, together with the right to use the common areas of the Centre in common with the Licensor, the other occupants of the Centre and the public.

### 3.2 Term

The Term commences on the date in Item 7 and ends on the date in Item 8, unless ended earlier under this agreement.

### 3.3 Fitout period

The Licensee may occupy the Licensed Area during the fitout period in Item 23 for the purpose of carrying out the approved fitout. No licence fee, turnover fee or promotion levy is payable for the fitout period, but every other obligation of the Licensee under this agreement, including insurance and the Centre rules, applies during it.

### 3.4 No option

There is no option to renew. The Licensee acknowledges that it has no right to a further licence and that the Licensor may licence or lease the Licensed Area to any other person after the Expiry date.

### 3.5 Negotiation for a further licence

If the Licensee wishes to negotiate a further licence it must give the Licensor written notice not later than 31 December 2026. The Licensor must respond in writing within 60 days after receiving that notice, either by offering terms for a further licence or by declining to offer a further licence. Neither party is obliged to agree, and a failure to agree does not give rise to any claim by the Licensee.

### 3.6 Holding over

If the Licensee remains in occupation after the Expiry date with the Licensor's written consent, it does so as a monthly licensee on the terms of this agreement so far as they can apply, at the licence fee, turnover fee and promotion levy payable immediately before the Expiry date, terminable by either party on one month's written notice expiring on any day. Occupation after the Expiry date without consent is a trespass and clause 13.4 applies.

## 4. Fee

### 4.1 Licence fee

The Licensee must pay the licence fee in Item 11 by equal monthly instalments of $1,800.00 plus GST in advance on the first day of each month, without deduction, set-off or demand, by direct debit from the account nominated by the Licensee, or by such other method as the Licensor requires in writing.

### 4.2 Promotion levy

The Licensee must pay the promotion levy in Item 14 with each instalment of the licence fee. The Licensor must apply the promotion levy, together with amounts collected from other occupants, to the marketing, advertising and promotion of the Centre, and must give the Licensee a written summary of promotional expenditure for each accounting year within three months after the end of that year on written request.

### 4.3 Review of the licence fee

The licence fee is fixed for the Term. The promotion levy may be increased by the Licensor once in each accounting year, by not more than 5% or the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index (All Groups, Melbourne), whichever is the greater, on not less than one month's written notice.

### 4.4 No separate outgoings

The licence fee includes the Licensee's contribution to the Centre's outgoings, including rates, taxes, insurance, air conditioning, common area cleaning, security, waste collection and centre management. The Licensee must pay for its own electricity where separately metered, its own telephone and internet, and its own point of sale and merchant fees.

### 4.5 Interest on late payment

If any Fee remains unpaid for 7 days after its due date, the Licensee must pay interest on the unpaid amount from the due date until payment at 2% per annum above the rate fixed from time to time under section 2 of the Penalty Interest Rates Act 1983 (Vic).

### 4.6 Fee is payable regardless of trading

The Fee is payable whether or not the Licensee trades, except where the Licensed Area is unusable for a continuous period of more than 5 days because of an act or omission of the Licensor, in which case the licence fee and promotion levy abate proportionally for the period of unusability.

## 5. Turnover fee, reporting and audit

### 5.1 Gross turnover

Gross turnover means the total of all money and the value of all other consideration received or receivable by the Licensee, or by any person on the Licensee's behalf, from business conducted at or from the Licensed Area, whether for cash or on credit and whether or not the goods or services are delivered or performed at the Licensed Area. Without limiting that meaning, gross turnover includes:

(a) all amounts received at the Licensed Area for dry cleaning, laundering, pressing, alterations and repairs, whether the work is done at the Licensed Area or at the Licensee's plant at 118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo;

(b) all amounts received at the Licensed Area for garments received at any other place, where the customer pays at the Licensed Area;

(c) the retail sale of garment care products, hangers, covers and similar goods;

(d) deposits forfeited by customers and amounts received for uncollected garments; and

(e) amounts received from insurers, employers or other third parties for work booked in at the Licensed Area.

### 5.2 Exclusions from gross turnover

Gross turnover does not include:

(a) GST;

(b) refunds and allowances actually made to customers for goods or services previously included in gross turnover;

(c) amounts received for garments received at the Licensed Area but paid for at the Licensee's Bendigo premises, provided those amounts are not otherwise included;

(d) proceeds of the sale of the Licensee's own plant, fittings or equipment; and

(e) discounts allowed to staff, to a maximum of 2% of gross turnover in any accounting year.

### 5.3 Turnover fee

Within 30 days after the Licensor gives the Licensee an account calculated from the annual certified statement for an accounting year, the Licensee must pay the Licensor the turnover fee in Item 12, being 4% of the amount by which gross turnover for that accounting year exceeds the turnover threshold of $180,000.00, plus GST. For a part accounting year the turnover threshold is apportioned on a daily basis.

### 5.4 Monthly reporting

The Licensee must give the Licensor, by the 7th day of each month, a written statement of gross turnover at the Licensed Area for the preceding month, signed by the Licensee or by a person authorised by the Licensee. The statement must be given in the form in Annexure C or in such other form as the Licensor reasonably requires, and must be supported by point of sale reports on request.

### 5.5 Annual certified statement

Within 60 days after the end of each accounting year the Licensee must give the Licensor a statement of gross turnover for that accounting year, certified as correct by the Licensee's accountant or by the director of the Licensee, reconciled to the Licensee's business activity statements for the periods falling within that accounting year.

### 5.6 Records

The Licensee must keep at the Licensed Area or at its Bendigo premises, for at least five years, full and accurate records of gross turnover, including point of sale records, daily takings summaries, docket books, banking records and the records required by the taxation laws. The Licensee must operate a point of sale system which records every transaction at the Licensed Area separately from transactions at any other premises of the Licensee.

Licensed Area Shop 12, Lansell Square, 233 High Street, Kangaroo Flat VIC 3555 - 24 m2 on the mall alignment.
A licence, not a lease: no exclusive possession, no estate in land, and the Licensor may relocate under clause 8.6.
Agreement dated 11 June 2024. Fitout period 17 to 30 June 2024, no fee payable.
Term three years, 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2027. No option to renew.
To negotiate a further licence the Licensee must give written notice by 31 December 2026; the Licensor answers within 60 days, and neither side must agree.
Licence fee $21,600.00 plus GST a year, paid $1,800.00 plus GST monthly in advance. The fee is fixed for the Term - there is no review.
Promotion levy $1,296.00 plus GST a year, $108.00 plus GST monthly, raisable once an accounting year by the greater of 5% or Melbourne CPI on one month's notice.
Turnover fee 4% of gross turnover above the $180,000.00 threshold, plus GST, due 30 days after the Licensor's account.
Outgoings are included in the licence fee; there is no separate contribution. The Licensee pays its own electricity, telephone and merchant fees.
Security: bank guarantee $5,940.00, three months' fee plus GST.
Insurance: public liability $20,000,000; customers' goods at least $50,000.
Approved trading hours Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 5:00 pm and Saturday 9:00 am to 1:00 pm.
Turnover reported monthly by the 7th, with a certified annual statement within 60 days of 30 June.
