### 5.7 Late reporting

If the Licensee does not give a monthly statement within 7 days after it is due, the Licensee must pay the Licensor an administration charge of $50.00 plus GST for each week or part week the statement remains outstanding, to a maximum of $500.00 plus GST for any one statement. If a monthly statement is more than 30 days late, the Licensor may estimate gross turnover for that month at 110% of the highest monthly gross turnover reported in the preceding 12 months, and that estimate is taken to be the gross turnover for that month unless the Licensee gives the statement and supporting records within a further 14 days.

### 5.8 Audit

The Licensor may, once in each accounting year and once within 12 months after the end of the Term, have the Licensee's records of gross turnover examined by an accountant nominated by the Licensor. The Licensee must give that accountant access to the records within 10 business days of a written request. The Licensor bears the cost of the examination unless it shows that gross turnover for the period examined was understated by more than 5%, in which case the Licensee must pay the reasonable cost of the examination and any turnover fee shortfall, with interest under clause 4.5, within 14 days.

### 5.9 Confidentiality

The Licensor must keep the Licensee's turnover information confidential and must not disclose it except to its officers, professional advisers, financiers, auditors and the owner of the Centre, or where required by law, or in aggregated form which does not identify the Licensee.

## 6. Trading

### 6.1 Obligation to trade

The Licensee must open the Licensed Area for business and trade continuously during the Licensee's approved trading hours in Item 19 throughout the Term, properly staffed, stocked and lit, with the counter attended at all times while the Licensed Area is open.

### 6.2 Centre trading hours and variation

The centre trading hours are in Item 18. The Licensor has approved in writing, on 14 June 2024, the shorter trading hours in Item 19 for the Licensee, having regard to the service nature of the permitted use. The Licensor may vary the centre trading hours on not less than one month's written notice. The Licensee's approved hours continue to apply unless the Licensor withdraws that approval on not less than three months' written notice, and the Licensee must then trade during the centre trading hours.

### 6.3 Extended trading

The Licensee must open during any additional trading period nominated by the Licensor for the Christmas trading period, being not more than 10 days in any accounting year, on not less than 21 days' written notice.

### 6.4 Failure to trade

If the Licensee fails to open during the approved trading hours, otherwise than because of an event beyond its control, the Licensee must pay the Licensor liquidated damages of $150.00 plus GST for each day or part day on which it fails to open, which the parties agree is a genuine pre-estimate of the loss to the Centre from a dark shop on the mall alignment.

### 6.5 Presentation

The Licensee must keep the Licensed Area clean, tidy and well presented, must keep garment racking behind the counter line and within the Licensed Area, must not place any rack, sign, bin, A-frame or display outside the licence line marked on the plan in Annexure A, and must ensure that its staff wear the uniform and name badge approved by the Licensor.

## 7. Use of the Licensed Area

### 7.1 Permitted use

The Licensee must use the Licensed Area only for the permitted use in Item 16 and for no other purpose.

### 7.2 No plant, no cleaning on site

The Licensee must not, at the Licensed Area:

(a) install or operate any dry cleaning machine, washing machine, tumble dryer, boiler, still, steam generator, compressor or press;

(b) carry out any dry cleaning, wet cleaning, laundering, dyeing or bulk pressing;

(c) bring, store, use or handle any solvent, including perchloroethylene and hydrocarbon solvent, or any solvent-contaminated waste, filter, residue or rag;

(d) use water for any purpose other than hand washing at the hand basin in Item 5, or connect any appliance to the water supply or to the sewer; or

(e) carry out any process which produces steam, odour, heat, noise, effluent or trade waste.

The only steam appliance permitted at the Licensed Area is a single hand-held garment steamer of not more than 2,000 W, filled from the hand basin, used for touch-up finishing only, and switched off and stored behind the counter when not in use.

### 7.3 Garments to be cleaned off site

All garments received at the Licensed Area for cleaning must be transported to the Licensee's plant at Shop 4, 118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo, and cleaned there or at another licensed plant, and returned to the Licensed Area for collection by the customer. Garments must be transported in a covered vehicle and must not be left in the Centre's common areas, service corridors or loading dock at any time.

### 7.4 Garment storage

The Licensee must keep all garments within the Licensed Area, on the racking, bagged and tagged. The Licensee must not store garments in the Centre's common areas, must not exceed the racking capacity of the Licensed Area, and must remove uncollected garments to its Bendigo premises where they are held for more than 60 days.

### 7.5 Odour

The Licensee must ensure that garments brought into the Centre do not give off solvent odour. Garments must be fully aired at the Licensee's plant before delivery to the Licensed Area. If the Licensor gives the Licensee written notice of a substantiated odour complaint, the Licensee must investigate and report to the Licensor within 5 business days and must take the steps reasonably necessary to prevent a recurrence.

### 7.6 Compliance with laws

The Licensee must comply, at its own cost, with every law, regulation, permit, licence and notice applying to its use of the Licensed Area, including the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 (Vic) and the Australian Consumer Law, must display the prices and turnaround times for its services, and must give the Licensor a copy of any notice or order received from a regulator in relation to the Licensed Area within 3 business days.

### 7.7 No nuisance

The Licensee must not cause or allow any nuisance, obstruction, noise, odour or interference with any other occupant of the Centre or with the Centre's customers, must not play amplified music, and must not use any loudspeaker, bell or public address device.

## 8. Fitout, signage, rules and the Licensor's rights

### 8.1 Fitout

The Licensee must carry out the fitout of the Licensed Area in accordance with the Licensor's shopfitting guide and the drawings approved in writing by the Licensor before the Commencing date. The Licensee must not commence any fitout or shopfitting work until the Licensor has approved the drawings, the contractor has given the Licensor a certificate of currency for public liability insurance of not less than $20,000,000 and workers compensation insurance, and the contractor has completed the Centre's contractor induction.

### 8.2 Signage

The Licensee may display one fascia sign to the dimensions, materials, illumination and position approved by the Licensor in writing, in accordance with the Centre's signage code. The Licensee must not display any other sign, poster, decal, price ticket or promotional material visible from the mall without the Licensor's prior written approval, other than a single A4 price list mounted on the counter.

### 8.3 Centre rules

The Licensee must comply, and must ensure its employees and contractors comply, with the Centre rules in Annexure B. The Licensor may amend the Centre rules from time to time on not less than 14 days' written notice, provided the amended rules are not inconsistent with this agreement and apply generally to occupants of the Centre.

### 8.4 Licensor's works

The Licensor may at any time carry out repairs, alterations, refurbishment, extension or redevelopment of the Centre, may close or alter any part of the common areas, may alter the location of entrances, travelators, amenities and car parking, and may erect hoardings and scaffolding, without any abatement of the Fee and without any claim by the Licensee, provided the Licensor uses reasonable endeavours to minimise interference with the Licensee's business and to maintain reasonable access to the Licensed Area.

### 8.5 Access by the Licensor

The Licensor and its employees, contractors and agents may enter the Licensed Area at any time to inspect, to clean, to carry out works, to read meters, to exercise the Licensor's rights under this agreement, to comply with a requirement of a public authority, and in an emergency. The Licensor must, other than in an emergency, use reasonable endeavours to avoid interfering with the Licensee's business.

### 8.6 Relocation

(a) The Licensor may relocate the Licensee to another area within the Centre on not less than three months' written notice.

(b) The new area must be of a comparable size and of a standard of position and customer flow reasonably comparable to the Licensed Area, and must be suitable for the permitted use.

(c) The Licensor must pay the Licensee's reasonable costs of dismantling, moving and reinstalling the counter, racking and signage, and of altering stationery and advertising material, on production of invoices, to a maximum of the amount in Item 27.

(d) On relocation, the licence fee, the promotion levy and the turnover threshold remain unchanged unless the parties agree otherwise in writing, and every other provision of this agreement continues to apply to the new area, which then becomes the Licensed Area.

(e) If the Licensee does not accept the relocation, it may terminate this agreement by written notice given within 21 days after the Licensor's notice, and the termination takes effect on the date nominated in the Licensor's notice for relocation.

### 8.7 No exclusivity

The Licensor gives no exclusivity of trade. The Licensor may licence or lease any other part of the Centre to a person carrying on a business which competes with the Licensee's business, and the Licensee has no claim in respect of that.

## 9. Services, cleaning and waste

### 9.1 Services

The Licensor must provide lighting, power, air conditioning to the mall, and water to the hand basin, during the centre trading hours. The Licensor is not liable for any interruption to a service which is beyond its reasonable control, and no interruption entitles the Licensee to terminate or to any abatement except under clause 4.6.

### 9.2 Cleaning

The Licensor cleans the common areas. The Licensee must clean the Licensed Area daily, including the counter, racking, floor covering and glass within the Licensed Area, and must keep the hand basin and its trap clean and clear.

### 9.3 Waste

The Licensee must remove all its waste from the Licensed Area to the Centre's waste compactor at the loading dock, at the times allowed by the Centre rules, and must separate recyclable material. The Licensee must not place any garment bag, hanger box, packaging or other waste in the mall bins, and must not bring into the Centre any waste generated at its Bendigo premises.

### 9.4 Deliveries

Deliveries to and collections from the Licensed Area must be made through the service corridor at the times allowed by the Centre rules, and not through the mall during centre trading hours. Garment trolleys must be covered and must not be left unattended in the service corridor.

## 10. Insurance and indemnity

### 10.1 Licensee's insurance

The Licensee must take out and keep current throughout the Term, with an insurer authorised to carry on insurance business in Australia:

(a) public and products liability insurance for not less than the amount in Item 21 for any one occurrence, noting the interest of the Licensor and of the owner of the Centre;

(b) insurance of customers' goods in the Licensee's care, custody or control at the Licensed Area for not less than the amount in Item 22;

(c) insurance of the Licensee's counter, racking, fittings, equipment and stock for full replacement value;

(d) plate glass insurance for the full replacement value of all glass installed by the Licensee; and

(e) workers compensation insurance as required by law.

### 10.2 Evidence

The Licensee must give the Licensor a certificate of currency for each policy before it first occupies the Licensed Area and within 14 days after each renewal, and must notify the Licensor within 5 business days if a policy is cancelled, is not renewed, or is materially altered.

### 10.3 Licensor's insurance

The Licensor insures the Centre and its own liability. That insurance is for the Licensor's benefit only, does not extend to the Licensee, its property or its customers' goods, and the Licensee must not rely on it.

### 10.4 Conduct affecting insurance

The Licensee must not do anything at the Licensed Area which invalidates or increases the premium of the Licensor's insurance, and must pay any increase in that premium caused by its use of the Licensed Area.

### 10.5 Indemnity

The Licensee indemnifies the Licensor and the owner of the Centre against all liability, loss, cost and expense in connection with loss of or damage to property, or injury to or death of any person, arising from the Licensee's use or occupation of the Licensed Area, from any act or omission of the Licensee or of its employees, contractors or customers, or from any breach of this agreement by the Licensee, except to the extent caused by the negligence or default of the Licensor.

### 10.6 Release

The Licensee occupies the Licensed Area at its own risk and releases the Licensor from liability for loss of or damage to the Licensee's property, the Licensee's customers' goods, or the Licensee's business, however caused, except to the extent caused by the negligence or default of the Licensor.

### 10.7 Customers' goods

The Licensee is solely responsible to its customers for garments received at the Licensed Area. The Licensor is not a bailee of any garment and has no liability to any customer of the Licensee.

## 11. Assignment

### 11.1 Personal right

This licence is personal to the Licensee. The Licensee must not assign, sublicense, part with possession of, share the occupation of, or otherwise deal with its rights under this agreement, and must not permit any other person to trade from the Licensed Area.

### 11.2 Change in control

A change in the persons holding a majority of the issued shares or of the voting power in the Licensee is a dealing prohibited by clause 11.1 unless the Licensor consents in writing, other than a transfer by will or on intestacy.

### 11.3 Sale of the Licensee's business

If the Licensee sells its dry cleaning business as a going concern, it may ask the Licensor in writing to grant a new licence to the purchaser on the same terms for the balance of the Term. The Licensor must not unreasonably refuse, but may require that the purchaser demonstrate financial standing and retailing experience at least equivalent to the Licensee's, that the purchaser provide equivalent security and a guarantee from its principals, that the Licensee pay the Licensor's reasonable costs, and that the Licensee and the Guarantor remain liable for all amounts accrued to the date the new licence is granted.

### 11.4 Licensor may deal freely

The Licensor may sell, transfer, mortgage or otherwise deal with the Centre or with its interest in it. The Licensee must, on request, sign any document reasonably required to acknowledge the interest of a purchaser, mortgagee or new manager, and this agreement continues on the same terms.

## 12. Default and termination

### 12.1 Default

The Licensee is in default if:

(a) any Fee remains unpaid for 7 days after its due date, whether or not demanded;

(b) the Licensee breaches any other provision of this agreement and does not remedy the breach within 14 days after written notice;

(c) the Licensee is wound up, has a controller or administrator appointed, or is unable to pay its debts as they fall due;

(d) the Licensee ceases to trade from the Licensed Area for 7 consecutive days without the Licensor's written consent;

(e) the Licensee gives the Licensor a turnover statement which is materially false; or

(f) the Guarantor dies or becomes bankrupt and a replacement guarantor acceptable to the Licensor is not provided within 30 days.

### 12.2 Essential terms

Clauses 4.1 (licence fee), 5.4 and 5.5 (turnover reporting), 6.1 (obligation to trade), 7.1 and 7.2 (use, and no plant or cleaning on site), 10.1 (insurance) and 11.1 (assignment) are essential terms, and breach of an essential term is a repudiation of this agreement.

### 12.3 Immediate termination

The Licensor may terminate this agreement immediately by written notice, without any notice to remedy, if the Licensee breaches clause 7.2, if the Licensee's occupation creates an immediate risk to the health or safety of any person in the Centre, or if the Licensee becomes insolvent.

### 12.4 Termination for other default

For any other default the Licensor may terminate this agreement by written notice after the time for remedy in clause 12.1 has passed. On termination the Licensee's right to occupy ends immediately and the Licensee must vacate the Licensed Area in accordance with clause 13.

### 12.5 Damages

Termination does not affect the Licensor's right to recover the Fee accrued to the date of termination, interest under clause 4.5, and damages for the loss of the benefit of this agreement for what would have been the remainder of the Term. The Licensor must take reasonable steps to mitigate its loss.

### 12.6 Licensor may remedy

If the Licensee fails to do anything this agreement requires it to do, the Licensor may, after giving 7 days' written notice or immediately in an emergency, do it, and the reasonable cost is payable by the Licensee on demand.

### 12.7 Termination by the Licensee

The Licensee may terminate this agreement under clause 8.6(e), and may otherwise terminate on 6 months' written notice given at any time after 30 June 2026, in which case the Licensee must pay the Licensor an amount equal to two months' licence fee and promotion levy on the date the termination takes effect.

### 12.8 No waiver

Acceptance of the Fee after a default, or delay in acting on a default, does not waive the default or affect the Licensor's rights.

## 13. End of term and make good

### 13.1 Vacating

On the Expiry date or on earlier termination the Licensee must remove all its garments, stock, records, equipment, counter, back counter, racking, signage and fittings, and give the Licensed Area back to the Licensor clean and free of rubbish.

### 13.2 Make good

The Licensee must make good all damage caused by the installation or removal of its fitout, including:

(a) removing the fascia sign and its fixings and making good the fascia to a paint-ready finish;

(b) removing all floor fixings and reinstating the floor covering to the Centre's base building standard;

(c) removing all wall and bulkhead fixings and making good, patched and painted to match;

(d) capping off the hand basin, its waste and its water service at the point directed by the Licensor, by a licensed plumber; and

(e) removing all cabling, power outlets and data outlets installed by the Licensee and terminating them safely.

### 13.3 Customers' garments

The Licensee must return every customer garment held at the Licensed Area before it vacates, and must give the Licensor written confirmation that no customer garment remains in the Centre. The Licensor may dispose of any garment left in the Licensed Area more than 7 days after the Licensee vacates, and the Licensee indemnifies the Licensor against any claim arising from that disposal.

### 13.4 Failure to vacate

If the Licensee does not vacate and make good by the Expiry date or by the date of termination, the Licensee must pay the Licensor an occupation fee of double the daily licence fee for each day it remains, and the Licensor may remove and store the Licensee's property at the Licensee's cost, and may treat any property left more than 7 days as abandoned and dispose of it.

### 13.5 No compensation

The Licensee is not entitled to any compensation, and makes no claim, for goodwill, for loss of profits, for the value of its fitout, or for the ending of this agreement in accordance with its terms.

## 14. Retail Leases Act acknowledgement

### 14.1 The parties' position

The parties have entered into this agreement as a licence. The Licensor's position, which the Licensee acknowledges it has had the opportunity to obtain advice about, is that a licence of this kind, granted over a small serviced position within a shopping centre without exclusive possession and subject to the relocation right in clause 8.6, is not a retail premises lease and that the Retail Leases Act does not apply to it.

### 14.2 If the Act applies

If it is determined that the Retail Leases Act applies to this agreement, then:

(a) this agreement is read subject to the Act, and any provision inconsistent with the Act is read down to the extent of the inconsistency or, if it cannot be read down, severed, without affecting the rest of this agreement;

(b) the Licensee is not liable for land tax or any amount on account of land tax;

(c) the relocation provisions in clause 8.6 operate subject to section 39 of the Act, and the notice period and compensation are those required by that section if greater than those in clause 8.6;

(d) the provisions of clause 11.3 operate subject to sections 60 to 64 of the Act; and

(e) the Licensor must not recover from the Licensee its costs of preparing, negotiating or executing this agreement.

### 14.3 Disclosure statement given without admission

The Licensor gave the Licensee a document in the form of a disclosure statement under the Retail Leases Act on 24 May 2024, and a copy of this agreement on the same day. The Licensor did so as a matter of prudence and without admitting that the Act applies. The Licensee acknowledges receiving both documents at least 14 days before signing this agreement.

### 14.4 Dispute resolution

Whether or not the Retail Leases Act applies, either party may refer a dispute under this agreement to the Victorian Small Business Commission for mediation, and the parties must participate in that mediation in good faith before commencing proceedings, other than proceedings for urgent injunctive relief or for the recovery of a liquidated amount.

### 14.5 No representation about turnover

The Licensor has not made and does not make any representation about the turnover, profitability or customer numbers that the Licensee may achieve at the Licensed Area, about the Centre's trading performance, about the tenancy mix of the Centre, or about the continued occupation of the Centre by any other occupant. The Licensee acknowledges that it has relied on its own enquiries.

## 15. Security and guarantee

### 15.1 Bank guarantee

The Licensee must, before it first occupies the Licensed Area, give the Licensor an unconditional and irrevocable bank guarantee for the amount in Item 20, issued by an authorised deposit-taking institution, in favour of the Licensor, with no expiry date or with an expiry date not earlier than 6 months after the Expiry date.

### 15.2 Call on the guarantee

The Licensor may call on the bank guarantee for any Fee owing, any interest, any liquidated damages under clause 6.4, any cost of remedying a breach, and any cost of make good under clause 13. The Licensee must restore the guarantee to its full amount within 14 days.

### 15.3 Return

The Licensor must return the bank guarantee to the Licensee within 30 days after the later of the end of the Term, the Licensee vacating and completing make good, the annual certified statement for the final accounting year being given, and all amounts owing being paid.

### 15.4 Guarantee and indemnity

The Guarantor guarantees to the Licensor the payment of the Fee and the performance of the Licensee's obligations under this agreement, and indemnifies the Licensor against loss arising from the Licensee's failure to pay or perform. The Guarantor's liability is that of a principal debtor, is not affected by any indulgence given to the Licensee, by any variation of this agreement, by the relocation of the Licensed Area, or by the Licensor's release of any security, and continues during any period of holding over.

## 16. Notices, GST and general

### 16.1 Notices

A notice under this agreement must be in writing and may be given by hand, by prepaid post to the address in Item 25 or Item 26, or by email to the address in Item 25 or Item 26. A notice is taken to be received: if delivered by hand, on delivery; if posted, on the third business day after posting; if emailed, at the time the email enters the recipient's information system, unless the sender receives an automated notice of non-delivery. A party may change its address by notice.

### 16.2 GST

All amounts payable under this agreement are exclusive of GST. If GST is payable on a taxable supply made under this agreement, the recipient must pay the supplier the GST at the same time as the consideration, on receipt of a valid tax invoice. Where a party must reimburse another party for an expense, the amount reimbursed is the expense less any input tax credit available.

### 16.3 Costs

Each party bears its own costs of negotiating and preparing this agreement. The Licensee must pay the Licensor's reasonable costs of any consent or variation it requests, and any stamp duty assessed on this agreement.

### 16.4 Entire agreement

This agreement records the entire agreement between the parties about the Licensed Area and supersedes all earlier agreements, representations and understandings. A variation must be in writing and signed by both parties.

### 16.5 Governing law

This agreement is governed by the law of Victoria and the parties submit to the jurisdiction of the courts and tribunals of Victoria.

### 16.6 Severance

If a provision of this agreement is void or unenforceable it is severed and the rest of this agreement continues in force.

### 16.7 Counterparts

This agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, and all counterparts together form one agreement.

## ANNEXURE A — PLAN OF THE LICENSED AREA

Shop 12 is on the ground floor of the Centre, on the northern mall alignment between the western travelator and the amenities corridor. The Licensed Area is 24 m², being 6.0 m along the mall alignment by 4.0 m deep, bounded by the licence line marked on the Centre's tenancy plan dated 3 May 2024. The Licensed Area comprises the counter and counter return on the mall alignment, the back counter, three double-sided garment rails to the rear wall with a nominal capacity of 220 garments, a hand basin and cupboard in the north-east corner, and the fascia above the mall alignment. Nothing may be placed forward of the licence line at any time.

## ANNEXURE B — CENTRE RULES

1. Trading. Trade only during your approved hours. The counter must be attended whenever the shop is open.

2. Presentation. Keep the counter, racking and fascia clean and in good order. No handwritten signs. No stock, racks or bins forward of the licence line.

3. Staff. Staff must wear the approved uniform and a name badge, must not eat, drink or use a mobile telephone at the counter, and must park in the staff parking area at the southern end of the car park.

4. Deliveries. All deliveries and collections through the service corridor and loading dock only, before 9:00 am or after 5:30 pm, other than by written approval of the Centre Manager. No garment trolleys through the mall during centre trading hours. Trolleys must be covered.

5. Waste. All waste to the compactor at the loading dock between 8:00 am and 9:00 am or between 5:30 pm and 6:00 pm. Cardboard flattened. No waste from any other premises may be brought into the Centre.

6. Noise and odour. No amplified music, bells or public address devices. Garments must not give off solvent odour.

7. Services. No connection to any water, drainage or gas service. No appliance may be connected to the hand basin. No portable heater, hot plate, kettle, iron or steam appliance other than the approved hand steamer.

8. Safety. Keep the fire exits, the service corridor and the sprinkler and detector heads clear. Report every incident, injury and spill to the Centre Management Office on the day it occurs. Complete the Centre's contractor induction before any contractor works on site.

9. Security. Lock the Licensed Area and secure the racking at close of trade. Keys and after-hours contact details for at least two people must be lodged with the Centre Management Office and kept current.

10. Promotions. Take part in the Centre's promotional activities as reasonably requested. Do not distribute leaflets in the mall or the car park without the Centre Manager's written approval.

11. Trading disputes. Direct any complaint about another occupant to the Centre Management Office and not to that occupant.

12. Reporting. Lodge the monthly turnover statement by the 7th of each month through the Centre's occupant portal or by email to the Centre Manager.

## ANNEXURE C — MONTHLY TURNOVER STATEMENT

To be given to the Centre Manager by the 7th day of each month.

# PART B — POLICY WORDING

This Part sets out the operative cover. Where a defined term is used it appears in the
Definitions at the end of B10. The Schedule at Part A prevails over this Part where the
two conflict.

## B1. Section 1 — Property / Material Damage

### 1.1 What is insured

Meridian will pay for physical loss of or damage to the insured property at the situations
shown in the Schedule occurring during the period of cover and caused by a peril not
excluded. Cover is on an accidental damage basis: the insured does not have to identify a
named peril, but does have to show that an identified event caused the damage.

### 1.2 Insured property

- **Landlord's fixtures and tenant's improvements** — the fitout, partitions, floor
  coverings, ceilings, lighting, shopfront joinery, plumbing and services installed by or
  at the cost of the insured, and the landlord's fixtures for which the insured is
  responsible under the lease. The interest of the landlord is noted; the landlord insures
  the building structure itself and the insured does not.
- **Plant and machinery** as itemised at A8. Each item is separately insured for the sum
  shown against it. A sum insured against one item is not available to make up a shortfall
  against another item.
- **Contents**, being the fitout, furniture, fittings, racking, conveyors not itemised,
  office and point of sale equipment.
- **Stock and materials** at the cost of replacement to the insured, without allowance for
  profit. Solvent held in the bunded store is stock.

### 1.3 Basis of settlement

Insured property is settled on a reinstatement basis: the cost of replacing or repairing
the property with property of the same kind, capacity and specification, without deduction
for depreciation. Where the insured does not proceed to reinstate, settlement is on an
indemnity basis, being replacement cost less an allowance for age, wear and condition.

Where an item of plant is no longer manufactured, Meridian will settle on the cost of the
nearest equivalent current model of the same capacity and specification, and will not pay
for a capacity or specification upgrade beyond that. Where a machine can be economically
repaired it will be repaired; a machine is a total loss only where the cost of repair
exceeds its replacement cost, or where the manufacturer's authorised agent certifies that
it cannot be returned to a safe and serviceable condition.

Reinstatement must be commenced with reasonable despatch and completed within 12 months of
the date of damage, or such further period as Meridian allows in writing.

### 1.4 Removal of debris

Meridian will pay the reasonable cost of removing, storing and lawfully disposing of
debris, dismantling damaged property, and cleaning up drains, pits and the trade waste
connection within the situation, up to $50,000. Where debris is contaminated with solvent
or solvent residue, disposal must be through a lawfully permissioned waste contractor, and
the cost of that disposal is included within this limit. This benefit does not extend to
the cost of removing or remediating contaminated soil or groundwater.

### 1.5 Extra cost of reinstatement

Where the insured is required by a statutory authority, a building regulation or the terms
of the lease to reinstate to a standard higher than the standard that existed before the
damage, Meridian will pay the additional cost, up to 20% of the amount otherwise payable
and not more than $100,000. This benefit does not apply to a requirement notified to the
insured before the damage occurred, and does not apply to any part of the property that
was not damaged.

By way of example, where a damaged boiler flue must on replacement be relocated or
re-sized to meet a current standard, the additional cost of doing so falls within this
benefit; where the boiler was already the subject of a written direction to alter the flue
before the damage, it does not.

### 1.6 Average / co-insurance

**This is the condition that most often reduces a property claim, so read it.**

If at the time of loss the actual replacement value of the insured property in a category
exceeds the sum insured shown for that category, the insured is treated as its own insurer
for the difference and bears a rateable proportion of the loss. Where the sum insured is
at least 90% of the actual replacement value, no reduction is applied.

Worked example. If the press line at item P5 is insured for $96,000 and its actual
replacement cost at the time of loss is $120,000, the sum insured is 80% of value, which
is below the 90% threshold. A $40,000 partial loss would be settled at
$40,000 x 96,000 / 120,000 = $32,000, less the excess of $2,500, so $29,500.

Average is applied item by item for itemised plant and category by category for contents
and stock. It applies to a partial loss as well as to a total loss, and it is the partial
loss where it bites hardest, because the insured is often unaware that the sum insured has
fallen behind replacement cost until the claim is assessed.

The insured should review each sum insured before each renewal, after any plant purchase
or replacement, and after any material change in the cost of imported equipment or the
exchange rate. Meridian will accept a written valuation from the manufacturer's authorised
agent as evidence of replacement cost.

documents.text:
### 1.7 Section 1 exclusions

Meridian does not cover under this Section:

1. wear, tear, gradual deterioration, rust, corrosion, mould, damp, dry rot, or the action
   of light, vermin or insects;
2. faulty workmanship or faulty materials, other than resulting damage to other property;
3. mechanical or electrical breakdown, which is dealt with under Section 5;
4. damage to a machine caused by its own operation on the goods within it, including
   damage caused by a foreign object left in a garment;
5. theft not accompanied by forcible and violent entry to or exit from a building, except
   theft by an identified person lawfully on the premises;
6. damage to customers' goods, which is dealt with under Section 4;
7. loss of solvent by evaporation, leakage or absence not attributable to an identified
   event, and any inventory shortfall of solvent;
8. damage to plant while it is being installed, dismantled or relocated by anyone other
   than the manufacturer's authorised service agent;
9. damage to electrical equipment by electrical current, arcing or self-heating, other
   than resulting fire damage to other property;
10. settling, shrinkage or expansion of buildings or foundations; and
11. the cost of repairing a defect that caused escaping water, though the resulting water
    damage is covered.

## B2. Section 2 — Business Interruption

### 2.1 What is insured

Where the insured suffers damage that is covered under Section 1 or Section 5, Meridian
will pay the resulting loss of gross profit and the increased cost of working during the
indemnity period. Cover under this Section depends on a claim being payable under Section
1 or Section 5; if the property claim fails, the interruption claim fails with it.

### 2.2 Sum insured and indemnity period

Gross profit sum insured $420,000. Indemnity period 12 months, commencing on the date the
damage occurs. Gross profit is turnover less the cost of solvent, chemistry, consumables,
packaging and outsourced processing. Wages of all employees are included within gross
profit and are not separately insured.

The 12 month indemnity period is chosen deliberately. A total loss of the Bendigo plant
would require the tenancy to be made good by the landlord, new plant to be ordered from
overseas, a boiler to be installed, commissioned and registered as plant, and the customer
base to be rebuilt. Twelve months is the period over which the insured's earnings would
reasonably be expected to be affected, and it is not a period during which the loss must
be resolved.

### 2.3 Additional increased cost of working

In addition to the increased cost of working recoverable under 2.1, Meridian will pay up
to $100,000 for additional expenditure reasonably and necessarily incurred to avoid or
reduce a reduction in turnover, whether or not that expenditure is recovered by the
resulting saving. This is the benefit that pays for outsourcing work to another plant,
hiring a mobile boiler, air freighting a replacement component, or paying overtime to
clear a backlog.

The economic limit test that applies to ordinary increased cost of working — that
expenditure is recoverable only up to the loss it saves — does not apply to this benefit.

### 2.4 The dry cleaner's exposure — boiler and machine outage

The insured's plant has two single points of failure: the steam boiler, on which every
press, finisher, still and the shirt unit depends, and the dry cleaning machines.

**The boiler.** Where the Fulton FB-030 suffers damage covered under Section 1 or a
breakdown covered under Section 5, the whole finishing line stops. Garments can still be
cleaned but cannot be finished, and the plant cannot deliver. Meridian records that in
that circumstance the insured may, without further authority, incur additional increased
cost of working under 2.3 for:

- the hire, delivery, connection, fuelling and removal of a temporary packaged steam
  boiler, for up to 60 days;
- the temporary gas or fuel connection and any temporary flue required for it;
- the outsourcing of pressing and finishing to another plant, including the cost of
  transporting garments to and from that plant; and
- overtime and additional casual labour to clear the resulting backlog.

The insured must notify Meridian within 48 hours of committing to hire. Where the boiler
is out of service for more than 14 days, Meridian will meet with the insured and the
broker to agree a plan for the balance of the indemnity period.

**The dry cleaning machines.** Where the Union XL-800 is out of service and the Realstar
HM-450 remains serviceable, or the reverse, the loss is assessed on the reduced throughput
actually achievable on the surviving machine, and not on a total cessation. The insured is
expected to reschedule work onto the surviving machine, and to advise customers of
extended turnaround, before outsourcing. Where the fabric or trim of a garment makes the
surviving machine unsuitable, outsourcing that garment is reasonable and is recoverable.

**The Kangaroo Flat drop store.** Damage at Situation 1 that stops production also stops
the earnings of Situation 2, because Situation 2 has no plant. Loss of turnover at
Situation 2 arising from damage at Situation 1 is recoverable under this Section.

### 2.5 Other benefits under this Section

- **Claims preparation costs** — the reasonable professional fees of an accountant or loss
  consultant engaged by the insured to prepare and substantiate a claim, up to $25,000.
  Fees payable on a contingency or percentage of settlement basis are not covered.
- **Prevention of access** — loss following damage to property within 100 m of a situation
  that prevents access to it, up to 12 weeks.
- **Public utilities** — loss following damage at the premises of the supplier of
  electricity, gas or water within 20 km of a situation, excess 24 hours.
- **Customers' and suppliers' premises** — loss following damage at the premises of a
  named customer or supplier, up to $50,000.
- **Loss of attraction** — loss following damage to a property within the same shopping
  centre as Situation 2 that materially reduces customer traffic, up to $25,000.
- **Rewriting of records** — the cost of reconstructing the garment tracking records and
  customer database, up to $15,000.

### 2.6 Time excess

72 hours. No claim is payable under this Section for an interruption that is made good
within 72 hours of the damage occurring. Where an interruption exceeds 72 hours, the loss
is calculated from the date of damage and the 72 hours is not deducted twice.

## B3. Section 3 — Public and Products Liability

Meridian will indemnify the insured against all sums the insured becomes legally liable to
pay as compensation for personal injury or property damage happening during the period of
cover and caused by an occurrence in connection with the business.

**Limit of indemnity: $20,000,000 any one occurrence**, and in the aggregate during any one
period of cover in respect of products liability. Legal defence costs and the costs of an
inquest or inquiry incurred with Meridian's written consent are payable in addition to the
limit.

Cover extends to the insured's liability arising from:

- the pickup and delivery of garments, including work performed at a customer's premises;
- the sale or supply of goods, including hangers, covers and retail products;
- the use and occupation of the situations, including liability to a visitor or contractor;
- the insured's liability assumed under the Bendigo lease and the Kangaroo Flat licence,
  to the extent the liability would have existed without the agreement;
- goods sold or supplied and no longer in the insured's control; and
- the insured's participation in a market, fair or community event.

**Excluded under this Section:** liability for damage to property in the insured's physical
or legal control, which is dealt with under Section 4; liability to an employee arising out
of employment, which is the subject of workers compensation; liability arising from the
ownership or use of a registered vehicle, other than the loading and unloading of it;
liability for the cost of recalling, repairing, replacing or reperforming the insured's own
work or product; liability for pure financial loss unconnected with injury or damage; fines,
penalties, punitive and exemplary damages; liability arising from asbestos; liability
arising from a professional opinion given for a fee; and pollution liability except as
provided by General Exclusion 4.

## B4. Section 4 — Bailee's / Customers' Goods Liability

**This Section is the core of the cover for a dry cleaner. It is the Section under which
most claims are made, and the Section whose conditions the counter staff must know.**

### 4.1 What is insured

Meridian will indemnify the insured for loss of or damage to customers' goods while those
goods are in the insured's physical custody or under the insured's control for the purpose
of cleaning, wet cleaning, laundering, pressing, finishing, alteration, repair, storage or
delivery, and while those goods are:

- at Situation 1;
- at Situation 2;
- in transit between Situation 1 and Situation 2 in the insured's vehicle;
- in transit to or from a customer's address in the insured's vehicle; or
- at the premises of a specialist subcontractor engaged by the insured for leather
  cleaning, wedding gown preservation or curtain cleaning, for up to 30 days.

Cover applies whether or not the insured is legally liable for the loss or damage. This
Section is a first party cover on the goods of others, not a liability cover, and Meridian
will not require the customer to prove negligence. That does not make the policy a
guarantee of the insured's work; the exclusions at 4.3 are what confine it.

Customers' goods held for a customer under a storage or seasonal storage arrangement are
insured, provided the goods have been cleaned before storage and the storage arrangement
is recorded against a docket.

### 4.2 Limits and excess

| Limit | Amount |
|---|---|
| Any one event | $50,000 |
| Any one garment, or any one matched suit or matched set | $25,000 |
| Goods in transit in the insured's vehicle, any one event | $20,000 |
| Goods at a subcontractor's premises, any one event | $15,000 |
| Goods held in seasonal storage, any one event | $20,000 |
| Mysterious disappearance, any one event and in the aggregate in any one period of cover | $5,000 |
| Excess, each and every event | $2,500 |

A matched suit, a two piece or three piece outfit, or a set of curtains from one room is
treated as one garment for the purposes of the inner limit. Where one piece of a matched
set is damaged beyond repair, Meridian will pay for the whole set less an allowance for
the wear of the undamaged pieces, and the undamaged pieces become Meridian's property.

The any one event limit is the practical constraint. A conveyor holding 400 garments has a
replacement value well above $50,000. A fire that destroys the conveyor is one event, and
the most Meridian will pay for the garments on it is $50,000. The insured should
understand this and should not tell a customer otherwise.

### 4.3 What is not insured under this Section

Meridian does not pay for:

1. **Inherent vice** — a defect, weakness or characteristic within the garment itself,
   including latent weakness in fibre, an unstable dye, a fusible interlining that
   delaminates, adhesive failure in beading or trim, a deteriorated leather finish, a
   coated or bonded fabric that separates, or a fabric weakened by perspiration,
   deodorant, sunlight, atmospheric fume or previous cleaning.
2. **Colour change, colour loss, colour bleed or colour migration** occurring through no
   fault of the insured, including where the garment was cleaned by the process indicated
   on the care label, and including dye transfer between components of the same garment.
3. **Wear and tear, gradual deterioration, shrinkage or relaxation** consistent with the
   age and use of the garment, and the ordinary loss of finish, glaze, nap or pleating.
4. **Damage arising from correctly following the care label**, where the label was legible,
   was attached to the garment on intake, and specified the process used. This exclusion
   does not apply if the insured departed from the label, or if the insured knew or should
   reasonably have known that the label was wrong for the fabric and proceeded without an
   at-risk authorisation.
5. **Mysterious disappearance** beyond the $5,000 limit at 4.2 — meaning the loss of a
   garment which cannot be attributed to an identified event, and which is discovered only
   on stocktake, reconciliation or customer enquiry.
6. **Goods left uncollected for more than 3 months** from the date the garment was ready
   for collection, where the insured has given the customer at least one written or SMS
   notice that the garment is ready. After 3 months such goods cease to be insured under
   this Section, whether or not the insured continues to hold them.
7. Damage to buttons, buckles, sequins, beads, trims, zips and fastenings, unless the
   garment itself is also damaged.
8. Loss or damage to money, jewellery, documents, keys, spectacles or valuables left in a
   pocket or attached to a garment.
9. Loss or damage caused by moth, vermin or insects, whether present on intake or not.
10. Loss or damage arising from a process the insured was not equipped or competent to
    perform, including the cleaning of a garment the manufacturer marks as not cleanable.
11. Damage caused by the removal of a stain where the customer was told the stain might
    not respond and authorised the attempt.
12. Consequential loss of any kind, including a customer's claim for the cost of hiring a
    replacement garment, travel costs, loss of use, or distress and inconvenience.
13. Any amount recoverable from a subcontractor, to the extent actually recovered.
14. Loss or damage arising from the insured's failure to return a garment where the
    customer has not paid the cleaning charge and the insured is exercising a lien.

documents.text:
### 4.4 Claims conditions specific to this Section

The following conditions are conditions precedent to Meridian's liability under this
Section. They are not administrative preferences. A claim will be assessed against them.

**(a) Intake records.** The insured must create and retain, for every garment taken into
custody, a record showing the date of intake, the customer's name and contact details, a
description of the garment sufficient to identify it, the process requested, the fabric
and care label content where legible, and any pre-existing damage, staining, missing
button or wear noted at the counter. A docket number must be assigned and must be
traceable through the plant to the point of collection.

A description is sufficient if a person who has never seen the garment could pick it from
a rack of similar garments. "Navy wool two-button suit jacket, Zegna label, small ink mark
left cuff" is sufficient. "Suit jacket" is not.

**(b) At-risk authorisations.** Where the insured accepts a garment that is unlabelled,
carries an illegible or implausible label, is trimmed or embellished, is leather or suede,
is a wedding gown, is a vintage or heirloom item, has visible pre-existing damage, or
carries a stain that may not respond, the insured must obtain the customer's authorisation
to proceed at the customer's risk **before** processing. The authorisation must be in
writing or captured electronically, must identify the docket number and the garment, and
must state what the risk is. A verbal authorisation not recorded against the docket is not
an authorisation for the purposes of this condition.

A generic disclaimer printed on the back of the docket is not an at-risk authorisation. It
does not identify the garment, it does not state the risk, and it will not be treated as
one.

**(c) Retention.** Intake records and at-risk authorisations must be retained for not less
than 24 months and must be produced to Meridian on request. Where the insured cannot
produce the intake record for a garment that is the subject of a claim, Meridian may
decline the claim or may settle on the depreciated value of a garment of that general
description, at Meridian's election.

**(d) Reconciliation.** The insured must reconcile garments on the conveyor against open
dockets at least monthly and must record the result, including the number of unmatched
garments and the number of open dockets with no garment against them. A mysterious
disappearance claim will not be considered unless the reconciliation records for the three
months preceding the claim are produced.

**(e) Security and custody.** Garments must be held inside the locked premises outside
trading hours. Garments in the delivery vehicle must not be left in an unattended vehicle
overnight, and the vehicle must be locked when unattended. Garments awaiting collection at
Situation 2 must be behind the counter and not accessible to the public.

**(f) Subcontractors.** Where the insured sends goods to a subcontractor, the insured must
record the consignment, the garments in it, and the date sent and returned. The insured
must not send goods to a subcontractor who has not confirmed in writing that it holds
bailee's cover for goods in its custody.

**(g) Complaint register.** Every customer complaint about the condition of a garment must
be recorded on the day it is made, with the docket number, the complaint, and the action
taken. The register is the first document Meridian asks for when a claim is disputed.

### 4.5 Basis of settlement and disputed value

Settlement is on the basis of the **actual cash value** of the garment at the date of loss,
being the cost of replacing it with a garment of like kind and quality, less a fair
allowance for age, wear and fashion obsolescence. Meridian uses a published garment
depreciation schedule. As a guide:

| Garment | Depreciation | Residual floor |
|---|---|---|
| Wool suit or jacket | 20% per year of age | 20% of replacement cost |
| Business shirt | 33% per year | 10% |
| Formal or bridal gown | 15% per year | 25% |
| Leather or suede garment | 12.5% per year | 20% |
| Overcoat | 15% per year | 20% |
| Household curtains and drapes | 10% per year | 15% |
| Household linen, blankets, doonas | 20% per year | 10% |

**Where the customer's claimed value is disputed.** If the customer asserts a value that
the insured or Meridian does not accept, the following applies:

1. The customer is asked to produce proof of purchase, a bank or card statement, an
   insurance valuation or a retailer's written quotation for a like garment.
2. Where no proof is produced, Meridian will assess replacement cost from the brand, fibre
   content, construction and condition of the garment as recorded on intake, and from
   current retail pricing for a comparable garment.
3. Meridian will not accept a claimed value for a garment described on intake only as, for
   example, "jacket" or "dress", beyond the assessed value of a garment of that general
   description. **The specificity of the intake record is what protects the insured here.**
4. Where the parties remain apart, Meridian may appoint an independent textile assessor at
   Meridian's cost. The assessor's report is not binding on the customer, but Meridian's
   liability is limited to the assessed amount.
5. Meridian will not pay a claim for sentimental value, and will not pay for a garment on
   the basis of its original purchase price where that price is more than five years old,
   except on production of a current valuation.
6. Where a garment is repairable, Meridian will pay the cost of repair rather than
   replacement, provided the repair restores the garment to a saleable condition. Where a
   repair is possible but the customer refuses it, Meridian's liability is limited to the
   cost of the repair.

The insured must not admit liability, agree a value, offer a credit above $250, or settle
a customer complaint that may become a claim, without Meridian's written consent. A
goodwill re-clean, or a refund of the cleaning charge alone, is not an admission and does
not require consent.

### 4.6 How a bailee's claim is handled in practice

1. The customer complains. The complaint is recorded in the register on the day, with the
   docket number and the customer's description of the problem.
2. The garment is retained. It is bagged, tagged with the docket number, and put aside. It
   is not returned to the customer and it is not re-cleaned.
3. The intake docket, the at-risk authorisation if any, and the production record are
   pulled and copied.
4. The claim is notified to the broker within 30 days, with those documents and
   photographs of the garment.
5. Meridian assesses. Where liability and value are clear and the amount is under $5,000,
   Meridian settles on the documents. Otherwise a textile assessor is appointed.
6. Meridian pays the insured, less the $2,500 excess. The insured settles with the
   customer. Because the excess is $2,500, a claim for a single garment worth less than
   that is not worth notifying as a claim, though it should still be recorded in the
   register in case it forms part of a larger event.

## B5. Section 5 — Machinery Breakdown

Meridian will pay for sudden and unforeseen physical damage to the scheduled machinery
arising from mechanical or electrical breakdown, necessitating repair or replacement, up
to $250,000 any one breakdown, excess $1,000.

**Scheduled machinery**

| Item | Machine | Insured value |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Fulton FB-030 vertical gas fired steam boiler, 30 hp, MAWP 690 kPa, registration VIC-PV-118-4470, including burner, gas train, feedwater pump, level controls, gauge glass and safety valve | $48,000 |
| M2 | Union XL-800 dry cleaning machine including still, refrigerated recovery circuit, cage drive, solvent pumps and button trap | $185,000 |
| M3 | Realstar HM-450 dry cleaning machine including still and recovery circuit | $142,000 |
| M4 | Pilot K25 rotary screw air compressor, refrigerated dryer and 500 L receiver | $22,000 |

**Extensions.** Deterioration of stock following breakdown of refrigeration or of the
solvent recovery circuit, $10,000. Hire of substitute plant, $20,000. Expediting expenses
including overtime and express freight, $15,000. Damage to surrounding property caused by
the breakdown, $25,000.

**Conditions.** The boiler must be maintained and inspected in accordance with the
applicable Australian Standards and the plant registration held for it, and the current
inspection report must be produced to Meridian on request. Cover is excluded for damage
arising from operating the boiler with a defect that a competent person has notified in
writing and that remains unrectified beyond the date required by that notice. Cover is
also excluded for gradual scaling, corrosion, erosion or fatigue; for the cost of routine
overhaul or of a repair that was due in any event; for damage caused by operating the
boiler on untreated or incorrectly treated feedwater; and for damage to a wear part in the
course of ordinary use, including gaskets, seals, packing, filters, belts, refractory,
electrodes and gauge glass. Where a wear part fails and causes damage to other parts of
the machine, that resulting damage is covered.

## B6. Section 6 — Glass

Meridian will pay for the breakage of internal and external glass, mirrors, showcases and
counters at the situations, and for the cost of temporary boarding, removal of
obstructions, and the replacement of alarm foil, lettering and applied signage up to
$10,000. Excess $250. Cover excludes scratching or chipping without a full breakage, glass
already cracked at inception, and breakage during installation or removal.

## B7. Section 7 — Money

Meridian will pay for the loss of money belonging to the insured or for which the insured
is responsible: $10,000 while in transit or in the personal custody of the insured or an
employee; $5,000 while on the premises during business hours; $5,000 while in a locked
safe outside business hours; and $1,000 while on the premises outside business hours and
not in a locked safe. Damage to a safe, till or strongroom caused by theft or attempted
theft is included up to $5,000. Excess $250. Cover excludes shortage due to error or
omission, loss from an unattended vehicle, and loss arising from the acceptance of
counterfeit currency or a dishonoured payment instrument.

## B8. Section 8 — Employee Dishonesty

Meridian will pay for the loss of money or goods belonging to the insured caused by the
fraud or dishonesty of an employee, discovered during the period of cover or within 12
months after it ends, up to $50,000 any one event and in the aggregate. Excess $1,000.
Cover is conditional on the insured performing a bank reconciliation at least monthly and
on takings being banked at least weekly. Cover excludes loss discovered more than 12
months after the employee left, loss that cannot be established other than by inventory
computation or profit and loss computation alone, and any loss arising from the conduct of
a director of the named insured.

## B9. Section 9 — Tax Audit

Meridian will pay the reasonable professional fees of an accountant, tax agent or
solicitor incurred with Meridian's consent in responding to an official audit or
investigation of the insured's returns, up to $20,000 any one period of cover, excess
$500. Cover extends to an audit of income tax, GST, PAYG, fringe benefits tax, payroll tax
and superannuation guarantee obligations. Cover excludes fees for the original preparation
of a return, fees arising from a return lodged late, any tax, penalty, fine or interest,
and any audit arising from a matter the insured knew of before the period of cover began.

## B10. General conditions and exclusions

### GE1. General exclusions

This policy does not cover loss, damage, liability or expense arising from war, invasion,
civil commotion or the act of a lawfully constituted authority; from nuclear or
radioactive contamination; from an act of terrorism, except to the extent the Terrorism
Insurance Act 2003 (Cth) applies; from a cyber act, a computer virus or the failure of
electronic data, except resulting physical damage by fire or explosion; from asbestos;
from the deliberate or reckless act of the insured; from communicable disease; or from
confiscation, nationalisation or lawful seizure.

### GE2. Wear, tear and gradual causes

This policy does not cover the cost of maintenance, wear and tear, gradual deterioration,
inherent defect, latent defect, or damage that develops over time rather than from an
identified event. This exclusion does not apply to resulting physical damage that is
otherwise insured.

### GE3. Faulty design and workmanship

This policy does not cover the cost of correcting faulty design, faulty materials or
faulty workmanship, but does cover resulting damage to other property.

### GE4. Pollution and contamination — with a dry cleaning carve-back

**Excluded.** This policy does not cover loss, damage, liability, clean-up cost,
remediation cost, fine, penalty or expense of any kind arising directly or indirectly out
of the discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release or escape of pollutants or
contaminants, including perchloroethylene, hydrocarbon solvent, solvent residue, separator
water, still bottoms, spent filter cartridges, spent carbon, or any prescribed industrial
waste, into or upon land, the atmosphere, a watercourse, a drain, a sewer or any body of
water.

**Carve-back.** GE4 does **not** exclude loss, damage or liability arising from an escape
of solvent that is **sudden, identifiable, unintended and unexpected**, that commences at
an identifiable time during the period of cover, that is discovered by the insured within
**7 days** of commencing and notified to Meridian in writing within **30 days** of
discovery. Where the carve-back applies, Meridian will pay:

- physical damage to insured property at the situation caused by the escape;
- the cost of cleaning up the escaped solvent within the boundaries of the situation,
  including the removal and lawful disposal of contaminated material through a
  permissioned contractor;
- the cost of emergency response, including the attendance of a hazardous materials
  contractor and the ventilation and testing of the premises;
- the insured's legal liability for damage to third party property or for personal injury
  caused by the escape, within the Section 3 limit; and
- resulting business interruption within the Section 2 limit,

subject to a **sub-limit of $250,000** in the aggregate in any one period of cover, and
the standard excess.

The carve-back does not apply to: an escape that is gradual, repeated or continuing; an
escape from the drainage system, the trade waste connection or a sewer; contamination of
soil or groundwater beneath the situation existing before the period of cover; an escape
while the plant was being operated in breach of a statutory requirement or with a defect
notified in writing by a competent person and unrectified; an escape during the delivery
of solvent by a supplier, which is the supplier's liability; or any cost of remediating
land or groundwater outside the boundaries of the situation.

An example of the carve-back operating: a solvent line to the still fails while the
machine is running, perchloroethylene is released onto the plant floor and into the bund,
the insured discovers it the same day, contains it, engages a permissioned contractor and
notifies Meridian within the week. The clean-up, the damage to the floor covering and to
adjoining stock, and the interruption while the plant is ventilated and tested, are
covered within the sub-limit.

An example of the carve-back not operating: a slow weep from a separator over many months
saturates the slab beneath the machine and is found during a plant upgrade. That is
gradual, it is not discovered within 7 days of commencing, and it is excluded.
