documents.text:
### GC1. Statutory obligations — boiler and solvent store

The insured must comply, and must continue to comply, with every statutory obligation,
licence condition, permission and registration applying to the operation of the business,
and in particular:

**(a) The boiler.** The Fulton FB-030 must be registered as plant, the registration must
be current, and the boiler must be inspected by a competent person at the intervals
required by that registration and the applicable Australian Standards. Records of
inspection, safety valve testing, water treatment and daily operational logs must be kept
and produced on request. A defect identified in an inspection report must be rectified by
the date the report requires. The boiler must be operated only by a person holding the
required licence or competency, and the attendance regime recorded in the inspection
report must be maintained.

**(b) The solvent store.** Solvent must be stored in the bunded store, the bund must be
maintained impervious and free of standing water and stored product, the quantity stored
must not exceed two 200 L drums, and spill response materials must be available and
serviceable. Prescribed industrial waste must be removed only by a lawfully permissioned
transporter under a compliant tracking arrangement, and the records of removal must be
retained.

**(c) The dry cleaning plant.** The dry cleaning machines must be maintained in accordance
with the manufacturer's instructions and must not be operated with a disabled interlock,
vapour seal, carbon adsorber or refrigerated recovery circuit. Where the manufacturer's
manual specifies a maintenance interval, that interval must be kept and the work recorded.

Breach of GC1 that is causally connected to a loss entitles Meridian to reduce its
liability to the extent it has been prejudiced, and in the case of a breach that
materially increased the risk of the loss, to decline the claim. Breach of GC1 that is not
connected to the loss does not of itself defeat a claim.

### GC2. Unoccupancy

If a situation is left unoccupied for more than **60 consecutive days**, cover under
Sections 1, 4, 6, 7 and 8 at that situation is suspended from the 61st day unless Meridian
has agreed in writing to continue it, and Meridian may impose conditions and an additional
premium. While unoccupied, the insured must maintain the alarm and its monitoring, keep
the premises secured, turn off the gas and water at the mains except to any service
required for fire protection, remove all money, remove all customers' goods, and inspect
the premises at least weekly and record the inspection. For the purposes of this condition,
a situation closed for a period of ordinary holiday closure of not more than 21 days is not
unoccupied.

### GC3. Reasonable care and risk management

The insured must take all reasonable precautions to prevent loss, damage and injury,
maintain the property in sound condition, comply with the manufacturer's maintenance
schedule for each item of scheduled plant, and remedy a defect or danger as soon as
practicable after becoming aware of it. Failure to take a precaution is a breach of this
condition only where the insured was reckless as to the consequences.

### GC4. Alteration of risk

The insured must tell Meridian, through the broker, as soon as reasonably practicable if
the business changes in a way that materially alters the risk, including a change of
solvent type, the installation or removal of scheduled plant, a change of occupancy at a
situation, the addition or closure of a site, a change in the alarm or its monitoring, the
commencement of a process not described at A3, or the entry into a contract that assumes a
liability beyond the ordinary.

### GC5. Claims notification and time limits

The insured must:

- notify Meridian, or the broker, of any loss, damage or occurrence that may give rise to
  a claim **as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event within 30 days** of
  becoming aware of it;
- notify the police immediately in the case of theft, malicious damage or a missing
  garment believed stolen, and obtain a report number;
- not incur expense in connection with a claim, other than reasonable emergency expense to
  prevent further loss, without Meridian's consent;
- forward every writ, summons, demand or letter of claim to Meridian unanswered,
  immediately on receipt;
- not admit liability, negotiate or settle any claim without Meridian's consent; and
- take all reasonable steps to preserve the damaged property and not dispose of it until
  Meridian has had a reasonable opportunity to inspect it.

Late notification does not of itself defeat a claim, but Meridian may reduce its liability
by the amount of prejudice caused by the delay. Where a garment has been returned to the
customer or disposed of before Meridian could inspect it, the prejudice is usually
substantial.

### GC6. Subrogation

Meridian is entitled, after paying a claim, to exercise in the insured's name every right
of recovery the insured has against a third party. The insured must do everything
reasonably required to enable that recovery and must not, without Meridian's consent,
enter into an agreement that limits or excludes the liability of a third party in a way
that prejudices that right. Amounts recovered are applied first to Meridian's outlay, then
to the insured's uninsured loss including the excess. Meridian will not exercise rights of
recovery against an employee of the insured except where the loss arose from that
employee's fraud or wilful misconduct.

### GC7. Cancellation

The insured may cancel at any time by written notice, and Meridian will refund the
unearned premium on a pro rata basis less any non-refundable levy or duty and less the
broker's fee. Meridian may cancel only in the circumstances permitted by section 60 of the
Insurance Contracts Act 1984 (Cth), by giving three business days' written notice to the
insured's last known address, and will give the same notice to any party whose interest is
noted at A5.

### GC8. Duty of disclosure

Before entering into, renewing, varying, extending or reinstating this policy, the insured
has a duty under the Insurance Contracts Act 1984 (Cth) to take reasonable care not to
make a misrepresentation to Meridian. The insured must answer Meridian's questions
honestly and to the best of its knowledge, and must tell Meridian about anything it knows,
or a reasonable person in the circumstances could be expected to know, that is relevant to
Meridian's decision to insure and on what terms. The duty applies to every person insured,
and to the broker acting on the insured's behalf.

Matters relevant to this business include a prior claim or loss whether insured or not, a
notice or direction from a regulator, an unrectified defect in scheduled plant, a change
in the solvent used, an insolvency event, and a criminal conviction of a director for an
offence of dishonesty.

If the duty is not complied with, Meridian may reduce its liability, cancel the policy,
or, in the case of fraudulent misrepresentation, treat the policy as if it never existed.

### GC9. Other insurance, GST and jurisdiction

The insured must tell Meridian of any other policy covering the same loss. Where another
policy covers the same loss, Meridian will pay only its rateable proportion. Where the
insured is registered for GST, claim payments are reduced by the input tax credit the
insured is entitled to claim, and the insured must advise its input tax credit entitlement
when claiming. This policy is governed by the law of Victoria and the parties submit to
the jurisdiction of its courts.

### GC10. Complaints

A complaint should be made first to the broker or to Meridian's Internal Dispute
Resolution team at complaints@meridianunderwriting.com.au or on 1300 663 004. Meridian
will acknowledge a complaint within 1 business day and respond within 30 calendar days. If
the complaint is not resolved within 30 days, or the insured is not satisfied with the
response, the insured may refer it to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority.

### GC11. Premium payment

If the premium is not paid within 30 days of the due date, Meridian may cancel the policy
in accordance with GC7. Where premium funding is used, the funder's notice of cancellation
authority operates in addition to this condition, and cancellation by the funder for
non-payment of an instalment cancels this policy from the date stated in the funder's
notice.

### GC12. Definitions

**Customers' goods** — garments, textiles and household items belonging to a person other
than the insured, accepted by the insured in the ordinary course of the business.

**Damage** — sudden and accidental physical loss or destruction of, or physical damage to,
tangible property.

**Event** — one occurrence or series of occurrences arising from one originating cause.
All garments lost or damaged in one fire, one theft, one vehicle incident or one machine
malfunction constitute one event.

**Excess** — the first amount of each claim borne by the insured. Where more than one
Section responds to one event, only the highest single excess applies.

**Garment** — one item of clothing or one item of household textile. A matched suit or set
is one garment.

**Mysterious disappearance** — the loss of property that cannot be attributed to an
identified event and where no evidence of theft, misdelivery or destruction exists.

**Occurrence** — an event, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the
same general conditions, which results in personal injury or property damage neither
expected nor intended by the insured.

**Situation** — a location described at A4.

---

# PART C — MAKING A CLAIM

## C1. What to do first

1. **Make the site safe.** Isolate the machine, shut the gas at the boiler, or secure the
   premises, as the case requires. Do not restart plant that has failed.
2. **Prevent further loss.** Move garments away from water. Cover stock. Board glass.
   Reasonable emergency expense is covered.
3. **Do not throw anything away.** Meridian or its assessor needs to see the damaged
   garment, the failed component or the broken glass. A garment that has been disposed of,
   or a component that has been scrapped by a repairer, will usually be settled at a
   reduced amount or not at all.
4. **Report to the police** where theft, malicious damage or a suspected stolen garment is
   involved, and obtain a report number.
5. **Call the broker on (03) 5442 6180**, or Meridian on 1300 663 004. Claims may be
   lodged 24 hours a day.

## C2. What Meridian needs, by Section

**Property or machinery breakdown (Sections 1 and 5)** — the date, time and circumstances;
photographs of the damage before anything is moved; the make, model, serial number and age
of the plant; a repairer's report identifying the cause; a quotation to repair or replace;
the most recent service record; and for the boiler, the current inspection report and the
daily log book for the period.

**Business interruption (Section 2)** — the last two years of financial statements;
monthly turnover for the 12 months before the damage; the payroll; invoices for outsourced
processing and plant hire; and a written statement of what was done to reduce the loss.

**Liability (Section 3)** — every document received from the claimant, unanswered; the
incident record; the names of witnesses; and photographs of the scene.

**Glass, money, employee dishonesty, tax audit (Sections 6 to 9)** — for glass, a
glazier's quotation and a photograph; for money, the takings record and the banking
record; for employee dishonesty, the reconciliations, the employment record and the police
report; for tax audit, the notice from the authority and the practitioner's fee estimate.

**Bailee's / customers' goods (Section 4)** — see C3.

## C3. The record-keeping that decides a bailee's claim

A Section 4 claim is assessed on the paperwork. Meridian will ask for:

1. **The intake docket** for the garment, showing the date, the customer, the garment
   description, the process requested, the care label content and any pre-existing damage
   noted at the counter.
2. **The at-risk authorisation**, where one was required under 4.4(b).
3. **The production record** showing which machine, which programme, which operator and
   which date the garment was processed on.
4. **The garment itself**, retained and not returned to the customer until Meridian has
   inspected it or agreed in writing that it need not.
5. **The customer's claim**, in writing, stating what they say happened and what they say
   the garment is worth.
6. **Proof of value** — receipt, statement, valuation or retailer's quotation.
7. **The complaint register entry** made on the day the complaint was received.
8. **The reconciliation records** for the three preceding months, where the claim is for a
   garment that cannot be found.
9. **The subcontractor consignment record**, where the garment was sent out.

**In practice, claims fail for four reasons:** the intake record described the garment too
generally to support the value claimed; no at-risk authorisation was obtained for a
garment that plainly needed one; the garment was returned to the customer or disposed of
before it could be inspected; or the loss is a mysterious disappearance with no
reconciliation records behind it. Each of these is within the insured's control at the
counter, and each of them costs nothing to fix.

## C4. Excess

The excess shown against the responding Section is deducted from each claim payment. Where
one event triggers more than one Section, only the highest single excess applies. The
excess is not payable in advance; it is deducted from settlement. Because the bailee's
excess is $2,500, a single-garment claim below that figure is not economic to notify,
though it should still be recorded in the complaint register in case it later forms part
of a larger event or a pattern.

## C5. Assessment and payment

Meridian will acknowledge a claim within 1 business day, appoint an assessor where required
within 3 business days, and make a decision within 10 business days of receiving all
requested information. Where the claim is straightforward and under $5,000, Meridian may
settle on the documents without an assessor. Where the claim is complex, Meridian will
provide an update at least every 20 business days. Payment is made to the insured, not to
the customer, unless the insured directs otherwise in writing.

Progress payments are available on a property claim where reinstatement will take more
than 60 days and the insured has incurred cost. A request for a progress payment should be
made through the broker with supporting invoices.

---

**End of policy schedule and wording — Policy MDC-BP-4471822**
**Meridian Underwriting Australia Pty Ltd · AFSL 241 663**
**This policy renews on 30 September 2026. Renewal terms are issued through Hargreaves &
Locke Insurance Brokers not less than 30 days before that date. The insured should review
the sums insured at A8, the gross profit figure at A7 and the bailee's limits at 4.2
before accepting renewal terms.**

# GOLDFIELDS PLANT INSPECTION SERVICES PTY LTD

## Pressure Equipment In-Service Inspection Report and Registration Record

**Inspection body:** Goldfields Plant Inspection Services Pty Ltd
ABN 78 604 221 337
7 Nolan Street, Bendigo VIC 3550
(03) 5441 2290 · inspections@goldfieldsplant.com.au

Inspection body accreditation No. **IBA-0374**, type A inspection body operating to
AS/NZS ISO/IEC 17020, scope: in-service inspection of boilers and pressure vessels to
AS 3788.

**Report number:** GPIS-2026-1188
**Report issue:** 1 (final)
**Date of inspection:** 24 June 2026
**Date of report:** 26 June 2026
**Supersedes:** GPIS-2025-0974 dated 26/06/2025

| Party | Detail |
|---|---|
| Owner / operator | Aveline Holdings Pty Ltd ACN 617 903 558, trading as Main Street Dry Cleaners |
| Responsible officer | Karen Whitfield, Director |
| Site | Shop 4, 118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo VIC 3550 |
| Plant location on site | Boiler house, rear of plant area, adjacent the Bath Lane roller door |
| Site contact on the day | P. Nguyen, plant operator |

**Inspector:** G. Mattison
Pressure Equipment Inspector, competent person for the purposes of AS 3788 Section 3
Qualifications: Advanced Diploma of Engineering (Mechanical); Certificate IV in Pressure
Equipment In-Service Inspection; Standard Boiler Operation (high risk work) licence;
Non-destructive testing Level 2, ultrasonic thickness testing and magnetic particle
testing
Inspector registration within the inspection body: **GPI-INS-114**
Authorised signatory for reports issued under accreditation IBA-0374

---

## 1. Purpose and summary

### 1.1 Purpose

This report records the annual external in-service inspection of the Fulton FB-030
vertical gas fired steam boiler installed at Shop 4, 118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo,
carried out on 24 June 2026 in accordance with AS 3788 *Pressure equipment — In-service
inspection*, and records the particulars of the Victorian plant registration held for
that item.

It also records the safety valve test, the safety device function tests, the water
treatment review, the operator competency and log review, and the observations and
defects arising, with the action required and the date by which each must be completed.

### 1.2 Summary of outcome

The boiler was found to be in sound condition and fit for continued service at its
registered maximum allowable working pressure of 690 kPa, subject to the rectification of
the two defects listed at Section 9 within the times stated there.

No condition was found that required the boiler to be taken out of service. No condition
was found that required a reduction in the maximum allowable working pressure. The safety
valve lifted, passed and reseated within tolerance. The water level controls and the low
water cut-out operated correctly on test. Boiler water chemistry was within limits, with a
rising total dissolved solids trend noted for attention.

Two matters require action:

- **Item 1** — the lower gauge glass gland is weeping and must be repacked. **Category 3,
  30 days, by 24 July 2026.**
- **Item 2** — the bottom blowdown valve packing is worn and must be replaced. **Category
  4, at the next shutdown and in any event by 30 November 2026.**

Twelve further observations are recorded at Section 9. None of them affects fitness for
service. One of them — the three gaps in the daily operating log during May 2026 — is a
management system matter that the operator must close out, and is discussed at Section 11.

### 1.3 Next inspection dates

| Activity | Interval applied | Last performed | Next due |
|---|---|---|---|
| External in-service inspection | 12 months | 24/06/2026 | **24/06/2027** |
| Internal inspection | 24 months | 18/06/2024 | **June 2028** |
| Hydrostatic test | 15 years from manufacture, then as determined | 2014 (manufacture) | **2029** |
| Safety valve lift test | 12 months | 24/06/2026 | 24/06/2027 |
| Safety device function tests | 12 months by inspector; monthly by operator | 24/06/2026 | 24/06/2027 |
| Plant registration renewal | 5 years | 01/07/2022 | **30/06/2027** |

The internal inspection interval was extended from 12 to 24 months at the 2024 inspection
on the basis of sound internal condition, a stable water treatment regime and a
satisfactory operating history. That extension is reviewed at each external inspection and
is confirmed for a further year by this report. It will be reconsidered if the total
dissolved solids trend noted at observation 12 is not brought back.

---

## 2. Registration record

### 2.1 Registration particulars

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Item registration number | **VIC-PV-118-4470** |
| Registration type | Registration of plant (item registration), steam boiler |
| Registration holder | Aveline Holdings Pty Ltd ACN 617 903 558 |
| Registered location | Shop 4, 118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo VIC 3550 |
| Date first registered | 14/08/2014 |
| Current registration period | 01/07/2022 to **30/06/2027** |
| Design registration | VIC-DR-2013-8871 (design verification accepted 2013) |
| Hazard level (AS 4343) | **B** |
| Registered MAWP | 690 kPa |
| Registration renewal lodgement window | From 30/03/2027; the regulator's renewal notice is ordinarily issued about 90 days before expiry |

The registration certificate was sighted on site on the day of inspection, laminated and
displayed on the boiler house wall adjacent the control panel, together with the previous
inspection report GPIS-2025-0974 and the current safety valve test certificate.

### 2.2 What the registration obliges the operator to do

Registration of an item of plant is not a one-off event. It carries continuing
obligations, and it is those obligations that this inspection is evidence of having been
met. The operator must:

1. **Keep the registration current.** The registration expires on 30 June 2027 and must be
   renewed before that date. Operating a registered item of plant after its registration
   has lapsed is an offence, and it also voids the machinery breakdown cover under the
   business pack policy, which requires the registration to be current.
2. **Have the item inspected by a competent person at the required intervals**, and keep
   the reports. This report satisfies that obligation for the 2026 external inspection.
3. **Not alter the item, its pressure parts, its safety valve set pressure or its safety
   controls** without a competent person's assessment and, where the alteration is
   material, a fresh design verification.
4. **Notify the regulator** of a change of the registration holder, a change of the
   registered location, the permanent decommissioning of the item, or an incident
   involving the item.
5. **Ensure the item is operated only by a person holding the required licence or
   competency**, and keep evidence of that competency.
6. **Maintain the operating and maintenance records** required by AS 2593 for the
   attendance category applied to the boiler, and produce them on request.
7. **Rectify defects** identified in an inspection report by the date the report requires,
   and keep evidence of the rectification for production at the next inspection.
8. **Keep the plant records for the life of the item** — the design and manufacturing data,
   the registration, every inspection report, every repair record, every safety valve
   certificate, and the operating logs for at least the period between internal
   inspections. Where the item is sold or relocated, those records go with it.
9. **Display the registration number on or adjacent the item**, legibly.

### 2.3 Records sighted

| Record | Status |
|---|---|
| Registration certificate VIC-PV-118-4470 | Sighted, current to 30/06/2027 |
| Manufacturer's data report and nameplate rubbing | Sighted, held in the plant file |
| Design verification VIC-DR-2013-8871 | Sighted (copy) |
| 2021 refurbishment report and weld repair record | Sighted, see 4.4 |
| Previous inspection report GPIS-2025-0974 | Sighted; all 2025 items closed out, see 9.4 |
| Safety valve certificate, 2025 test | Sighted; superseded by this report |
| Daily operating logs, 01/07/2025 to 24/06/2026 | Sighted; three gaps in May 2026, see Section 11 |
| Water treatment service reports, 12 monthly | Sighted, see Section 10 |
| Operator licences | Sighted, see Section 11 |
| Gas installation compliance certificate, 2021 | Sighted (issued on completion of the refurbishment) |

---

## 3. Plant particulars

### 3.1 Identification

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Plant description | Vertical gas fired tubeless steam boiler |
| Make | Fulton |
| Model | FB-030 |
| Serial number | FB030-2014-3312 |
| Nameplate | Stainless plate, riveted to the front casing at eye height, legible |
| Year of manufacture | 2014 |
| Date installed | 2014 (commissioned 11/08/2014) |
| Refurbished | 2021 (see 4.4) |
| Item registration | VIC-PV-118-4470 |
| Insurance | Scheduled item M1 under Meridian Underwriting policy MDC-BP-4471822, machinery breakdown, insured value $48,000 |

### 3.2 Design and duty data

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Rated output | 30 boiler horsepower |
| Steam output, from and at 100 °C | 470 kg/h |
| Maximum allowable working pressure (MAWP) | 690 kPa gauge |
| Design temperature | 171 °C (saturation at MAWP) |
| Hydrostatic test pressure | 1,035 kPa (1.5 x MAWP) |
| Heating surface | 13.9 m² |
| Gas input, high fire | 1,320 MJ/h (367 kW) |
| Fuel | Natural gas |
| Normal water content at working level | 340 L |
| Shell outside diameter | 965 mm |
| Overall height | 1,880 mm |
| Shell plate nominal thickness | 10.0 mm |
| Shell plate minimum required thickness | 8.6 mm |
| Corrosion allowance | 1.5 mm |
| Materials of construction | Shell and heads SA-516 Gr 70; furnace SA-516 Gr 70; nozzles SA-106 Gr B |
| Design and manufacturing code | ASME Section I, design verified for Australian registration under AS 1210 |
| Hazard level | AS 4343 Hazard Level B |
| Attendance category | AS 2593 limited attendance, 24 hour (LA-24) |

### 3.3 Operating parameters as set and found

| Parameter | Setting found | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Burner cut-in pressure | 580 kPa | As per 2021 commissioning record |
| Burner cut-out pressure | 640 kPa | Modulating high/low burner, high fire below 600 kPa |
| High pressure limit, manual reset | 660 kPa | Tested, see Appendix B |
| Safety valve set pressure | 690 kPa | Equal to MAWP, see Section 8 |
| Steam pressure supplied to the plant | 550 to 620 kPa at the machines | Reduced at the header take-offs |
| Normal water level | 175 mm above the furnace crown | Marked on the gauge glass frame |
| Low water alarm level | 100 mm above the crown | First low, audible alarm |
| Low water cut-out level | 75 mm above the crown | Second low, lockout, manual reset |
| Feedwater temperature | 82 °C | Hotwell |
| Blowdown vessel | 200 L, vented, discharging to the trade waste connection | Coliban Water trade waste agreement TW-4471 |

### 3.4 Service and duty

The boiler serves the whole of the Bendigo production plant. Steam is reticulated to the
Sankosha shirt unit, the utility press, the trouser topper and trouser legger, the Trevil
steam-air finisher and Suzy form finisher, the spotting board, and the stills of the Union
XL-800 and Realstar HM-450 dry cleaning machines. Condensate returns by gravity to the
hotwell.

The boiler is fired from about 6:30 each weekday and from about 7:30 on Saturday, and is
shut down at the end of production. It is not fired on Sunday. Annual firing hours are
estimated by the operator at 2,600 to 2,800. Load is intermittent and peaks during the
morning shirt run and again in the mid-afternoon finishing run. The boiler is the single
point of failure for the whole finishing line; there is no standby boiler and no steam
accumulator.

---

## 4. Scope and standards applied

### 4.1 Scope of this inspection

This was an **external in-service inspection** conducted with the boiler cold at the
commencement of the inspection, then fired and brought to working pressure for the
functional testing. It comprised:

- visual examination of all accessible external surfaces of the pressure envelope, the
  casing having been opened at the front and the rear access panels removed;
- ultrasonic thickness measurement at 14 locations on the shell, heads and furnace;
- examination of all fittings, mountings, connections and pressure retaining components
  accessible without dismantling;
- examination of the safety valve, and a lift test on steam under boiler pressure;
- function testing of the water level controls, the low water cut-out, the high pressure
  limit, the flame safeguard and the gas train safety devices;
- examination of the feedwater system, the hotwell, the softener and the chemical dosing
  arrangement;
- examination of the blowdown arrangement and its discharge;
- examination of the gas train and the flue system;
- combustion analysis at high fire and at low fire;
- sampling and testing of boiler water, feedwater and condensate;
- review of the operating logs, the water treatment records, the maintenance records and
  the operator competency records; and
- review of the close-out of items raised in the previous report.

### 4.2 What this inspection did not cover

This was not an internal inspection. The pressure envelope was not entered and the
waterside and fireside internal surfaces were not directly examined; the last internal
examination was on 18 June 2024 and the next is due in June 2028. No hydrostatic test was
performed; the next is due in 2029. The furnace refractory was viewed through the burner
opening only. Buried, insulated or otherwise inaccessible surfaces were not examined
except where thickness readings were taken through prepared windows. The steam
reticulation beyond the crown valve and the first isolating valve, and the steam-using
equipment, are outside the scope of this report.

Nothing in this report is a statement about the condition of the electrical installation
beyond the safety devices tested, or about the structural adequacy of the building.

### 4.3 Standards and instruments applied

| Standard | Application in this inspection |
|---|---|
| **AS 3788** *Pressure equipment — In-service inspection* | The governing standard. Determined the scope, the inspection intervals, the competency of the inspector, the acceptance criteria for wastage and defects, and the form of this report. |
| **AS 1210** *Pressure vessels* | Applied to the assessment of minimum required wall thickness, to the assessment of the 2021 weld repair, and to the assessment of nozzle and attachment condition. |
| **AS 2593** *Boilers — Safety management systems and supervision services* | Applied to the attendance category, the safety device requirements, the operator competency requirements and the operating log requirements. |
| **AS 4343** *Pressure equipment — Hazard levels* | Applied to confirm the hazard level of the item, which drives the registration and inspection obligations. |
| **AS 1271** *Safety valves, other valves, liquid level gauges and other fittings for boilers and unfired pressure vessels* | Applied to the safety valve, the gauge glass, the pressure gauge and the boiler mountings. |
| **AS 3814** *Industrial and commercial gas-fired appliances* | Applied to the gas train, the burner safety sequence and the flue. |
| **AS 2885**, **AS 4037**, **AS 1228** | Not applicable to this item. |

Instruments used: ultrasonic thickness gauge, 5 MHz twin crystal probe, calibrated
06/05/2026, certificate UT-2026-0442; digital test pressure gauge 0 to 1,600 kPa,
calibrated 11/02/2026, certificate PG-2026-0118; flue gas analyser, calibrated 02/06/2026,
certificate FGA-2026-0231; digital thermometer with K-type probe; boiler water test kit,
reagents in date; and a calibrated stopwatch for timing safety sequences.

### 4.4 History taken into account

- **2014** — manufactured, imported, design verified, installed and commissioned at the
  Bendigo site. Registered 14 August 2014.
- **2018** — first internal inspection after four years of service. Light scale on the
  waterside, no wastage of consequence, cleaned and returned to service.
- **2021** — refurbishment. The furnace was removed and replaced, the burner was replaced
  with a modulating high/low unit, the gas train was renewed to AS 3814, the level control
  chamber was replaced, the insulation and casing were renewed and the flue was replaced
  above the roof line. The weld repair to the furnace-to-tubesheet attachment was carried
  out by a qualified welder to a qualified procedure, radiographed, and accepted. Records
  sighted and held in the plant file. The MAWP was not altered.
- **2022** — registration renewed to 30 June 2027.
- **2024** — internal inspection, 18 June. Waterside clean, no scale of consequence, no
  measurable wastage against the 2018 datum, internal inspection interval extended to 24
  months on that basis.
- **2025** — external inspection, GPIS-2025-0974. Two items raised: a leaking union on the
  chemical dosing line, and a pressure gauge reading 20 kPa high. Both closed out, see 9.4.
- **2026** — this inspection.

---

## 5. Inspection methodology

documents.title: Boiler inspection report — Sequence followed on the day, Boiler mountings and fittings generally, Blowdown arrangement
documents.background: The annual AS 3788 external inspection, carried out 24 June 2026 by Goldfields Plant Inspection. Registration VIC-PV-118-4470 expires 30 June 2027. Two items need action — the gauge glass gland and the blowdown valve packing — and the report notes gaps in our daily logs in May.
documents.text:
### 5.1 Sequence followed on the day

The inspection was performed over five and a half hours on 24 June 2026, commencing at
07:15 with the boiler cold and off line from the previous evening.

1. **Documentation review, 07:15 to 08:00.** Registration, previous report, logs, water
   treatment reports, maintenance records and operator licences reviewed with the
   responsible officer and the plant operator before any physical work commenced.
2. **Isolation and permit, 08:00 to 08:15.** The boiler was confirmed off line, cold, and
   at atmospheric pressure. The gas was isolated at the manual shut-off cock and locked.
   The electrical supply was isolated and tagged. The crown valve was closed. A permit was
   raised and countersigned by the operator.
3. **External examination cold, 08:15 to 09:45.** Casing panels removed at the front and
   rear. Visual examination of the shell, heads, furnace throat, nozzles, attachments,
   supports and the underside of the boiler. Examination of all mountings and fittings.
   Examination of the gauge glass, the level control chamber, the blowdown arrangement,
   the feedwater connection and the safety valve installation.
4. **Ultrasonic thickness testing, 09:45 to 10:45.** Fourteen locations, prepared by wire
   brushing to bare metal where insulation and paint allowed, with couplant, three readings
   per location and the lowest recorded. Locations marked and recorded so they can be
   repeated at the next inspection. See Appendix A.
5. **Feedwater, softener and chemical dosing examination, 10:45 to 11:15.** Hotwell,
   feedwater pumps, non-return and isolating valves, softener resin bed and brine
   saturator, chemical dosing pump and pot.
6. **Water sampling and testing, 11:15 to 11:45.** Boiler water drawn from the sample cock
   after a purge and cooled in a stainless sample cooler; feedwater from the hotwell
   outlet; condensate from the return line. Tested on site. See Section 10.
7. **Return to service and warm-up, 11:45 to 12:45.** Permit closed, isolations removed,
   gas restored, boiler fired and brought up slowly to working pressure with the operator
   at the panel.
8. **Functional testing at pressure, 12:45 to 13:45.** Gauge glass blowdown, level control
   tests, low water cut-out by controlled evaporation, high pressure limit, flame failure,
   gas pressure switches, purge timing, and the safety valve lift test. See Sections 6, 7,
   8 and Appendix B.
9. **Combustion analysis, 13:45 to 14:10.** At high fire after 10 minutes of stable firing,
   and at low fire.
10. **Close-out with the operator and the responsible officer, 14:10 to 14:45.** Findings
    walked through at the boiler, defects and required dates explained, photographs taken.

### 5.2 Acceptance criteria applied

- **Wall thickness.** A reading is acceptable where it is at or above the minimum required
  thickness of 8.6 mm for the shell and 10.8 mm for the furnace. A reading within 10% of
  the minimum required thickness is reportable and triggers a shortened re-measurement
  interval. The rate of loss is assessed against the 2018 and 2024 datum readings.
- **Surface defects.** Any crack, lamination, gouge, arc strike or bulge in a pressure part
  is a Category 1 finding. Isolated pitting is assessed against the remaining thickness at
  the pit base.
- **Leakage.** Any leakage of steam or water from a pressure part or a pressure retaining
  joint is reportable. Leakage from a packed gland is assessed on its rate and its
  location; a weep that can be contained by repacking is Category 3, an active leak that
  cannot be isolated is Category 1.
- **Safety valve.** Popping pressure within +3% / -0% of set pressure; reseat within 10% of
  set pressure; no chatter; no leakage after reseat.
- **Safety devices.** Each device must operate at its set point and must produce the
  required response — alarm, lockout, or shutdown with manual reset as applicable. Flame
  failure lockout within 1 second of flame loss.
- **Water chemistry.** Assessed against the limits at Section 10, which are the water
  treatment supplier's limits for this boiler type and duty and are consistent with
  AS 2593 guidance.

---

## 6. Detailed findings — pressure parts, fittings and systems

### 6.1 Shell, heads and external pressure envelope

The shell was examined externally over its full accessible height, front, rear and both
sides, with the casing panels removed and the insulation lifted at the prepared thickness
test windows.

The external surface is sound. The paint system is intact over the great majority of the
shell. There is light surface oxidation at the lower shell adjacent the blowdown
connection, consistent with historical minor weeping from the blowdown valve gland and
consistent with observation item 2. The oxidation is superficial; a wire brush and probe
found sound metal beneath and no pitting of consequence. There is no bulging, no
distortion, no evidence of overheating, no arc strike, no gouge and no crack.

The top head and the crown are sound and dry. The bottom head and the boiler underside
were examined with a mirror and a torch and are dry, with no accumulation of debris or
water beneath the boiler.

Ultrasonic thickness readings are recorded at Appendix A. The lowest shell reading was
10.1 mm against a nominal 10.0 mm and a minimum required 8.6 mm. The lowest furnace
reading was 12.2 mm against a minimum required 10.8 mm. Comparison against the 2024 datum
shows no measurable loss within the resolution of the instrument. There is no wastage
requiring action, and no basis on wastage grounds to shorten any interval.

### 6.2 Furnace, tubesheet and the 2021 weld repair

The furnace throat and the furnace-to-tubesheet attachment were examined visually through
the burner opening with the burner head withdrawn, and by magnetic particle examination of
the accessible portion of the 2021 repair weld and its heat affected zone.

The repair weld is sound. No linear indication, no crack, no undercut of consequence and
no evidence of service-induced cracking were found. The weld cap profile is smooth and
blends well into the parent metal. The magnetic particle examination covered 340 mm of the
accessible weld length; the balance is not accessible without entry and will be examined
at the 2028 internal inspection.

The refractory at the furnace throat is intact, with a hairline surface craze pattern that
is normal for the material and the service and is not a defect. The furnace internal
surface visible through the opening is clean and carries a light even oxide with no
scaling, no soot loading and no evidence of flame impingement.

### 6.3 Nozzles, connections and attachments

All nozzles, branches, doubling plates and attachments were examined at their welds and at
the parent metal adjacent.

| Connection | Condition |
|---|---|
| Crown / main steam outlet | Sound. Weld and flange faces good. No leakage. Bolting complete, correct grade, evenly tensioned. |
| Safety valve branch | Sound. Full bore, no reduction, no isolation valve fitted between the boiler and the valve, which is correct. |
| Feedwater inlet | Sound. Check valve and stop valve in the correct order. No leakage. |
| Bottom blowdown | Sound at the weld. See item 2 for the valve packing. |
| Surface / TDS blowdown | Sound. Skimmer connection clear. |
| Gauge glass connections, upper and lower | Sound at the boiler. See item 1 for the lower gland. |
| Level control chamber connections | Sound. Renewed 2021. Isolating cocks free and correctly padlocked open. |
| Pressure gauge connection with siphon | Sound. Siphon clear on blowdown. |
| Chemical dosing injection | Sound. The union raised in 2025 has been replaced and is dry. |
| Sample cock | Sound. Operates freely. |
| Vent / air cock | Sound. Operates freely. |
| Drain | Sound. Plugged and dry. |

The boiler supports and the mounting feet are sound, square, and bear evenly on the
plinth. The holding down bolts are complete and tight. There is no distortion of the
supports and no evidence of movement. Clearance around the boiler is adequate for
inspection and maintenance on all four sides, with 800 mm at the narrowest point.

### 6.4 Boiler mountings and fittings generally

All mountings are of the correct pressure rating and are compatible with the MAWP.

- **Crown valve** — screw down non-return type, DN40, operates freely through its full
  travel, gland dry, handwheel present and legible, position indicator clear.
- **Pressure gauge** — 100 mm dial, 0 to 1,000 kPa, with a red set pointer at 690 kPa and
  a siphon. Checked against the calibrated test gauge at 300, 500 and 620 kPa; readings
  agreed within 5 kPa at every point. The gauge replaced in 2025 after the previous gauge
  was found reading 20 kPa high; the replacement is accurate and its calibration record is
  in the plant file.
- **Test cock** — fitted below the gauge, operates freely.
- **Fusible plug** — not fitted to this design; not required.
- **Nameplate** — legible, correctly attached, MAWP and serial number agree with the
  registration.
- **Isolating cocks on level controls** — of the padlockable type, padlocked open, keys held
  by the operator, correct.

### 6.5 Safety valve — installation

One safety valve is fitted, which is correct for this output and hazard level.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Make and type | Hartland Valve Co. type SV-25, full lift, spring loaded, open bonnet with easing lever |
| Inlet / outlet | DN25 / DN40 |
| Set pressure | 690 kPa |
| Certified capacity | 520 kg/h at 3% accumulation |
| Serial number | HV-25-14-7702 |
| Seal | Lead seal, wired, seal number 4471 applied at this test |

The valve is mounted vertically, directly on a full bore branch on the top head, with no
isolating valve, no restriction and no bend between the boiler and the valve. The discharge
pipe is DN40, rises vertically, is independently supported so that no load is carried by
the valve body, is fitted with a drain at its lowest point which was proved clear, and
terminates outside the building above the roof line in a position where discharge cannot
strike a person or an adjacent surface. The discharge pipe was checked for obstruction with
a light and a probe and is clear.

The certified capacity of 520 kg/h exceeds the maximum evaporative capacity of the boiler
of 470 kg/h, as required. The easing lever is present, free, and reachable from the
operating position.

The lift test result is at Section 8.

### 6.6 Water level controls

The boiler is fitted with two independent water level control systems in a side-mounted
chamber, as required for the attendance category applied.

| Device | Type | Function | Set point | Result on test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary level control | Conductivity probe, three tip | Modulates the feed pump on and off | Pump on 150 mm, pump off 195 mm above crown | Correct, pump cycled cleanly at both points |
| First low water alarm | Conductivity probe | Audible and visual alarm, no shutdown | 100 mm above crown | Alarm sounded at 103 mm, correct |
| Low water cut-out (second low) | Independent conductivity probe on a separate circuit | Burner lockout, manual reset | 75 mm above crown | Burner locked out at 78 mm, manual reset required and confirmed, correct |
| Level control chamber blowdown | Manual valve | Clears the chamber | — | Operated, chamber cleared and refilled cleanly, level restored within 4 seconds |

The low water cut-out was tested by the controlled evaporation method with the feedwater
isolated and the burner on low fire, under the inspector's direct supervision, with the
operator at the panel and the manual gas cock within reach. The level was allowed to fall
until the cut-out operated. The burner shut down, the gas valves closed, the lockout was
indicated at the panel, and the unit required a manual reset before it would refire. That
is the correct behaviour.

The probe tips were withdrawn and examined. They are clean, with a light even oxide and no
scale bridging between tips and no erosion. The chamber internals were viewed through the
inspection plug and are clean.

The level control chamber and its connecting pipework were renewed in 2021 and remain in
good condition. Both isolating cocks are the padlockable type, are padlocked in the open
position, and were confirmed open before and after testing.

### 6.7 Gauge glass

A single reflex gauge glass is fitted in a bronze frame with upper and lower fittings,
each with an integral isolating cock and a ball check, and with a drain cock at the lower
fitting. The normal water level is marked on the frame.

The glass itself is clean, clear, undamaged, free of chipping and free of the vertical
etching that indicates an aged glass, and the water line was clearly visible from the
operating position at all times during the inspection.

The gauge glass was blown down under the inspector's observation. The water returned
briskly and settled within 3 seconds, which indicates that both connections are clear.
The upper and lower cocks operate freely and seal.

**The lower gland is weeping.** A steady bead of moisture forms at the lower packing nut
and runs down the fitting and onto the shell below. The weep is small — a drop forming
roughly every 40 seconds at working pressure — and it is contained, and it does not
prevent the gauge from performing its function. It is nevertheless a leak from a pressure
retaining joint and it must be corrected. The gland nut has already been taken up to the
end of its available travel, so tightening further will not help; the packing is spent and
must be renewed. This is **item 1** at Section 9 and is required within 30 days.

The staining on the shell below the gauge glass is the mineral residue from this weep. It
was cleaned back during the inspection so that the staining seen at the next inspection
will be new staining and not old.

No spare gauge glass, gasket set or packing is held on site. That is recorded as
observation 11.

### 6.8 Feedwater system

| Component | Condition |
|---|---|
| Hotwell / feed tank | 300 L, insulated, lid fitted, vent clear and directed away from the walkway. Sound, no corrosion of consequence at the waterline. Operating at 82 °C, measured. |
| Hotwell level control | Ballcock with an overflow to the floor waste. Operates cleanly, no hunting, no overflow in service. |
| Makeup water | Through the softener. Meter fitted and read at each water treatment service. |
| Condensate return | Gravity return from the plant, entering below the hotwell water line, which is correct. Return measured at 54% of feedwater. |
| Feedwater pump | Aquastream MS-4 multistage centrifugal, 1.5 kW. No leakage at the mechanical seal. Bearing noise normal. Delivery pressure 810 kPa against a boiler pressure of 620 kPa, adequate margin. |
| Standby pump | None fitted. See observation 13. |
| Feed check valve | Operates and seals. Tested by isolating the stop valve and observing no reverse flow. |
| Feed stop valve | Operates freely, gland dry. |
| Strainer | Cleaned during the inspection. Light fine debris only, no scale. |
| Softener | Twin tank, brine regeneration, timed with a meter override. Resin bed level correct, no channelling visible, brine saturator at correct level with salt present. |
| Chemical dosing | Positive displacement dosing pump feeding oxygen scavenger and alkalinity builder into the feed line downstream of the pump. Injection point sound. Dosing pot at 60% at the time of inspection. The union that was leaking in 2025 has been replaced. |

The feedwater arrangement is correct in principle and in execution. The only matters
arising are observation 4 (the hotwell thermometer) and observation 13 (no standby feed
pump), neither of which affects fitness for service.

### 6.9 Blowdown arrangement

Bottom blowdown is by a single line from the lowest point of the shell through two valves
in series — a quick opening lever valve at the boiler and a slow opening screw-down valve
downstream — discharging to a 200 L vented blowdown vessel and from there to the trade
waste connection under Coliban Water trade waste agreement TW-4471.

Surface blowdown for total dissolved solids control is manual, from a skimmer connection
at the normal water line, through a needle valve to the same blowdown vessel.

| Component | Condition |
|---|---|
| Quick opening blowdown valve | Operates freely through its full travel. Lever intact. Seals on closing. Gland dry. |
| Slow opening screw-down blowdown valve | Operates freely. **Packing worn** — the gland nut is near the end of its travel and a trace of moisture is present at the gland after operation. Seals on closing at present. See item 2. |
| Blowdown line | Sound, full bore, correctly supported, falls continuously to the vessel, no traps, no reduction. |
| Blowdown vessel | 200 L, vented to atmosphere outside the building, vent clear. Internally clean on inspection through the access plug. |
| Discharge to trade waste | Cooled and diluted through the vessel. Temperature at the discharge measured at 41 °C on a bottom blowdown, within the trade waste agreement limit of 60 °C. |
| Blowdown procedure | Displayed on the boiler house wall. Correct: quick opening valve opened last and closed first, short sharp blows, level watched throughout. |

Bottom blowdown is recorded in the daily log as being performed once per operating day at
the start of the shift, which is appropriate for this duty and this water quality. Surface
blowdown is recorded as being performed when the operator's TDS test exceeds the action
level. See observation 12 on the TDS trend.

documents.title: Boiler inspection report — Gas train and burner, Result, Items requiring action
documents.background: The annual AS 3788 external inspection, carried out 24 June 2026 by Goldfields Plant Inspection. Registration VIC-PV-118-4470 expires 30 June 2027. Two items need action — the gauge glass gland and the blowdown valve packing — and the report notes gaps in our daily logs in May.
documents.text:
### 6.10 Gas train and burner

The gas train was renewed in 2021 to AS 3814 and is in good condition.

| Component | Condition and result |
|---|---|
| Manual shut-off cock | Accessible, correctly labelled, operates freely, lockable, within reach of the operating position |
| Gas filter | Clean on inspection, element in good condition |
| Gas pressure regulator | Operating at 2.75 kPa outlet, stable, vent line clear and terminating outside |
| Low gas pressure switch | Set 1.5 kPa, operated at 1.55 kPa on test, lockout with manual reset, correct |
| High gas pressure switch | Set 4.0 kPa, operated at 3.92 kPa on test, lockout with manual reset, correct |
| Safety shut-off valves | Two in series, class A, with proof of closure on the upstream valve. Both closed within 0.6 seconds on demand. Valve proving sequence completed and passed on each start observed. |
| Burner | Modulating high/low, forced draught, renewed 2021. Head and diffuser clean, no distortion, no carbon build-up. Ignition electrodes correctly gapped at 3 mm and in good condition. |
| Flame safeguard | UV scanner. Flame signal 68% at high fire, 61% at low fire, both well above the 25% minimum. Scanner lens clean. |
| Flame failure response | Simulated by obscuring the scanner. Lockout in **0.8 seconds**, within the 1 second requirement. Manual reset required and confirmed. |
| Pre-purge | 30 seconds at full purge rate, timed. Correct. |
| Post-purge | 15 seconds, timed. Correct. |
| Air proving switch | Operated on obstruction of the fan inlet, lockout, correct |
| Gas leak test | Leak detection fluid applied to every joint in the train with the gas on and the boiler off. No leakage found at any joint. |

Combustion analysis:

| Parameter | High fire | Low fire | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oxygen | 4.2% | 5.6% | Within band |
| Carbon dioxide | 9.6% | 8.8% | Within band |
| Carbon monoxide | 42 ppm | 31 ppm | Well below the 400 ppm action level |
| Net stack temperature | 218 °C | 176 °C | Normal, consistent with clean heat transfer surfaces |
| Ambient at analyser | 14 °C | 14 °C | — |
| Calculated combustion efficiency | 82.4% | 83.1% | Good for this boiler type and age |

The low carbon monoxide and the normal stack temperature together indicate clean
combustion and clean fireside heat transfer surfaces, which is consistent with the visual
examination of the furnace and with the water treatment record.

### 6.11 Flue

The flue is a DN250 twin wall stainless steel system, renewed above the roof line in 2021,
rising 6.2 m from the boiler outlet through the plant ceiling and roof to a terminal cowl
above the roof line and clear of the adjacent parapet.

The flue was examined from the boiler outlet to the ceiling penetration internally by
sight and externally over its full accessible length, and from the roof at the terminal.
The joints are sound and correctly banded. The supports are secure. The roof penetration
flashing is intact and weather-tight. There is no evidence of gas leakage at any joint, no
evidence of condensate staining below any joint inside the building, and no distortion.

There is light brown discolouration at the flue cap and immediately below it at the roof
penetration. This is consistent with normal weathering and with condensate at the cold end
of a flue on a boiler that cycles daily; it is not perforation and it is not corrosion of
consequence. It is recorded as observation 7 for monitoring rather than as a defect.

The draught at the boiler outlet was measured at minus 12 Pa at high fire, which is within
the range the burner is set for. There is no evidence of spillage at the draught diverter
or of down-draught at the terminal.

### 6.12 Boiler house, environment and services

The boiler occupies a dedicated area at the rear of the plant, partitioned from the
production floor, with a door to the plant and a second door to the Bath Lane roller door
area.

- **Ventilation** — high and low level permanent openings to outside, unobstructed,
  sufficient for the gas input. Verified clear.
- **Lighting** — measured at approximately 90 lux at the gauge glass. This is low for the
  task of reading a water level and carrying out a level control test. See observation 6.
- **Housekeeping** — generally good. The boiler house is not used for storage, the floor
  is clear, and there is no combustible material within 1 m of the boiler. A wooden wedge
  was in use holding the boiler house door open at the time of inspection; see observation
  10.
- **Fire extinguisher** — dry chemical, 4.5 kg, mounted at the doorway, tagged and in test
  to 03/2027.
- **Emergency stop** — mushroom head, outside the boiler house door, correctly labelled,
  tested and functional.
- **Signage** — boiler house identification, gas isolation location, no unauthorised entry,
  and the blowdown procedure are all displayed and legible. The registration number is
  displayed on the boiler.
- **Noise and heat** — nothing abnormal. Surface temperatures on the casing measured
  between 38 °C and 44 °C, normal for the insulation fitted.
- **Steam header lagging** — a section of lagging approximately 400 mm long has been
  removed from the steam header immediately downstream of the crown valve, apparently
  during a past valve repair, and not replaced. Bare pipe at that point is a burn risk and
  a heat loss. See observation 3.

---

## 7. Safety device function test results

The full record is at Appendix B. In summary, every safety device fitted to the boiler was
tested during this inspection and every device performed correctly. No device was found
bypassed, disabled, strapped, jumpered or set outside its correct set point. No evidence
was found of any past bypassing.

| Device | Required response | Result |
|---|---|---|
| First low water alarm | Alarm at 100 mm above crown | **Pass**, operated at 103 mm |
| Low water cut-out | Lockout with manual reset at 75 mm | **Pass**, operated at 78 mm, manual reset confirmed |
| Primary level control | Feed pump on 150 mm, off 195 mm | **Pass** |
| High pressure limit | Lockout with manual reset at 660 kPa | **Pass**, operated at 657 kPa |
| Operating pressure control | Burner off at 640 kPa, on at 580 kPa | **Pass** |
| Flame failure | Lockout within 1 second | **Pass**, 0.8 seconds |
| Low gas pressure switch | Lockout at 1.5 kPa | **Pass**, 1.55 kPa |
| High gas pressure switch | Lockout at 4.0 kPa | **Pass**, 3.92 kPa |
| Air proving switch | Lockout on loss of air | **Pass** |
| Valve proving system | Prove closed before start | **Pass** |
| Pre-purge timing | 30 seconds | **Pass**, 30 seconds |
| Safety valve | Lift, pass and reseat within tolerance | **Pass**, see Section 8 |
| Emergency stop | Isolate burner and fan | **Pass** |

---

## 8. Safety valve test record

### 8.1 Method

The safety valve was tested on steam under boiler pressure. The operating pressure control
and the high pressure limit were temporarily raised under the inspector's direct control,
with the calibrated test gauge fitted at the test cock and observed continuously, with the
operator at the panel and the manual gas cock within reach, and with the boiler house
cleared of all other persons. The burner was held at high fire and the pressure allowed to
rise until the valve lifted. Pressure was then reduced and the reseat pressure recorded.
The controls were immediately restored to their normal set points and re-verified before
the boiler was returned to normal service.

The test was a lift, pass and reseat test. It was not an accumulation test; the capacity of
the valve is established by its certification and its certified capacity exceeds the
maximum evaporative capacity of the boiler.

### 8.2 Result

| Parameter | Value | Requirement | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Set pressure (nameplate and certificate) | 690 kPa | 690 kPa, equal to MAWP | Correct |
| **Popping pressure, measured** | **703 kPa** | Not more than 3% above set (711 kPa), not below set | **Pass**, +1.9% |
| Behaviour on lift | Sharp, clean pop to full lift, no simmer before lift, no chatter, no hammer | Sharp lift, no chatter | **Pass** |
| **Reseat pressure, measured** | **641 kPa** | Not more than 10% below set (621 kPa) | **Pass**, blowdown 7.1% |
| Leakage after reseat, observed 10 minutes | None | No leakage | **Pass** |
| Easing lever operation | Free, valve lifted and reseated cleanly on the lever at 600 kPa | Free and functional | **Pass** |
| Discharge pipe | Clear, drained, supported, terminating safely | Clear | **Pass** |
| Ambient conditions | 14 °C, still | — | — |
| Test gauge used | Digital, calibration certificate PG-2026-0118, 11/02/2026 | In calibration | — |

### 8.3 Sealing

The valve adjustment was not altered. The valve was resealed after the test with a lead
seal and wire, **seal number 4471**, applied by the inspector. The seal must not be broken
except by a competent person. A broken seal is evidence that the set pressure may have been
altered, and if a broken seal is found the valve must be removed, reset and recertified
before the boiler is returned to service.

### 8.4 Safety valve history and next action

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 2014 | Supplied and certified with the boiler, set 690 kPa |
| 2019 | Removed, overhauled, reset and recertified by the valve agent |
| 2021 | Checked in place during the refurbishment, no adjustment |
| 2023 | Lift test on steam, popped 698 kPa, reseat 638 kPa |
| 2024 | Lift test on steam, popped 700 kPa, reseat 640 kPa |
| 2025 | Lift test on steam, popped 701 kPa, reseat 639 kPa |
| **2026** | **Lift test on steam, popped 703 kPa, reseat 641 kPa. Passed. Sealed 4471.** |
| **2029** | **Removal, overhaul, reset and recertification by the valve agent is recommended, to coincide with the hydrostatic test.** |

The popping pressure has drifted upward by 5 kPa over four years, which is a normal and
very small drift and remains comfortably within tolerance. It is the trend to watch: if the
valve pops above 711 kPa at any future test it fails, and it must then be removed and
overhauled. The 2029 overhaul recommendation is made to keep ahead of that.

---

## 9. Observations and defects

### 9.1 Risk rating system used

| Category | Meaning | Required action |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — Critical** | The item is not fit for continued service. A hazard exists or may exist immediately. | Cease operation immediately. Do not return to service until rectified and re-inspected. |
| **2 — High** | A defect that will become critical if not corrected. | Rectify within 7 days. |
| **3 — Medium** | A defect in a pressure part, fitting or safety-related component that must be corrected but does not presently prevent safe operation. | Rectify within 30 days. |
| **4 — Low** | A defect or deterioration that must be corrected at a planned opportunity. | Rectify at the next shutdown, and in any event by the date stated. |
| **5 — Observation** | A condition, practice or record matter that does not affect fitness for service. | Recommended action, no compliance date. Reviewed at the next inspection. |

**No Category 1 or Category 2 findings were made at this inspection.**

### 9.2 Items requiring action

**Item 1 — Gauge glass lower gland weeping. Category 3. Rectify by 24 July 2026.**

*Finding.* The lower gauge glass fitting is weeping steadily at the packing gland,
producing a drop approximately every 40 seconds at working pressure, running down the
fitting and staining the shell below. The gland nut has been taken up to the end of its
available travel and further tightening will not stop the weep; the packing is spent.

*Significance.* This is a leak from a pressure retaining joint on a fitting that the
operator relies on to read the water level. It is small and contained today. Left alone,
the packing will continue to degrade, the leak rate will rise, the wetting will accelerate
external corrosion of the fitting and the shell beneath it, and eventually the fitting may
be difficult to isolate without shutting the boiler down at short notice. Steam at 620 kPa
from a failed gland is a burn hazard to anyone standing at the gauge glass, which is
exactly where the operator stands each morning.

*Required action.* Isolate, depressurise and repack the lower gauge glass gland with the
correct grade of packing. While the fitting is apart, renew the glass and both gaskets,
prove the connection clear, and check the ball check operates. On return to service, blow
the gauge down, confirm the water returns and settles within 5 seconds, and confirm the
gland is dry at working pressure.

*Required by.* **24 July 2026** — 30 days from the date of inspection.

*Evidence required.* The repair must be recorded in the plant maintenance record with the
date, the person who carried out the work, and the parts used. That record will be sighted
at the next inspection. Photographic evidence of the dry gland at working pressure emailed
to this office will close the item out earlier.

*Competency.* This work may be carried out by a competent maintenance person or by the
boiler service contractor. It is not work that requires a pressure equipment inspector.

---

**Item 2 — Bottom blowdown valve packing worn. Category 4. Rectify at the next shutdown
and in any event by 30 November 2026.**

*Finding.* The slow opening screw-down blowdown valve shows wear in the gland packing. The
gland nut is near the end of its travel, and a trace of moisture appears at the gland
after the valve is operated, although the valve seals on its seat and is dry between
operations. The light surface oxidation on the lower shell adjacent this connection,
noted at 6.1, is the historical residue of this condition.

*Significance.* The blowdown valve is operated under full boiler pressure once every
operating day. Its gland is a pressure retaining joint that is worked hard, and it is
adjacent the operator's hands during the blowdown. Packing that is at the end of its
adjustment will begin to pass, first as a wisp during operation and then as a continuous
weep. Blowdown valve glands do not fail gracefully. This item is rated Category 4 rather
than Category 3 because the valve currently seals, the weep is intermittent and only on
operation, and the work is properly done with the boiler cold and depressurised rather
than as an emergency.

*Required action.* At the next planned shutdown, isolate and depressurise the boiler, and
replace the gland packing in the slow opening blowdown valve. Inspect the valve seat and
spindle while apart; if the seat is wire-drawn or the spindle is scored, replace the valve
rather than repack it. Clean back the surface oxidation on the shell adjacent the blowdown
connection to bare metal, verify by probe that there is no pitting, and re-paint with a
suitable high temperature coating.

*Required by.* **30 November 2026.** The operator has advised that a plant shutdown is
planned for the second week of October 2026, which is a suitable opportunity and would
close this item well within time.

*Evidence required.* Maintenance record with date, person, parts and a note of the seat
and spindle condition found.
