documents.title: Boiler inspection report — Observations, Operator competency and log review, Conclusion
documents.background: The annual AS 3788 external inspection, carried out 24 June 2026 by Goldfields Plant Inspection. Registration VIC-PV-118-4470 expires 30 June 2027. Two items need action — the gauge glass gland and the blowdown valve packing — and the report notes gaps in our daily logs in May.
documents.text:
### 9.3 Observations

The following are recorded as Category 5 observations. None affects fitness for service.
Each will be reviewed at the next external inspection.

**Observation 3 — Steam header lagging incomplete.** Approximately 400 mm of lagging is
missing from the steam header immediately downstream of the crown valve, apparently
removed during a past valve repair and not replaced. Bare pipe at approximately 165 °C is
a contact burn hazard at head height near the boiler house doorway, and it is a continuous
heat loss into a space that does not need it. *Recommended:* re-lag with a removable
insulation blanket so it can be taken off for future valve work and put back.

**Observation 4 — Hotwell thermometer missing.** The pocket is fitted at the hotwell
outlet but no thermometer is installed. The operator has no way of confirming feedwater
temperature, which is the first defence against dissolved oxygen corrosion. Feedwater
temperature measured 82 °C on the day with the inspector's instrument, which is correct.
*Recommended:* fit a 0 to 120 °C dial thermometer in the existing pocket and add the
reading to the daily log.

**Observation 5 — Light corrosion staining on the burner front plate.** Superficial rust
staining is present on the burner front plate below the gas train, consistent with
condensate dripping from the gas train during cold starts in winter. No perforation, no
loss of section, no effect on the pressure envelope. *Recommended:* clean back and touch
up at the next service; monitor.

**Observation 6 — Boiler house lighting.** Illuminance measured at approximately 90 lux at
the gauge glass. The operator reads a water level and performs level control tests at this
position daily. *Recommended:* increase to at least 200 lux at the gauge glass and at the
control panel, by adding a luminaire or relocating the existing one.

**Observation 7 — Flue cap discolouration.** Light brown discolouration at the flue
terminal and immediately below it at the roof penetration, consistent with normal
weathering and cold-end condensate on a daily-cycling boiler. No perforation. *Recommended:*
examine again at the 2027 external inspection; if the discolouration has spread or any
perforation is evident, replace the terminal section.

**Observation 8 — Daily operating log gaps in May 2026.** Three operating days in May 2026
have no log entry — 13 May, 14 May and 27 May 2026. Discussed in full at Section 11.
*Recommended:* the actions at 11.4.

**Observation 9 — Chemical labelling and safety data sheets.** The label on the chemical
dosing pot has faded to the point that the product name is not legible from the operating
position, and the safety data sheet folder in the boiler house holds a superseded revision
for the oxygen scavenger. *Recommended:* re-label the dosing pot and obtain current safety
data sheets from the water treatment supplier at the next service.

**Observation 10 — Boiler house door wedged open.** A wooden wedge was in use holding the
boiler house door open at the time of inspection. The door is a fire and smoke separation
between the boiler house and the production floor. *Recommended:* remove the wedge. If
airflow is the reason the door is being held open, review the boiler house ventilation
with the operator rather than defeating the door.

**Observation 11 — No critical spares held on site.** No spare gauge glass, gasket set,
gland packing or level probe is held. A gauge glass failure at 07:00 on a Monday stops the
whole finishing line until a part can be obtained from Melbourne. *Recommended:* hold on
site a spare gauge glass and gasket set, a roll of the correct gland packing, a spare
level probe and a spare UV scanner. The total cost is small against the cost of a day of
lost production.

**Observation 12 — Total dissolved solids trending upward.** Boiler water TDS has risen
from 2,240 ppm in February 2026 to 2,980 ppm at this inspection, against an upper limit of
3,500 ppm. The result is within limits and no action is required to remain compliant, but
the trend is one directional across five months and it will reach the limit on its present
slope during the spring peak, when firing hours are highest. *Recommended:* increase the
frequency of surface blowdown, review the makeup rate against the condensate return, and
have the water treatment supplier check for a fall in condensate return or an increase in
makeup at the October service.

**Observation 13 — No standby feedwater pump.** A single feedwater pump is fitted. Failure
of that pump stops the boiler and therefore the whole finishing line. This is a business
continuity observation rather than a safety observation; the low water protection will
shut the boiler down safely if the pump fails. *Recommended:* hold a spare pump or pump
head on site, or arrange a same-day supply agreement with the pump supplier.

**Observation 14 — Ultrasonic thickness test locations not permanently marked.** The
thickness test locations were marked with paint at previous inspections and some marks
have weathered. Reliable trend data depends on measuring the same points each time.
*Recommended:* the locations were re-marked with weather resistant paint and numbered
during this inspection; leave the marks in place and do not paint over them.

### 9.4 Close-out of items from the previous report

| Ref | Item raised in GPIS-2025-0974 | Status at this inspection |
|---|---|---|
| 2025/1 | Leaking union on the chemical dosing line, Category 3, required by 26/07/2025 | **Closed.** Union replaced 09/07/2025, maintenance record sighted, joint dry on inspection. |
| 2025/2 | Pressure gauge reading approximately 20 kPa high, Category 3, required by 26/07/2025 | **Closed.** Gauge replaced 15/07/2025 with a new 100 mm gauge and siphon; verified against the test gauge at three points during this inspection and accurate within 5 kPa. |
| 2025/3 | Observation — hotwell insulation damaged at the lid | **Closed.** Lid insulation replaced. |
| 2025/4 | Observation — no spares held on site | **Not closed.** Repeated at observation 11. |

---

## 10. Water treatment review

### 10.1 Arrangement

Water treatment is under a service contract with Castlemaine Industrial Water Pty Ltd,
contract CIW-4412, comprising a monthly attendance, on-site testing, chemical supply, a
written service report each visit, and an annual system review. **The contract expires on
31 October 2026** and requires 30 days' notice to renew or terminate.

The treatment programme is a conventional phosphate and alkalinity programme with sodium
sulphite as the oxygen scavenger and an amine for condensate line protection, fed
continuously by dosing pump into the feed line, with softened makeup and a manual surface
blowdown for total dissolved solids control.

The operator performs a daily boiler water test for total dissolved solids and alkalinity
and records the result in the log. The supplier performs the full suite monthly.

### 10.2 Results measured at this inspection, 24 June 2026

**Boiler water** — sample drawn from the sample cock after purging, cooled in a stainless
sample cooler.

| Parameter | Limit for this boiler | Result 24/06/2026 | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| pH at 25 °C | 10.5 to 11.8 | **11.2** | Within limits, mid-range, good |
| Total alkalinity as CaCO3 | 300 to 700 ppm | **480 ppm** | Within limits |
| Caustic (hydroxide) alkalinity as CaCO3 | 200 to 400 ppm | **265 ppm** | Within limits |
| Total dissolved solids | Not more than 3,500 ppm | **2,980 ppm** | Within limits; rising trend, see observation 12 |
| Chloride | Not more than 300 ppm | **214 ppm** | Within limits |
| Sulphite reserve | 30 to 70 ppm | **44 ppm** | Within limits, good scavenger residual |
| Phosphate as PO4 | 20 to 50 ppm | **31 ppm** | Within limits |
| Total hardness | Nil | **Nil** | Correct |
| Suspended solids | Not more than 200 ppm | **65 ppm** | Within limits, clean |
| Appearance | Clear, no oil | Clear, no oil, no odour | Correct |

**Feedwater** — sample drawn at the hotwell outlet.

| Parameter | Limit | Result 24/06/2026 | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| pH at 25 °C | 8.3 to 9.5 | **8.8** | Within limits |
| Total hardness as CaCO3 | Not more than 2 ppm | **2 ppm** | **At the limit.** See 10.4 |
| Dissolved oxygen | Not more than 0.10 ppm | **0.06 ppm** | Within limits |
| Temperature | Not less than 80 °C | **82 °C** | Within limits |
| Conductivity | Not more than 400 µS/cm | **310 µS/cm** | Within limits |
| Iron | Not more than 0.10 ppm | **0.04 ppm** | Within limits, low |

**Condensate** — sample drawn at the return line into the hotwell.

| Parameter | Limit | Result 24/06/2026 | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| pH at 25 °C | 8.0 to 9.0 | **8.4** | Within limits |
| Iron | Not more than 0.10 ppm | **0.03 ppm** | Within limits, indicates the amine programme is working |
| Conductivity | Not more than 30 µS/cm | **18 µS/cm** | Within limits, no contamination |
| Condensate return as a proportion of feedwater | Target not less than 50% | **54%** | Acceptable |

### 10.3 Twelve month trend

| Parameter | Aug 25 | Nov 25 | Feb 26 | May 26 | Jun 26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boiler water pH | 11.4 | 11.3 | 11.1 | 11.2 | 11.2 |
| Boiler water TDS, ppm | 2,410 | 2,180 | 2,240 | 2,760 | **2,980** |
| Total alkalinity, ppm | 520 | 495 | 460 | 470 | 480 |
| Sulphite reserve, ppm | 51 | 38 | 46 | 41 | 44 |
| Phosphate, ppm | 34 | 29 | 33 | 28 | 31 |
| Feedwater hardness, ppm | Nil | Nil | 1 | 2 | **2** |
| Condensate return, % | 58 | 57 | 56 | 55 | 54 |

Two trends are visible and they are related. Feedwater hardness has moved from nil to 2
ppm over five months, and boiler water total dissolved solids has risen by a third over
the same period while condensate return has slipped by four percentage points. More
makeup water, with a trace of hardness slipping through the softener, is the most likely
explanation for both.

### 10.4 Assessment and recommendations

Boiler water chemistry is **compliant**. Every parameter is within limits, the scavenger
residual is healthy, the phosphate residual is adequate, the suspended solids are low, and
the condensate iron is very low. The waterside condition found at the 2024 internal
inspection was consistent with a well run programme and there is nothing in this year's
results to change that view.

Two matters are recommended for attention, neither of which is a defect:

1. **Feedwater hardness at the limit.** A hardness of 2 ppm is at the limit and it was nil
   six months ago. Hardness in the feedwater is what forms scale on the heat transfer
   surfaces, and scale is what turns a clean boiler into a fuel-wasting boiler and then
   into an overheated one. The softener should be checked for resin exhaustion or fouling,
   the brine draw and the regeneration timing verified, and a hardness test performed
   immediately after a regeneration to confirm the softener is producing nil hardness when
   freshly regenerated. This should be done at the next monthly service.
2. **Rising total dissolved solids.** See observation 12. Increase surface blowdown
   frequency and investigate the fall in condensate return. A four point fall in condensate
   return means more cold makeup, more chemical, more blowdown and more gas.

The daily operator tests are being performed and recorded, other than on the three days
discussed at Section 11. The daily results recorded by the operator agree closely with the
inspector's results on the day, which indicates the operator is testing correctly and the
reagents are in date.

---

## 11. Operator competency and log review

### 11.1 Attendance category

The boiler is operated under **AS 2593 limited attendance, category LA-24**. In practice
that means the boiler may operate without a person in continuous attendance, provided that
a competent person carries out and records the prescribed checks and tests at intervals
not exceeding 24 hours, and provided the safety devices that make unattended operation
possible are in place, tested and functional.

The safety devices that support this category — two independent low water devices, the low
water cut-out with manual reset, the high pressure limit with manual reset, the flame
safeguard with lockout, and the valve proving system — were all tested at this inspection
and all passed. See Section 7 and Appendix B.

The attendance category is confirmed for the coming year. It is confirmed on the basis
that the daily check regime is performed and recorded. That is the condition on which
unattended operation rests, and it is the reason the log gaps at 11.3 matter.

### 11.2 Operator competency

| Person | Role | Competency | Evidence sighted | Expiry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Peter Nguyen | Plant operator, primary boiler attendant | Standard boiler operation (high risk work), class BS | Licence card sighted, No. HRW 2214887 | 12/03/2029 |
| Marco Rossi | Presser and finisher, secondary boiler attendant | Standard boiler operation (high risk work), class BS | Licence card sighted, No. HRW 2331904 | 05/08/2027 |
| Karen Whitfield | Director, responsible officer | Not an operator; responsible for the management system | — | — |

Two licensed attendants for a single boiler on a five and a half day operation is
appropriate. It gives cover for leave and illness without relying on an unlicensed person.

Both attendants were able, when asked, to describe the daily check regime, the correct
blowdown procedure, the action to take on a low water alarm, the action to take on a low
water lockout, and the location and operation of the manual gas isolation and the
emergency stop. Mr Nguyen carried out the gauge glass blowdown and assisted with the level
control tests during the inspection, competently and without prompting.

Formal refresher training was last recorded in March 2024. There is no fixed requirement
for refresher training for this class of licence, but a documented annual refresher — even
a short one run by the boiler service contractor — is good practice and would strengthen
the management system. That is a recommendation, not a finding.

### 11.3 Log review, 1 July 2025 to 24 June 2026

The daily operating log is a bound book kept on the boiler house wall. The prescribed
entries are the date, the time of the check, the steam pressure, the water level observed,
the gauge glass blowdown, the bottom blowdown, the level control test, the boiler water
TDS and alkalinity test results, the chemical dosing pot level, any abnormality, and the
attendant's initials.

**249 operating days fell within the review period. 246 have a complete entry. Three have
no entry at all:**

| Date with no entry | Day | Circumstances established on enquiry |
|---|---|---|
| 13/05/2026 | Wednesday | Primary attendant on leave. Boiler fired and operated by the secondary attendant, who did not complete the log. |
| 14/05/2026 | Thursday | As above. |
| 27/05/2026 | Wednesday | Primary attendant present. Attendant states the checks were performed but the log was not completed on the day and was not back-filled. |

The 246 completed entries are of good quality. They are legible, they are initialled, the
recorded test results are plausible and internally consistent, and abnormalities are
recorded rather than glossed over — there are four entries during the period noting a
level control test that required a second attempt, and one noting a burner lockout on a
cold start that reset and ran normally. A log that records only good news is a log that is
being filled in at the end of the week; this one is not.

### 11.4 What the gaps mean, and what must be done

**What they mean.** Under a limited attendance regime, the log is not paperwork. It is the
evidence that the checks that make unattended operation safe were actually carried out. A
day with no entry is a day on which it cannot be demonstrated that the water level was
observed, that the gauge glass was proved clear, that the level controls were tested, or
that the water chemistry was within limits. On those three days in May 2026 the boiler
operated at 620 kPa with no record that anyone confirmed it was safe to do so.

Three gaps in 249 days is a lapse, not a systemic failure, and no harm resulted — the
boiler was in sound condition before and after, the water chemistry either side of the
gaps was within limits, and no abnormality was recorded on the surrounding days. It is
recorded here as an observation and not as a defect for that reason.

But it is a lapse with three specific consequences the operator should understand:

1. **Regulatory.** The obligation to keep the records is a condition of operating a
   registered boiler under a limited attendance regime. A regulator reviewing this log
   after an incident would treat a gap as a failure of the safety management system, not
   as an administrative oversight.
2. **Insurance.** The machinery breakdown cover on this boiler is conditional on the
   operating records being kept and produced on request. A claim for boiler damage
   following a low water event on a day with no log entry would be difficult to sustain.
3. **Practical.** The gap conceals information. If the boiler had been fired hard on 13
   and 14 May with a level control drifting, nobody would know, because nobody wrote
   anything down.

**Required response.** This is an observation and carries no compliance date, but the
following is expected to be in place at the next inspection:

- a short written procedure stating that the boiler is not to be fired on any day on which
  the daily check regime has not been completed and recorded, signed by the responsible
  officer;
- a documented handover step for use when the primary attendant is on leave, so that the
  secondary attendant knows the log is theirs for the period;
- a weekly review of the log by the responsible officer or the shop manager, initialled, so
  that a gap is found within days rather than at the annual inspection; and
- a note in the log at each of the three gap dates recording that no entry was made, why,
  and what was done about it. Gaps are not to be back-filled with invented readings, which
  would be far worse than the gap itself.

---

## 12. Conclusion and certification

### 12.1 Conclusion

The Fulton FB-030 vertical gas fired steam boiler, serial FB030-2014-3312, registration
VIC-PV-118-4470, installed at Shop 4, 118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo, was subjected to an
external in-service inspection on 24 June 2026 in accordance with AS 3788.

The pressure envelope is in sound condition. No wastage of consequence was found; the
lowest recorded shell thickness of 10.1 mm is well above the minimum required 8.6 mm, and
there is no measurable loss against the 2024 datum. The 2021 furnace repair weld is sound
on magnetic particle examination of its accessible length. All mountings, fittings and
connections are correct, of the right rating, and serviceable. The safety valve lifted at
703 kPa, passed cleanly and reseated at 641 kPa, all within tolerance, and has been
resealed. Every safety device fitted was tested and every device passed. Boiler water and
feedwater chemistry are within limits. The gas train and flue are sound and combustion is
clean and efficient.

Two defects were found, neither of which prevents continued safe operation: a weeping
gauge glass gland requiring repacking within 30 days, and worn blowdown valve packing
requiring replacement at the next shutdown. Twelve observations were recorded, of which
the most significant are the three gaps in the daily operating log in May 2026 and the
upward trend in boiler water total dissolved solids.

The boiler inspection report, fourth of five parts: the twelve observations, the water treatment review, the operator and log review, and the conclusion.
Fulton FB-030, serial FB030-2014-3312, registration VIC-PV-118-4470, inspected 24 June 2026 under AS 3788.
Observations 3 to 14 are all Category 5 with no compliance date, reviewed at the next inspection: missing steam header lagging; no hotwell thermometer; burner front plate staining; lighting only 90 lux at the gauge glass against 200; flue cap discolouration; three log gaps in May 2026; faded dosing pot label; boiler house door wedged open; no critical spares on site; rising dissolved solids; no standby feedwater pump.
The two 2025 defects are closed out; the 2025 observation about spares is not.
Water treatment is under contract CIW-4412 with Castlemaine Industrial Water Pty Ltd, monthly attendance. It expires on 31 October 2026 and needs 30 days' notice to renew or terminate.
Boiler water compliant on 24 June 2026: pH 11.2 (limit 10.5 to 11.8), alkalinity 480 ppm, total dissolved solids 2,980 ppm against a 3,500 ppm limit, nil hardness. Feedwater hardness 2 ppm — at the limit and up from nil six months ago, so have the softener checked at the next monthly service.
Operators, both licensed for standard boiler operation: Peter Nguyen, HRW 2214887, expires 12 March 2029; Marco Rossi, HRW 2331904, expires 5 August 2027.
Log review 1 July 2025 to 24 June 2026: of 249 operating days, 246 have a complete entry; no entry on 13, 14 and 27 May 2026. Under AS 2593 limited attendance the log is the evidence the checks were done, and a gap could defeat a machinery breakdown claim. Gaps are not to be back-filled.
Conclusion: pressure envelope sound, every safety device passed, chemistry within limits, two defects to rectify.

### 12.2 Certification

I certify that:

1. I am a competent person for the purposes of AS 3788 in respect of this class of
   pressure equipment, and I carried out this inspection personally.
2. The inspection was carried out in accordance with AS 3788, and the standards listed at
   4.3 were applied.
3. The findings recorded in this report are a true record of the condition of the
   equipment as found on 24 June 2026.
4. **In my opinion the pressure equipment is fit for continued service at its registered
   maximum allowable working pressure of 690 kPa, until the next external inspection due on
   24 June 2027, subject to the rectification of items 1 and 2 at Section 9 by the dates
   stated there, and subject to the conditions at Section 13.**

**G. Mattison**
Pressure Equipment Inspector, GPI-INS-114
For and on behalf of Goldfields Plant Inspection Services Pty Ltd
Inspection body accreditation IBA-0374

## 13. Conditions of this certificate

1. This report certifies the condition of the equipment **as found on the date of
   inspection**. It is not a warranty of future condition and it does not guarantee that
   the equipment will remain fit for service until the next inspection.
2. The certification at 12.2 is **conditional on the rectification of items 1 and 2** by
   the dates stated. If either item is not rectified by its date, the certification lapses
   in respect of that item and the equipment should not be operated until it is rectified
   and this office has been notified.
3. The certification is conditional on the equipment continuing to be **operated within
   its registered parameters** — at or below 690 kPa MAWP, on natural gas, at the settings
   recorded at 3.3 — and on the safety devices remaining in place, in service, at their set
   points, and not bypassed, strapped or disabled.
4. The certification is conditional on the **daily check regime being carried out and
   recorded** in accordance with the AS 2593 limited attendance category applied. Operation
   without those records is operation outside the basis of this certificate.
5. The certification is conditional on the **water treatment programme being maintained**
   and the chemistry kept within the limits at 10.2.
6. **Any repair, alteration or modification to a pressure part, to the safety valve, or to
   a safety device must be notified to this office before it is carried out.** A repair to
   a pressure part requires a qualified welder working to a qualified procedure and
   requires assessment by a competent person before the equipment returns to service.
   Adjusting the safety valve set pressure, changing a safety device set point, or breaking
   the safety valve seal, voids this certificate.
7. **If the equipment is subjected to an abnormal condition** — a low water event, an
   overpressure event, a furnace overheat, a fire, an impact, or an operation of the low
   water cut-out that is not a test — it must be taken out of service and inspected by a
   competent person before it is returned to service, whatever the date of the next
   scheduled inspection.
8. **If the equipment is relocated, sold, or the registration holder changes**, the
   regulator must be notified and the plant records, including this report, must go with
   the equipment.
9. This report is issued to the owner named at the head of it. It may be given to the
   regulator, to an insurer, to a purchaser and to a service contractor. It may not be
   reproduced in part in a way that alters its meaning.
10. Nothing in this report relieves the owner of any duty imposed on it by law. Where a
    requirement of this report conflicts with a requirement of the regulator, the
    regulator's requirement applies.
11. This office should be contacted if the owner is uncertain about any finding, any
    required action, or any date in this report. There is no charge for that advice.

---

| B16 | Pre-purge | Timer | 30 s | 30 s | Full purge before ignition | 30 s at purge rate | Pass |
| B17 | Post-purge | Timer | 15 s | 15 s | Purge after shutdown | 15 s | Pass |
| B18 | Emergency stop | Mushroom head, external to boiler house | — | — | Isolate burner and fan | Burner and fan isolated, manual reset required | Pass |
| B19 | Gas train tightness | Leak detection fluid, all joints | — | — | No leakage | No leakage at any joint | Pass |
| B20 | Safety valve easing lever | Manual | — | Lifted at 600 kPa | Free operation, clean reseat | Lifted and reseated cleanly | Pass |

**Operator monthly test obligations.** Between annual inspections the operator must test
and record: the gauge glass blowdown, daily; the level control operation, daily; the low
water alarm, weekly; the low water cut-out by controlled evaporation, monthly; and the
safety valve easing lever, monthly. The last operator low water cut-out test before this
inspection was recorded on 5 June 2026 and was satisfactory.

---

## Appendix C — Photographic record

Twenty-one photographs were taken during the inspection. They are held on the inspection
body's file against report GPIS-2026-1188 and a full set has been provided to the owner
electronically. They are described below so that this report remains meaningful as a text
record and so that the next inspector knows what was photographed and from where.

**C1 — General arrangement, boiler house, from the doorway.** The boiler stands centrally
on its plinth with the control panel on the left hand side at eye height and the flue
rising vertically at the rear right. The gauge glass, pressure gauge and level control
chamber are all visible from this position. Clearance around the boiler is evident. The
wooden door wedge that is the subject of observation 10 is visible at the bottom left of
the frame.

**C2 — Nameplate.** Close photograph of the stainless nameplate on the front casing,
legible, showing make, model FB-030, serial FB030-2014-3312, year 2014 and MAWP 690 kPa.

**C3 — Registration certificate as displayed.** The laminated registration certificate
VIC-PV-118-4470 on the boiler house wall, showing the expiry date of 30 June 2027.

**C4 — Shell, right side, casing removed.** The bare shell over its mid height showing an
intact paint system, no distortion and no corrosion. Thickness test locations 4 and 5 are
visible as numbered paint marks.

**C5 — Lower shell adjacent the blowdown connection.** The area of light surface oxidation
described at 6.1, photographed before cleaning, with a scale rule in frame. The extent is
approximately 120 mm by 80 mm.

**C6 — The same area after wire brushing.** Sound metal beneath, no pitting, no loss of
section. Taken to establish the datum for the 2027 comparison.

**C7 — Gauge glass, general.** The reflex gauge glass in its frame with the normal water
level mark visible and the water line clearly readable.

**C8 — Gauge glass lower gland, close.** Item 1. The weep at the lower packing nut is
visible as a bead of moisture at the gland with a run mark down the fitting below. The
gland nut can be seen to be near the end of its travel. This is the key evidential
photograph for item 1.

**C9 — Shell staining below the gauge glass, before cleaning.** The mineral residue trail
from the weep, running approximately 200 mm down the shell.

**C10 — The same area after cleaning.** Cleaned back so that any staining seen in 2027 is
new staining.

**C11 — Blowdown valve arrangement.** Both blowdown valves in series, the quick opening
lever valve at the boiler and the slow opening screw-down valve downstream, with the line
falling away to the blowdown vessel.

**C12 — Slow opening blowdown valve gland, close.** Item 2. The gland nut is visible near
the end of its travel with a trace of moisture at the gland after operation.

**C13 — Safety valve installation.** The valve mounted vertically on its full bore branch
on the top head, with no isolating valve between the boiler and the valve, the discharge
pipe rising and independently supported, and the drain at the low point.

**C14 — Safety valve seal after test.** Close photograph of the new lead seal and wire,
seal number 4471, legible.

**C15 — Level control chamber.** The side-mounted chamber with both isolating cocks
padlocked open and the probe head assembly in place.

**C16 — Level probe tips withdrawn.** The three tip probe assembly on a clean bench, tips
clean with a light even oxide, no scale bridging, no erosion.

**C17 — Gas train.** The full train from the manual cock through the filter, regulator,
pressure switches and the two safety shut-off valves, showing the 2021 installation and
its labelling.

**C18 — Burner head withdrawn.** The burner head and diffuser clean and undistorted, with
the ignition electrodes correctly gapped and the UV scanner sight tube clear.

**C19 — Furnace throat and the 2021 repair weld.** Taken through the burner opening. The
repair weld cap is visible with a smooth profile blending into the parent metal. Light
surface craze in the refractory is visible and is normal.

**C20 — Magnetic particle examination in progress on the repair weld.** Contrast paint and
ink applied over the accessible 340 mm of weld length, no indication present.

**C21 — Flue terminal from the roof.** The cowl and the roof penetration flashing, showing
the light brown discolouration described at observation 7 and the intact flashing, with the
parapet in frame to show that the terminal is clear of it.

---

documents.text:
# Solvent, Process Chemistry and Waste Removal Supply Agreement

**Agreement number:** SVX-2024-0318
**Supplier:** Solvex Chemicals Australia Pty Ltd
**Customer:** Aveline Holdings Pty Ltd trading as Main Street Dry Cleaners
**Commenced:** 1 April 2024
**Initial term:** 3 years, expiring 31 March 2027, then rolling 12 months
**Price schedule in force:** Schedule B, effective 1 April 2026

---

## 1. Parties, recitals, term and renewal

### 1.1 Parties

This Agreement is made between:

**Solvex Chemicals Australia Pty Ltd** ABN 88 104 552 719 of 6 Bridge Road,
Campbellfield VIC 3061 (**the Supplier**); and

**Aveline Holdings Pty Ltd** ACN 617 903 558, ABN 42 617 903 558, of Shop 4,
118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo VIC 3550, trading as Main Street Dry Cleaners
(**the Customer**).

### 1.2 Recitals

A. The Supplier formulates, imports and distributes dry cleaning solvents,
process chemistry and ancillary consumables to the textile care industry in
Victoria, and arranges the removal of prescribed industrial waste generated by
its customers through a permissioned transporter.

B. The Customer operates a dry cleaning plant at Shop 4, 118 Hargreaves Street,
Bendigo VIC 3550 (**the Site**), which houses a perchloroethylene dry cleaning
machine, a hydrocarbon dry cleaning machine, a solvent recovery still, wet
cleaning equipment and a bunded solvent store.

C. The Customer wishes to appoint the Supplier as its supplier of solvent and
process chemistry, and to have the Supplier arrange removal of the prescribed
industrial waste generated at the Site, and the Supplier is willing to do so on
the terms set out below.

### 1.3 Term

This Agreement commenced on 1 April 2024 and continues for an initial term of
three years, expiring on 31 March 2027 (**the Initial Term**), unless terminated
earlier under clause 9.

### 1.4 Renewal

At the end of the Initial Term this Agreement continues automatically for
successive rolling periods of twelve months on the same terms, as varied by any
price schedule then in force, unless either party gives written notice of
termination under clause 9.1. No further act of either party is needed to effect
a rolling renewal.

### 1.5 Exclusivity

For so long as this Agreement is on foot the Customer must purchase all of its
requirements for perchloroethylene, hydrocarbon solvent, charge soap, sizing and
spotting chemistry from the Supplier, other than incidental quantities purchased
in an emergency where the Supplier has confirmed in writing that it cannot
supply within the required time.

---

## 2. Definitions

**ADG Code** means the Australian Code for the Transport of Dangerous Goods by
Road & Rail, Edition 7.9, as amended or replaced.

**Business Day** means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday
observed in Bendigo, Victoria.

**Collection** means an attendance at the Site by the Waste Contractor to remove
Prescribed Industrial Waste under clause 5.

**CPI** means the Consumer Price Index, All Groups, Melbourne, published by the
Australian Bureau of Statistics.

**Dangerous Goods** has the meaning given in the Dangerous Goods Act 1985 (Vic)
and the Dangerous Goods (Storage and Handling) Regulations 2022 (Vic).

**Goods** means the solvents, process chemistry, filtration media, still bags,
personal protective equipment and other products supplied by the Supplier under
this Agreement.

**Order Acknowledgement** means the written confirmation issued by the Supplier
accepting an order, stating the lines, quantities, prices and delivery date.

**PIW** or **Prescribed Industrial Waste** means industrial waste that is
prescribed as such under the Environment Protection Act 2017 (Vic) and the
Environment Protection Regulations 2021 (Vic), including reportable priority
waste.

**Price Schedule** means the schedule of prices in force from time to time under
clause 4, the current version being Schedule B effective 1 April 2026.

**SDS** means a Safety Data Sheet prepared in accordance with the Code of
Practice for the Preparation of Safety Data Sheets for Hazardous Chemicals.

**Site** means Shop 4, 118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo VIC 3550, including the
rear laneway access off Bath Lane.

**Trained Receiver** means a person nominated by the Customer under clause 3.7
who has been trained to receive, check and place a consignment of Dangerous
Goods and to respond to a spill.

**Waste Contractor** means Sovereign Environmental Services Pty Ltd, or such
other EPA permissioned transporter as the Supplier may appoint under clause 5.2.

**Waste Transport Certificate** means the transport record required for the
transport of reportable priority waste under the Environment Protection
Regulations 2021 (Vic), whether created in the EPA waste tracking system or in
any successor system.

---

## 3. Supply obligations

### 3.1 Ordering

The Customer may place orders by telephone to the Supplier's Campbellfield order
desk, by email to orders@solvexchemicals.com.au, or through the Supplier's
online account portal. Each order must state the Agreement number
SVX-2024-0318, the product code and description, the quantity, and the name of
the person placing the order. An order is not accepted until the Supplier issues
an Order Acknowledgement.

The Customer must nominate in writing the persons authorised to place orders on
its account. As at the date of Schedule B the authorised persons are Karen
Whitfield, Nadia Farrell and Peter Nguyen. The Supplier may accept an order from
any person who identifies themselves as one of the authorised persons and is not
obliged to verify their authority.

### 3.2 Lead times

The Supplier will deliver stock lines within five Business Days of accepting an
order for delivery to Bendigo and surrounding districts. Non-stock lines,
including special order spotting chemistry, non-standard filtration media and
any product identified in the Price Schedule as indent, will be delivered within
ten Business Days of order acceptance.

Lead times run from acceptance, not from the placing of the order, and do not
run while an account is suspended under clause 7.4.

### 3.3 Minimum order

The Customer must purchase not less than four 200 L drums of perchloroethylene
in each twelve month period commencing 1 April. If in any such period the
Customer purchases fewer than four drums, the Supplier may invoice the Customer
for the shortfall at the drum price then in force, and the Customer must pay
that invoice on the ordinary terms. Drums purchased in excess of four in a
period do not carry forward.

The minimum order value for any single delivery is $250 excluding GST. Orders
below that value will be held and consolidated with the next order unless the
Customer asks for immediate delivery and pays the delivery fee set out in the
Price Schedule.

### 3.4 Delivery windows

Deliveries to the Site are made to the rear laneway off Bath Lane between 7:00
and 12:00 on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The Customer must ensure the laneway is
clear of vehicles and stock, and that a Trained Receiver is present for the
whole of the nominated window. Where the Supplier attends within the window and
cannot deliver, a failed delivery fee applies.

Deliveries outside the standard windows may be arranged by agreement and attract
the out-of-window fee in the Price Schedule. The Supplier does not deliver
solvent to the Site during retail trading hours on a Saturday.

### 3.5 Title and risk

Risk in the Goods passes to the Customer on the Goods being unloaded at the
Site. Title in the Goods does not pass until the Supplier has received payment
in full of all amounts owing by the Customer on any account. Until title passes
the Customer holds the Goods as bailee, must store them so that they are
identifiable as the Supplier's property, and the Supplier may enter the Site
during trading hours on reasonable notice to recover them.

This clause creates a security interest for the purposes of the Personal
Property Securities Act 2009 (Cth) and the Customer consents to the Supplier
registering that interest on the Personal Property Securities Register.

### 3.6 Dangerous goods delivery

Perchloroethylene is consigned as UN 1897, TETRACHLOROETHYLENE, Class 6.1,
Packing Group III. Amyl acetate is consigned as UN 1104, AMYL ACETATES, Class 3,
Packing Group III. Hydrocarbon solvent is a C1 combustible liquid under AS 1940
and is not a dangerous good for transport at the flash point supplied.

The Supplier will:

(a) transport all Dangerous Goods in accordance with the ADG Code, in packaging
that is UN performance tested, correctly marked and within its test life;

(b) ensure each vehicle carries the transport documentation, emergency
information and equipment required by the ADG Code for the load carried;

(c) ensure drivers hold the licences and dangerous goods driver competencies
required for the load; and

(d) provide the Customer with the current SDS for each product on or before
first delivery and again on any revision.

### 3.7 Customer's receiving obligations

The Customer must at all times maintain at the Site:

(a) a bunded receiving and storage area for solvent drums, with a bund capacity
of not less than 110% of the largest container stored plus 25% of the aggregate
capacity of all other containers, impervious to the solvents stored, kept free
of accumulated water, and with no drain to sewer or stormwater;

(b) segregation of Class 3 and Class 6.1 goods from incompatible materials in
accordance with the Dangerous Goods (Storage and Handling) Regulations 2022
(Vic);

(c) a Trained Receiver present at each delivery who is competent to check the
consignment against the delivery documentation, to refuse a damaged or leaking
container, to direct the placement of drums, and to respond to a spill; and

(d) spill containment materials sufficient for a 200 L release, and an eyewash
and safety shower within ten seconds' travel of the decanting point.

The Customer confirms that the aggregate quantity of Dangerous Goods held at the
Site is below the placarding quantity for the classes held, and must notify the
Supplier in writing before that ceases to be the case.

The Supplier's driver may refuse to unload if the receiving area is not
compliant, if no Trained Receiver is present, or if unloading cannot be carried
out safely. A refusal on any of those grounds is treated as a failed delivery.

### 3.8 Decanting and transfer

Solvent must be transferred from drum to machine by closed coupling or by a
grounded and bonded pump. The Customer must not decant solvent by gravity into
an open vessel, must not leave a transfer unattended, and must bond the drum and
the receiving vessel before transferring hydrocarbon solvent. Empty drums must
be closed, bung fitted, and returned to the bunded store pending collection.

---

**Container deposits**

A refundable deposit of $180.00 applies to each 200 L solvent drum and $45.00 to
each 20 L process chemistry container. Deposits are credited on return of the
container to the Supplier in sound, closed and drainable condition.

### 4.2 Price review

Prices are reviewed annually with effect from 1 April. The Supplier must give
the Customer written notice of the reviewed prices not less than thirty days
before they take effect. The aggregate increase in the price of any line item at
an annual review must not exceed the increase in CPI for the twelve months to
the December quarter immediately preceding the review, plus three percentage
points.

The perchloroethylene drum price has moved as follows: $1,745.00 from 1 April
2024; $1,798.00 from 1 April 2025; $1,850.00 from 1 April 2026. The next annual
review takes effect 1 April 2027.

### 4.3 Pass-through of raw material and regulatory costs

Outside the annual review, the Supplier may vary the price of any line item on
thirty days' written notice where the variation is attributable to a change in
the landed cost of raw material, a change in freight or fuel cost, a change in
the exchange rate applying to imported product, or a change in a statutory
charge, levy, duty, licence fee or regulatory requirement affecting the product.

A notice under this clause must identify the line items affected, state the new
price and state the reason for the variation. If the aggregate effect of
pass-through variations in any twelve month period exceeds ten per cent of the
price of a line item, the Customer may terminate this Agreement on thirty days'
written notice given within twenty-eight days of the notice that took the
aggregate past ten per cent, and clause 9.1 does not apply to that termination.

### 4.4 Non-stock and indent lines

Non-stock and indent lines are quoted at the time of order and the quoted price
holds for fourteen days. An indent line ordered specially for the Customer may
not be cancelled once the Supplier has placed its own order, and is not
returnable except for a manufacturing fault.

---

## 5. Waste removal

### 5.1 Waste covered

The Supplier will arrange the removal from the Site of:

(a) still residue and separator water sludge from the Union XL-800 and the Bowe
MiniStill, classified as reportable priority waste, waste code N220, halogenated
organic solvents and residues;

(b) spent cartridge filters, spin disc cartridges, lint and button trap waste
contaminated with perchloroethylene, waste code N220;

(c) hydrocarbon still residue and spent filtration media from the Realstar
HM-450, waste code N205, non-halogenated organic solvents and residues; and

(d) spent activated carbon from the vapour adsorber, waste code N220.

Contaminated absorbents, rags and used personal protective equipment may be
included in a Collection under waste code N220 where they are packaged
separately and labelled as solid waste.

### 5.2 Subcontracting

The Supplier subcontracts the transport of PIW under this clause to Sovereign
Environmental Services Pty Ltd, an EPA permissioned transporter, and remains
responsible to the Customer for the performance of the Waste Contractor. The
Supplier may substitute another EPA permissioned transporter on written notice
to the Customer.

### 5.3 Packaging and labelling

The Customer must package waste for collection in the Supplier's supplied 200 L
open-head recovery drums or 20 L pails, in each case closed, sealed and not
overfilled beyond 90% of capacity. Each container must carry a durable label
stating the generator's name and address, the description of the waste, the
waste code, the date the container was first filled and the class label required
by the ADG Code.

The Customer must not mix waste streams, must not place free liquid in a
container nominated for solid waste, and must not place any waste in a container
that is corroded, dented at a seam, or missing a closure ring.

### 5.4 Waste Transport Certificates

For each Collection the Waste Contractor will initiate a Waste Transport
Certificate in the EPA waste tracking system. The Customer, as generator, must
verify and confirm the generator section of the certificate, including the waste
code, the quantity, the containers and the destination premises, before the load
leaves the Site.

The Customer must retain a copy of every certificate and must reconcile the
receiving section of each certificate when it is completed by the receiving
premises. The Supplier will provide the Customer with a consolidated
reconciliation of certificates and receipts within fourteen days of the end of
each quarter.

### 5.5 Collection schedule

Scheduled Collections are made quarterly, in the weeks commencing the second
Monday of March, June, September and December, from the rear laneway off Bath
Lane between 7:00 and 12:00.

Where the volume of PIW held at the Site exceeds four 200 L drums, or where any
waste has been held on site for a period approaching the limit permitted without
a permission, the Customer must request an on-call Collection and the Supplier
will attend within five Business Days.

### 5.6 Collection charges

| Item | Price |
|---|---|
| Scheduled quarterly Collection, up to 4 × 200 L drums | $420.00 |
| Each additional 200 L drum on a scheduled Collection | $96.00 |
| Each 20 L pail | $38.00 |
| On-call Collection, up to 4 × 200 L drums | $610.00 |
| Recovery drum supply, each | $88.00 |
| Rejected container handling, each | $145.00 |
| Waste Transport Certificate administration, per load | $46.00 |

### 5.7 Duty of care and non-delegable obligations

The Customer acknowledges that it is the generator of the waste for the purposes
of the Environment Protection Act 2017 (Vic), that it owes a general
environmental duty under that Act, and that its obligations as generator are not
transferred, shared or discharged by this Agreement or by any act of the
Supplier or the Waste Contractor.

Without limiting that acknowledgement, the Customer remains solely responsible
for correctly classifying the waste it produces, for accurately describing it,
for confirming the generator section of each Waste Transport Certificate, for
storing waste lawfully pending collection, and for reporting any spill, escape
or unlawful deposit at the Site.

The Supplier may refuse to accept a container for Collection where the contents
do not match the description given, where the container is unfit, or where
acceptance would place the Waste Contractor in breach of its permission. A
refusal on any of those grounds attracts the rejected container handling fee and
the container remains the Customer's responsibility.

### 5.8 Records

The Customer must keep records of the waste generated, stored and removed from
the Site, including copies of all Waste Transport Certificates and receiving
premises confirmations, for not less than three years. The Supplier will retain
its own copies for seven years and will provide copies to the Customer on
request within ten Business Days. A summary of the last four Collections is at
Annexure 2.

---

## 6. Safety and compliance

### 6.1 Safety Data Sheets

The Supplier will provide the current SDS for each product on or before first
supply, on each revision, and at any time on request. No SDS supplied under this
Agreement will be more than five years old at the date of supply.

### 6.2 Chemical register

The Customer must maintain a register of all hazardous chemicals held at the
Site, listing the product, the hazard classification, the maximum quantity held,
the location and the SDS revision date, and must keep the register readily
accessible to workers and to emergency services. The register current as at the
date of Schedule B is at Annexure 1.

### 6.3 Training

The Customer must ensure that every worker who handles, decants, receives or
disposes of the Goods has been trained in the hazards of the product, the
control measures, the use of personal protective equipment and the spill and
emergency procedures, and that records of that training are kept. The Supplier
will provide one product handling refresher session at the Site each year at no
charge.

### 6.4 Incident notification

The Customer must notify the Supplier by telephone within two hours, and in
writing within twenty-four hours, of any spill, escape, fire, exposure or
near-miss at the Site involving the Goods or the waste, and of any notice,
direction or infringement issued to the Customer by EPA Victoria or WorkSafe
Victoria that relates to the Goods, the waste or their storage.

### 6.5 Emergency response

The Supplier maintains a 24 hour technical emergency line on 1800 SOLVEX for
advice on spill, exposure and fire involving its products. The Customer must
keep the current SDS and the emergency information holder at the Bath Lane entry
so that they are accessible to emergency services without entering the plant.

### 6.6 Product stewardship

The Supplier will accept the return of unopened Goods that are within date and
in saleable condition, will accept the return of empty containers supplied by
it, and will manage returned product and containers through a licensed
reprocessing or disposal route. The Supplier will notify the Customer of any
change in a product's classification, formulation or regulatory status that
affects the way the Customer must store, use or dispose of it.

### 6.7 Storage audit

The Supplier may audit the Customer's storage, decanting and waste holding
arrangements once in each twelve month period on ten Business Days' notice, and
at any time following an incident notified under clause 6.4.

If an audit finds the arrangements non-compliant, the Supplier will give the
Customer written notice of the findings and a period of not less than
twenty-eight days to rectify them. If the non-compliance is not rectified within
that period, the Supplier may suspend supply of the affected Goods until it is,
and no failure to supply during a suspension under this clause is a breach by
the Supplier. Where the non-compliance presents an immediate risk of harm, the
Supplier may suspend supply immediately and notify the Customer of the reason in
writing within one Business Day.

---

## 7. Payment terms

### 7.1 Invoicing

The Supplier invoices on delivery. Payment is due thirty days from the end of
the month in which the invoice is dated. Payment is to be made by electronic
funds transfer to the account nominated on the invoice, quoting the invoice
number.

### 7.2 GST

All prices exclude GST. GST is payable in addition at the rate applying at the
time of supply and is shown separately on each tax invoice.

### 7.3 Interest on overdue amounts

Interest accrues on any amount not paid by its due date at 1.25% per month,
calculated daily from the due date until payment, and is payable on demand. The
Customer must also pay the Supplier's reasonable costs of recovery, including
mercantile agent fees and legal costs on a solicitor and own client basis.

### 7.4 Suspension of supply

If any amount is more than thirty days overdue, the Supplier may suspend further
supply, including Collections, on written notice until the account is brought
current. The Supplier will continue to accept and process Collections that are
necessary to avoid an immediate environmental risk notwithstanding a suspension,
and may charge for them at the on-call rate.

### 7.5 No set-off

The Customer must pay all amounts due without set-off, counterclaim or deduction
except where a credit note has been issued by the Supplier.

### 7.6 Guarantee

In consideration of the Supplier agreeing to supply on credit, Karen Whitfield
of Bendigo, Victoria, as director of the Customer, guarantees to the Supplier
the due and punctual payment of all amounts owing by the Customer under this
Agreement and indemnifies the Supplier against loss arising from the Customer's
failure to pay. The guarantee is a continuing guarantee, is not discharged by
any variation of the Price Schedule or any indulgence granted to the Customer,
and remains in force until all amounts owing have been paid in full.

---

## 8. Warranties, liability, indemnity and force majeure

### 8.1 Supplier warranties

The Supplier warrants that the Goods will correspond with their description and
specification, will be free from defects in materials and manufacture at the
time risk passes, will be supplied with a current SDS, and will be packaged,
marked and transported in accordance with the ADG Code where applicable.

### 8.2 Customer acknowledgements

The Customer acknowledges that solvent and process chemistry results depend on
machine condition, filtration state, load composition, water quality and
operator technique, and that the Supplier gives no warranty as to cleaning
results, garment outcomes or solvent mileage.

### 8.3 Consumer guarantees

Nothing in this Agreement excludes, restricts or modifies any guarantee, right
or remedy conferred by the Australian Consumer Law that cannot lawfully be
excluded. Where the Supplier's liability may lawfully be limited, it is limited
at the Supplier's option to replacing the Goods, supplying equivalent Goods,
paying the cost of replacing the Goods, or repairing the Goods.

### 8.4 Liability cap

Subject to clause 8.3, the aggregate liability of the Supplier to the Customer
under or in connection with this Agreement in any twelve month period is limited
to the total amount paid by the Customer to the Supplier under this Agreement in
that period. Neither party is liable to the other for loss of profit, loss of
revenue, loss of business opportunity, loss of goodwill or any indirect or
consequential loss.

### 8.5 Indemnity

The Customer indemnifies the Supplier and the Waste Contractor against loss,
damage, liability, penalty and cost arising from the Customer's misdescription
of waste, the Customer's failure to maintain compliant storage or receiving
arrangements, the Customer's breach of clause 5.7, or the act or omission of any
person at the Site other than the Supplier or the Waste Contractor.

### 8.6 Insurance

Each party must maintain public and products liability insurance of not less
than $20,000,000 for any one occurrence, and the Supplier must ensure the Waste
Contractor maintains environmental impairment liability cover appropriate to its
permission. Each party must produce a certificate of currency on request.

### 8.7 Force majeure

Neither party is liable for a failure to perform an obligation, other than an
obligation to pay money, to the extent the failure is caused by an event beyond
its reasonable control, including a supply chain failure affecting solvent
availability, a regulatory prohibition, a natural disaster or a public health
direction. The affected party must notify the other as soon as practicable and
must use reasonable endeavours to resume performance. If the event continues for
more than sixty days, either party may terminate this Agreement on fourteen
days' written notice.

---

## 9. Termination

### 9.1 Termination on notice

Either party may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving the other not
less than sixty days' written notice. A notice given under this clause takes
effect at the end of the sixty day period whether or not the Initial Term has
expired.

### 9.2 Termination for breach

Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the
other party commits a material breach and fails to remedy it within fourteen
days of written notice requiring it to do so, or commits a material breach that
is not capable of remedy, or becomes insolvent, has a controller or
administrator appointed, or resolves to wind up.

### 9.3 Effect of termination

On termination:

(a) all amounts owing to the Supplier become immediately due and payable;

(b) the Customer must pay for all Goods delivered and all Collections performed
before the effective date of termination;

(c) the Customer may retain drums of solvent on hand for which it has paid in
full, and title to those drums passes on payment;

(d) the Supplier will, at the Customer's request and cost, attend the Site
within twenty Business Days of termination to perform a final Collection of all
PIW then held, charged at the on-call rate;

(e) the Customer must return all deposit-bearing containers, whether full or
empty, within thirty days, and the Supplier will credit the deposit for each
container returned in sound, closed and drainable condition. A deposit is
forfeited for any container not returned within that period, or returned
punctured, seam-split, contaminated with a foreign substance or with its closure
ring missing; and

(f) clauses 5.7, 5.8, 6.4, 7.3, 7.6, 8 and 10 survive termination.

---

## 10. Notices and general

### 10.1 Notices

Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, sent by prepaid post, or sent
by email to the addresses below, and are taken to be received on delivery, on
the third Business Day after posting, or on the sending of the email provided no
delivery failure notification is received.

**To the Supplier:** The Contracts Manager, Solvex Chemicals Australia Pty Ltd,

### 10.2 Assignment

Neither party may assign this Agreement without the written consent of the
other, which must not be unreasonably withheld, except that the Supplier may
assign to a related body corporate on notice.

### 10.3 Variation

A variation of this Agreement must be in writing and signed by both parties,
except a variation of the Price Schedule made in accordance with clause 4.

### 10.4 Entire agreement

This Agreement records the entire agreement between the parties about its
subject matter and supersedes all prior arrangements, including the Supplier's
standard trading terms to the extent of any inconsistency.

### 10.5 Confidentiality

Neither party may disclose the pricing in this Agreement to a third party other
than to its professional advisers, its insurer, or as required by law.

### 10.6 Governing law and disputes

This Agreement is governed by the law of Victoria and the parties submit to the
non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Victoria. A party must not commence
proceedings about a dispute under this Agreement, other than for urgent
interlocutory relief, unless it has first given written notice of the dispute
and the parties' representatives have met, in person or by video conference,
within fourteen days of that notice to attempt to resolve it.

# Consumables Supply Agreement and Price List

**Agreement number:** TPS-MSD-2025
**Supplier:** Trentham Packaging & Supply Pty Ltd

**Commenced:** 1 February 2025
**Term:** 2 years, expiring 31 January 2027

## 1. Parties, recitals and term

### 1.1 Parties

This Agreement is made between:

**Trentham Packaging & Supply Pty Ltd** ABN 61 093 887 224 of 22 Enterprise Way,
Bendigo East VIC 3550 (**the Supplier**); and

**Aveline Holdings Pty Ltd** ACN 617 903 558, ABN 42 617 903 558, of Shop 4,
118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo VIC 3550, trading as Main Street Dry Cleaners
(**the Customer**).

### 1.2 Recitals

A. The Supplier is a wholesaler of packaging and consumables to the textile care
and hospitality trades in central Victoria, and holds stock at its Bendigo East
warehouse for next-run delivery.

B. The Customer operates a dry cleaning plant and retail store at Shop 4,
118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo (**the Plant**) and a drop store at Shop 12,
Lansell Square, 233 High Street, Kangaroo Flat (**the Drop Store**).

C. The Customer wishes to appoint the Supplier as its supplier of hangers,
polythene, garment covers, tickets and tags, packaging, press pads and covers
and counter supplies, and the Supplier is willing to supply on the terms below.

### 1.3 Term

This Agreement commenced on 1 February 2025 and continues for two years,
expiring on 31 January 2027. After that date it continues month to month on the
same terms unless terminated under clause 13 or replaced by a further written
agreement.

### 1.4 Scope

This Agreement covers supply to both the Plant and the Drop Store. It does not
cover solvent, process chemistry or waste removal, which the Customer sources
under a separate agreement with another supplier.

---

## 2. Definitions

**Branded Stock** means polythene, gown bags and laundry bags printed with the
Customer's artwork under clause 10.

**Business Day** means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday
observed in Bendigo, Victoria.

**Consignment Stock** means stock delivered to the Plant under clause 11 which
remains the property of the Supplier until drawn down.

**CPI** means the Consumer Price Index, All Groups, Melbourne, published by the
Australian Bureau of Statistics.

**Price List** means the schedule of prices in force from time to time under
clause 4, the current version being List 3 effective 1 February 2026.

**Rebate Year** means the twelve months ending 31 July.

**Standing Order** means the weekly order set out in Annexure A, as varied under
clause 3.1.

**Top-Up Order** means an order placed under clause 3.2 in addition to the
Standing Order.

---

## 3. Supply and ordering

### 3.1 Standing weekly order

The Customer maintains a Standing Order, set out in Annexure A, which the
Supplier picks, invoices and delivers each week without further instruction. The
Standing Order may be varied by the Customer in writing at any time, and a
variation takes effect from the first delivery falling more than two Business
Days after the Supplier receives it.

The Supplier will review the Standing Order with the Customer once each year
before the price review under clause 8, and will recommend changes where the
usage pattern shown by the account no longer matches the Standing Order.

### 3.2 Top-up orders

Top-Up Orders may be placed by telephone, by email to
sales@trenthamsupply.com.au or through the Supplier's trade portal by 15:00 on
the Business Day before the scheduled delivery. Lines held in the Bendigo East
warehouse are delivered on the next scheduled delivery run.

Indent lines, Branded Stock and press covers cut to a machine pattern are quoted
with a lead time when the order is acknowledged, and are ordered subject to
clause 9.2 and clause 10.

### 3.3 Order authority

The persons authorised to order on the account are Karen Whitfield, Nadia
Farrell and Sharon Delaney. The Supplier may accept an order from any person at
either site who identifies as one of the authorised persons and is not obliged
to verify their authority. The Customer must notify the Supplier in writing of
any change to the authorised persons.

### 3.4 Availability and substitution

Where a line is unavailable the Supplier will notify the Customer before
delivery and may substitute an equivalent line at the same or a lower price. A
substitution made without notice may be returned for full credit under
clause 9.1. Where a line is discontinued the Supplier will give the Customer not
less than sixty days' notice and will offer a replacement line and a sample.

### 3.5 Samples

The Supplier will supply a sample of any new or substituted line at no charge on
request. A sample supplied for evaluation remains the property of the Supplier
until the Customer places an order for that line.

## 5. Delivery and freight

### 5.1 Schedule

The Plant is delivered every Wednesday between 8:00 and 11:00 to the rear
laneway off Bath Lane. The Drop Store is delivered fortnightly on Tuesdays
between 9:00 and 11:00 to the centre loading dock at Lansell Square and
trolleyed to the tenancy. Where a scheduled delivery day falls on a public
holiday the delivery is made on the next Business Day.

### 5.2 Freight

Freight is free on orders of $350.00 or more excluding GST. Orders below that
value carry a delivery charge of $28.00. Same-day or after-hours delivery is
$85.00 where the Supplier can meet it. A delivery to the Drop Store outside the
fortnightly run carries the $28.00 charge regardless of order value.

### 5.3 Receipt and shortages

The Customer must check each delivery against the delivery docket at the time of
delivery. Shortages, incorrect lines and visible damage must be noted on the
docket and reported to the Supplier within two Business Days, after which the
delivery is taken to have been accepted as delivered.

### 5.4 Access

The Supplier's driver must not block the Bath Lane roller door for longer than
the delivery requires, and must not leave stock in the laneway unattended. Stock
is placed in the rear store, clear of the solvent store and clear of the
compressor bay.

---

## 6. Minimum order

The minimum value for any order, including a Top-Up Order, is $150.00 excluding
GST. The Standing Order satisfies the minimum for the week in which it is
delivered. Orders below the minimum are held and consolidated with the next
delivery unless the Customer asks for immediate delivery and pays the freight
charge under clause 5.2.

---

## 7. Rebates

### 7.1 Rebate tiers

A rebate is payable on the Customer's total net purchases in each Rebate Year,
calculated on the tiers below and applied to the whole of the annual spend, not
to the excess over each threshold.

| Annual net spend, excluding GST | Rebate |
|---|---|
| Below $12,000 | Nil |
| $12,000 to $17,999 | 1.5% |
| $18,000 to $23,999 | 2.5% |
| $24,000 to $29,999 | 3.5% |
| $30,000 to $39,999 | 5.0% |
| $40,000 and above | 6.0% |

### 7.2 Calculation and payment

The rebate is issued as a credit note against the Customer's account in August
following the end of the Rebate Year. Freight charges, printing set-up charges,
tagging guns and other equipment, and Consignment Stock not yet drawn down are
excluded from the calculation. Credits issued for returns are deducted from net
spend.

No rebate is payable while any amount on the account is more than sixty days
overdue, and a rebate otherwise payable is applied first against any overdue
amount.

---

## 8. Price review

Prices are reviewed once each year with effect from 1 February. The Supplier
must give the Customer written notice of the reviewed prices not less than
thirty days before they take effect. No line item may increase at a review by
more than the increase in CPI for the twelve months to the September quarter
immediately preceding the review, plus two percentage points.

Between reviews the Supplier may pass on a documented increase in the cost of
polythene resin or of imported hanger wire on thirty days' written notice,
limited to the lines affected and supported by the mill or supplier notice
relied on. The Customer may reject an increase notified under this paragraph by
giving notice within fourteen days, in which case the affected lines continue to
be supplied at the old price until the Supplier's current stock holding is
exhausted and are then withdrawn from the Price List.

The wire hanger lines were last increased at the review effective 1 February
2026, from $40.50 to $42.00 for the 16" line. The polythene lines were held at
the 1 February 2025 prices at that review.

---

## 9. Returns and credits

### 9.1 General returns

Unopened stock in saleable condition may be returned within thirty days of
delivery for full credit where the return is the result of a Supplier error, and
within ninety days for credit less a restocking charge of 15% where the Customer
has over-ordered. Returns must be booked with the Supplier in advance and are
collected on the next scheduled delivery run. Stock returned dirty, water
marked, crushed or without its original packaging is not credited.

### 9.2 Printed and made-to-order items

Branded Stock, printed laundry bags and press covers cut to a machine's pattern
are made to order and are **not returnable**, except for a manufacturing fault
or a printing error against the artwork approved under clause 10.2. A claim for
a printing error must be made within fourteen days of delivery and must identify
the roll or carton number printed on the packaging.

### 9.3 Faulty goods

Faulty goods are credited or replaced at the Customer's election. The Supplier
may require the return of a sample and, for wire hanger faults, the batch label
from the affected box. A claim for a latent fault in press pads or covers must
be made within ninety days of delivery.

---

## 10. Branded stock

### 10.1 Printed lines

The Supplier prints "Main Street Dry Cleaners — Bendigo's since 1987" together
with the Customer's telephone number and web address on the 21" and 40"
polythene and on the 60" gown bag. Printing is one colour, single side, repeated
at 900 mm intervals along the roll. The artwork specification is at Annexure D.

### 10.2 Minimum print run, artwork and lead time

The minimum print run for any branded line is 5,000 metres of polythene or 5,000
gown bags. The lead time is six weeks from written artwork approval. The
Customer must approve a printed proof in writing before the run is scheduled,
and the Supplier is not liable for an error that was present in the approved
proof.

Where a run is scheduled and the Customer cancels after the plate has been
mounted, the Customer must pay the mounting charge of $180.00.

### 10.3 Print charges and plate ownership

A one-off plate charge of $680.00 applies to each new artwork. Printed polythene
and printed gown bags are supplied at the premiums set out in clauses 4.3 and
4.4.

Title to the print plate passes to the Customer twelve months after the plate
charge is paid, after which the Supplier holds the plate as bailee for the
Customer and must release it to the Customer or to a nominated printer on
request. The plate charge for the Customer's current artwork was paid on
14 March 2025 and title passed on 14 March 2026.

### 10.4 Change of artwork

A change of artwork requires a new plate and a new plate charge. The Supplier
will run out existing printed stock before introducing new artwork unless the
Customer directs otherwise in writing and accepts the cost of the stock on hand.

---

## 11. Consignment stock

### 11.1 Lines held

The Supplier holds the following lines at the Plant on consignment: wire hangers
in the 14", 16" and 18" lengths, heavy shirt hangers in the 16" length, and the
21" and 40" polythene. Title to Consignment Stock remains with the Supplier
until it is counted as drawn down.

Risk in Consignment Stock passes to the Customer on delivery. The Customer must
store it under cover, clear of the floor, away from the solvent store and away
from any source of heat, and must not move it to another site.

### 11.2 Counting

Consignment Stock is counted on the first Wednesday of each month by the
Supplier's driver together with a member of the Customer's staff, and the count
sheet is signed by both. Stock drawn down since the previous count is invoiced
on the count date on the ordinary payment terms.

A discrepancy of more than 2% between the count and the expected draw-down is
investigated jointly before the invoice issues. A discrepancy that cannot be
reconciled is invoiced to the Customer.

### 11.3 Limits and removal

The consigned holding must not exceed six weeks of average usage measured over
the preceding three months. The Supplier may reduce the holding on notice, and
may remove Consignment Stock on seven days' notice if the account is suspended
under clause 12 or if this Agreement is terminated.

---

## 12. Payment

### 12.1 Terms

Payment is due thirty days from the end of the month in which the invoice is
dated, by electronic funds transfer to the account nominated on the invoice.
Prices exclude GST, which is payable in addition and is shown separately on each
tax invoice.

### 12.2 Interest and suspension

Interest accrues on any amount not paid by its due date at 1.0% per month,
calculated daily from the due date until payment. If any amount is more than
forty-five days overdue the Supplier may suspend supply, including the Standing
Order, on written notice until the account is brought current.

### 12.3 Credit limit

The account operates to a credit limit of $6,000. The Supplier may decline to
supply on credit above that limit and may require payment in advance for an
order that would take the account past it.

---

## 13. Warranty, liability and termination

### 13.1 Warranty

The Supplier warrants that the goods will correspond with their description,
will be of acceptable quality, and will be free from defects in materials and
workmanship. Nothing in this Agreement excludes, restricts or modifies a
guarantee, right or remedy conferred by the Australian Consumer Law that cannot
lawfully be excluded.

### 13.2 Liability

Where the Supplier's liability may lawfully be limited, it is limited at the
Supplier's option to replacing the goods, supplying equivalent goods or paying
the cost of replacement. The Supplier's aggregate liability under or in
connection with this Agreement in any twelve month period is limited to the
total amount paid by the Customer to the Supplier in that period.

Neither party is liable to the other for loss of profit, loss of revenue, loss
of goodwill or any indirect or consequential loss. The Supplier is not liable
for damage to a garment arising from the Customer's choice of cover, bag or
hanger for a particular fabric or finish.

### 13.3 Termination

Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving the other not less than
ninety days' written notice. Either party may terminate immediately by written
notice if the other commits a material breach and fails to remedy it within
fourteen days of written notice requiring it to do so, or becomes insolvent, has
a controller or administrator appointed, or resolves to wind up.

### 13.4 Effect of termination

On termination all amounts owing become immediately due and payable. The
Supplier may collect all Consignment Stock not yet drawn down within fourteen
days of the effective date. The Customer must pay for Branded Stock already
produced, and for Branded Stock in production against an approved artwork, up to
the minimum run quantity. Any print plate to which title has passed to the
Customer is released to the Customer at the Customer's cost.

---

## 14. Notices and general

### 14.1 Notices

Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, sent by prepaid post or sent
by email to the addresses below, and are taken to be received on delivery, on
the third Business Day after posting, or on the sending of the email provided no
delivery failure notification is received.

**To the Supplier:** The Sales Manager, Trentham Packaging & Supply Pty Ltd,
22 Enterprise Way, Bendigo East VIC 3550; accounts@trenthamsupply.com.au

**To the Customer:** The Director, Aveline Holdings Pty Ltd, Shop 4,
118 Hargreaves Street, Bendigo VIC 3550; hello@mainstreetdrycleaners.com.au

### 14.2 General

Neither party may assign this Agreement without the written consent of the
other, which must not be unreasonably withheld. A variation must be in writing
and signed by both parties, except a variation of the Price List made under
clause 8 or of the Standing Order made under clause 3.1. This Agreement records
the entire agreement between the parties about its subject matter. It is
governed by the law of Victoria and the parties submit to the non-exclusive
jurisdiction of the courts of Victoria.
